Using While as Although to express concession and contrast
While + subject + verb + other information, subject + verb + other information
While natural foods are nutritious, they are often too expensive.
雖然天然食品營養豐富，但價格往往太高。
在這個句型中，while 與 although 意思相同，用來先承認一項事實，再提出另一項與它形成對比或出乎意料的事實。
It connects two opposing ideas naturally. You do not need to split the information into several short sentences, so the expression becomes smoother.
把兩個相反的想法自然連接起來。不需要把資料拆成幾個短句，表達會更流暢。
It makes speaking and writing sound more balanced. You can first acknowledge the other side before presenting your main point, so your view does not sound overly one-sided.
讓說話和寫作顯得更平衡。你可以先承認另一面的事實，再表達主要觀點，不會令人覺得你的看法過於片面。
It is suitable for essays, discussions and spoken answers. The structure can compare advantages and disadvantages, ideals and reality, and different people’s views.
適合用於作文、討論和口語回答。這個句型可以用來比較優點與缺點、理想與現實，以及不同人的看法。
It reduces repeated use of but and although. Learning while gives you more sentence variety and makes your English sound more natural and mature.
減少重複使用 but 和 although。學會使用 while，可以令句式更多變，英文聽起來更自然和成熟。
In this lesson, While means “although”, not “during the time that”.
While 在本課表示「雖然」，不是「當……的時候」。
Add a comma after a While clause when it comes at the beginning of a sentence.
放在句首的 While clause 後面要加逗號。
Both sides of the comma must be complete clauses, normally each containing a subject and a verb.
逗號前後都必須是完整的子句，通常各自包含主語和動詞。
Do not add but before the main clause after using While.
使用 While 後，主句前不需要再加 but。

Incorrect: While natural foods are nutritious, but they are often expensive.
Pronouns must agree in number with the nouns they refer to.
代名詞必須與所指的名詞保持單複數一致。

Using few and little to express scarcity
Few + plural countable noun + plural verb + other information
Few with a plural countable noun
Little + uncountable noun + singular verb + other information
Subject + verb + few + plural countable noun
Few people paid attention to children with special educational needs.
很少人留意有特殊教育需要的孩子。

This structure lets you use one short word to state clearly that something exists in a very small or possibly insufficient quantity.
這個句型可以讓你只用一個簡短的詞，便清楚表達某種東西「數量很少」或「少得不足」。
It can replace repeated use of not many and not much, making sentences shorter and more natural.
它能代替經常重複的 not many 和 not much，令句子更簡潔、更自然。
It also helps you distinguish countable and uncountable nouns, such as few students but little time.
它亦能幫助你分辨可數名詞和不可數名詞，例如 few students，但要說 little time。
It is especially useful in essays, reports and discussions of social issues because it can clearly identify shortages of resources, support, time or participation.
在作文、報告和討論社會問題時，這個句型特別實用，因為它能清楚指出資源、支援、時間或參與人數不足。
Use few before plural countable nouns.
Few 放在複數可數名詞前。
Little 放在不可數名詞前。
Few and little normally carry a more negative meaning, indicating that the quantity may be insufficient.
Few 和 little 通常帶有較負面的意思，表示數量少得可能不足。
Few people helped.（幫忙的人很少，可能不夠。）
Little money remained.（剩下的錢很少，可能不夠用。）
Few / little and a few / a little have different meanings. Few / little means very few, very little or almost none; a few / a little means some.
Few / little 與 a few / a little 的意思不同。few / little 表示「很少、幾乎沒有」；a few / a little 表示「有一些」。
Answers in this exercise use only few or little. Do not add a.
本練習的答案只使用 few 或 little，不要自行加入 a。

Using so + must to connect a situation with a necessary action
Reason or situation + , so + subject + must + base verb + other information
Public funds are limited, so the government must spend the taxpayers’ money more wisely.
公共資金有限，所以政府必須更明智地使用納稅人的金錢。
It makes the reason and action clear. The structure states the situation first and then the action that must be taken, so readers can understand the relationship immediately.
清楚交代原因和行動。這個句型先說明情況，再說明必須採取的行動。讀者可以立即明白兩者之間的關係。
It combines two ideas in one sentence, so you do not need to separate the reason and necessary action into two short sentences.
把兩個相關意思合併成一句。你不需要把原因和必要行動分成兩個短句。
It shows that something is necessary, not merely advisable. Must clearly marks actions connected with safety, rules, deadlines or important responsibilities.
表明事情是必要，而不只是建議。當某個行動與安全、規則、限期或重要責任有關時，must 可以清楚顯示這不是普通建議。
It helps you explain practical solutions. In essays, reports, discussions or presentations, you can identify a problem and then propose the action that must be taken.
幫助你提出實際解決方法。在作文、報告、討論或簡報中，你可以先指出問題，再提出必須採取的措施。
It gives you a useful speaking frame. When you need to explain quickly that a situation makes an action necessary, use: ________, so ________ must ________.
提供容易使用的說話框架。當你需要迅速解釋「因為有這個情況，所以必須這樣做」時，可以直接使用：________, so ________ must ________。
The first clause states the reason or situation, such as a problem, limit, danger, rule or need.
前半句說明原因或情況，交代一個問題、限制、危險、規則或需要。
The second clause states the necessary action. Use so + subject + must + base verb to explain what must be done in that situation.
後半句說明必要行動。使用 so + 主語 + must + 原形動詞，說明在這個情況下必須採取甚麼行動。
The road is wet, so drivers must slow down.
道路濕滑，所以駕駛者必須減速。
Use the base form of the verb after must.
must 後面使用原形動詞。
Must expresses strong necessity and is stronger than should. Use it only when something is necessary, important, compulsory or cannot be ignored.
must 表示強烈的必要性，比 should 更強。只有當事情屬於必要、重要、強制或不能忽略時，才使用 must。
Must not + base verb expresses prohibition and does not mean do not have to.
must not + 原形動詞 表示某件事不可以做。must not 並不等於 do not have to。
Workers must not switch on the machine.
do not have to = 不一定需要做
A comma is normally required between the two complete clauses.
兩個完整句子之間通常要加逗號。
The library is closing soon, so we must choose our books quickly.
圖書館快要關門，所以我們必須盡快選好書籍。

Using whose to express ownership or a close connection
Person / animal / place / organisation / thing + whose + noun + verb + other information
I went to a restaurant whose decoration was superb.
我去過一間餐廳，它的裝潢非常出色。

I met a girl whose brother is in my class.
我遇到一個女孩，她的哥哥在我班上。
whose 後面的名詞屬於或與 whose 前面的人或事物有密切關係。
It clearly shows ownership or connection. This structure makes it clear which person or thing a detail is connected with.
這個句型能清楚顯示某件事物屬於誰，或某項資料與哪一個人或事物有關。
It joins two related sentences. Instead of writing two separate sentences, you can combine the information into one complete sentence.
你可以把兩個有關連的句子合併成一句，不需要把資料分開表達。
It avoids repeating the same noun. You do not need to repeat words such as the girl, the student, the company or the building.
它能避免重複使用「那個女孩」、「那名學生」、「那間公司」或「那幢建築物」等名詞。
It helps identify the exact person or thing. You can add an important detail to show exactly which person, place or object you mean.
你可以加入一項重要資料，讓讀者清楚知道你所指的是哪一個人、地方或物件。
It makes descriptions smoother and more detailed. This structure is useful when describing people, families, animals, places, organisations and objects in conversations, stories, essays and reports.
這個句型適合在對話、故事、作文和報告中描述人物、家庭、動物、地方、機構和物件，令內容更流暢和具體。
Use whose + noun. Do not add his, her, its or their after whose.
whose 後面直接加名詞，不可以再加入 his、her、its 或 their。
Correct: a girl whose brother is in my class
Incorrect: a girl whose her brother is in my class
The verb agrees with the noun after whose.
動詞的單複數由 whose 後面的名詞決定。
Whose can describe people and things.
whose 不但可以描述人，也可以描述動物、地方、機構和物件。
a student whose answer was correct
a hotel whose rooms were clean
Do not confuse whose with who’s. Whose means of whom / of which; who’s means who is or who has.
不要混淆 whose 與 who’s。whose 表示「誰的／它的」，沒有撇號；who’s 表示 who is 或 who has，有撇號。
Use commas for additional information about a known person or thing.
當 whose 子句只是補充一個已知人物或事物的額外資料時，子句前後通常需要使用逗號。
Chloe, whose father teaches music, can play three instruments.

me, not I; him, not he; her, not she; us, not we; them, not they
When an action follows instead of, use the -ing form because instead of is a prepositional phrase.
Instead of 後面接行動時，動詞要加 -ing。Instead of 是介詞，因此後面的動詞通常要變成 verb-ing。
Correct: I walked instead of taking the bus.
Incorrect: I walked instead of take the bus.
The two options before and after instead of should correspond: noun with noun, action with action, or manner with manner.
前後兩個選項應該互相對應：名詞對名詞、行動對行動、方式對方式。

Instead of may appear at the beginning of a sentence; normally add a comma after the introductory phrase.
Instead of 可以放在句子前面。當 Instead of 片語放在句首時，後面一般要加逗號。

Instead of is followed by a noun, object pronoun or verb-ing and directly compares two choices in the same sentence.
Instead of 是介詞片語，接名詞、受詞代名詞或 verb-ing，通常在同一句中直接比較兩個選項。

Instead is a sentence adverb that connects two complete ideas. It normally begins a new sentence and is followed by a comma; it cannot be followed directly by a noun or verb-ing.
Instead 是句子副詞，連接兩個完整意思。它通常放在新句子的開頭，後面加逗號，不可以直接接名詞或 verb-ing。
I did not take a taxi. Instead, I walked home.
Rather is a sentence adverb that corrects or restates an earlier idea more accurately, often meaning “more precisely” or “rather X than Y”.
Rather 是句子副詞，通常用來修正或更準確地表達前面的意思，可表示「更準確地說」、「更恰當地說」或「與其說是 X，不如說是 Y」。

Using Instead to show a replacement choice or action
Subject + negative action or rejected choice. Instead, + subject + replacement action.
Life should not be about others. Instead, it is about how we choose to live our lives.
人生不應該只關於別人；相反，它應該關乎我們如何選擇過自己的生活。
Instead, it is about how we choose to live our lives.
It clearly shows that you did not do A and chose to do B instead, so readers can immediately identify the rejected choice and the action actually taken.
清楚表示「沒有做 A，改為做 B」，讓讀者立即知道哪一個選擇被放棄，以及實際採取了甚麼行動。
It makes the relationship between two choices easier to understand.
讓兩個選擇之間的關係更容易理解。
It is useful for explaining a change of plan or decision in conversation, work emails, reports and compositions.
適合解釋改變計劃或決定，在日常對話、工作電郵、報告和作文中都非常實用。
It avoids repeatedly using but and gives your sentence structure more variety.
避免反覆使用 but，令句式更有變化。
It helps organise spoken answers: first state the choice not taken, then clearly present the actual decision.
幫助口語表達更加有組織：先說明沒有採取的選擇，再清楚提出真正的決定。
Instead must be followed by a complete sentence. The part after Instead needs a subject and a verb, although the subject may be omitted in an imperative.
Instead 後面要接一個完整句子。Instead 後面的部分必須有完整的主語和動詞，祈使句則可以省略主語。
I did not take the bus. Instead, I walked.
Incorrect: I did not take the bus. Instead, walking.
When Instead begins the second sentence, capitalise it and place a comma after it.
Instead 放在第二句開首時，首字母要大寫，後面要加逗號。
Do not join two complete sentences with only a comma. This exercise consistently uses a full stop followed by Instead, although advanced writing may use a semicolon.
不要只用逗號連接兩個完整句子。本練習統一使用完整句號 + Instead,；較進階的寫作也可以使用分號。
Incorrect: I did not call him, instead, I sent a message.
I did not call him. Instead, I sent a message.
I did not call him; instead, I sent a message.
Instead emphasises that the second choice replaces the first: the original action did not happen or a choice was rejected, and another action or choice took its place.
Instead 強調「第二個選擇取代第一個選擇」：原本的行動沒有發生，或某個選擇被放棄，而第二個行動或選擇取代了第一個。
Instead, introduces a complete replacement action. Instead of is followed by a noun, pronoun or verb-ing. Rather, generally corrects, clarifies or states an idea more accurately.

較強或較令人意外的重點
Subject + even + main verb + other information
After an auxiliary, modal or be
放在助動詞、情態動詞或 be 之後

Even + focused subject + verb + other information
Subject + auxiliary / modal / be + not + even + focused information
Having five children was normal and even necessary in the past.
在過去，生五個孩子是正常的，甚至是必要的。
Use even to highlight a person, thing, action, quality or result that is more surprising, less expected or goes further than the other information.
使用 even 強調較令人意外、較出乎預期，或比前一點更進一步的人、事、動作、特質或結果。
It shows exactly what is surprising. Even draws the reader’s attention to the least expected part of the sentence.
它能清楚指出哪一點最令人意外。even 會把讀者的注意力帶到句子中最出乎意料的部分。
It helps you build a stronger message. You can begin with an ordinary point and then add a stronger or more impressive point.
它能幫助你逐步加強意思。你可以先提出一般情況，再加入一個更強烈或更令人印象深刻的重點。
It joins related ideas more smoothly. Instead of repeatedly writing “more surprisingly” or using two separate sentences, you can connect the ideas with and even.
它能更流暢地連接相關意思。你不需要反覆使用「更令人意外的是」，也不需要把內容拆成兩句；使用 and even 便可把意思自然地連起來。
It makes examples and lists more powerful. Placing even before the most unexpected example makes the final item stand out.
它能令例子和列舉更有重點。把 even 放在最令人意外的例子前，可以令最後一項更加突出。
It expresses a surprising negative clearly. Not even shows that someone failed to do the easiest, smallest or most basic thing.
它能清楚表達令人意外的否定情況。not even 可以表示某人連最容易、最少或最基本的事情也沒有做到。
Place even before the word, phrase or meaning you want to emphasise.
even 要放在你想強調的字、詞組或意思之前。

Use and even when the second point goes further or is more surprising than the first.
當第二點比第一點更進一步或更令人意外時，可以使用 and even。

Even normally appears before a main verb, but after be, a modal verb or an auxiliary verb.

Not even means that someone did not do the easiest, smallest or most basic thing.

Even does not simply mean very: very increases degree, whereas even marks a point as more surprising.
even 並不只是表示 very；very 主要加強程度，even 則帶出「這一點更令人意外」的意思。

Using Not even to strengthen a negative statement
Subject + do / does / did + not even + base verb + other information
Subject + modal verb + not even + base verb + other information
Subject + be + not even + adjective / noun phrase / other information
Subject + have / has / had + not even + past participle + other information
Most surprising person or thing first
把最令人意外的人或事物放在句首
Not even + noun phrase + verb + other information
In the past, when TV was not even popular, people enjoyed their lives by socialising with one another.
在過去，當電視甚至還未普及的時候，人們透過互相交往來享受生活。
She did not even read the first page.
她連第一頁也沒有閱讀。
The water was not even warm.
They have not even started the meeting.
他們甚至還未開始會議。
Not even the teacher knew the answer.

Not even strengthens a negative statement by showing that something very basic, easy, likely or minimally expected did not happen or is not true. It often conveys surprise, disappointment, criticism or emphasis.
Not even 用來加強否定語氣，表示一件非常基本、非常容易、最有可能或最低限度應該發生的事情，也沒有發生或並不成立。它通常帶有驚訝、失望、批評或強調的語氣。
It makes the strength of the negative meaning clear by showing that the missing event or item was very basic, easy or expected.
讓否定語氣更加清楚：不只是表示某件事沒有發生，還能讓讀者知道，沒有發生的事情其實非常基本、容易或值得期待。
It highlights the lowest or simplest expectation and can show that someone failed to complete even the easiest step.
突出最低或最基本的要求，指出某人連最簡單的一步也沒有完成。
It makes descriptions and opinions more vivid by naturally conveying surprise, disappointment or criticism.
令描述和意見更有畫面，自然表達驚訝、失望或批評。
It can replace a longer explanation of how something failed to perform its most basic task.
可以縮短較長的解釋，不必使用「連最基本的事情也無法做到」等較長說法。
It provides useful speaking and writing frames such as “I did not even...”, “She could not even...”, “They have not even...”, “It was not even...” and “Not even the...”.
提供實用的說話及寫作框架，例如「I did not even...」、「She could not even...」、「They have not even...」、「It was not even...」及「Not even the...」。
Place not even before the part you want to emphasise.
Not even 要放在想強調的部分之前。
She did not even call me.
The room was not even clean.
After do, does or did, use the base form of the verb.
使用 do、does 或 did 時，後面的動詞須使用原形。
Correct: He did not even read the message.
Incorrect: He did not even readed the message.
With a modal verb or perfect tense, place not even after the first auxiliary verb.
情態動詞或完成時態中，not even 放在第一個助動詞之後。
The work had not even begun.
When Not even + person or thing is the subject, do not use inversion. This lesson does not cover advanced inversion such as “Not even once did he apologise.”
Not even + 人或事物作主語時，不需要倒裝。本練習不包括「Not even once did he apologise.」等較高階的倒裝句。
Correct: Not even the manager understood the problem.
Incorrect: Not even the manager did understand the problem.
Do not turn every ordinary negative sentence into not even. Use it only when the missing or untrue point is surprisingly basic or expected.
不要把每一個普通否定句都改成 not even。只有當句子帶有「這一點也沒有，實在令人意外」的意思時，才適合使用 not even。
He does not even like coffee, although he works in a café.
Not even strengthens a negative meaning. Even though means “although”, even if introduces a hypothetical condition, and not only adds another piece of information.
not even 加強否定，表示「連……也不」；even though 表示「儘管」；even if 表示「即使」，提出一個假設條件；not only 表示「不但」，用來加入另一項資料。
Even though he was tired, he continued working.
Even if it rains, we will go.
She is not only patient but also helpful.
Rewrite each sentence using not even to emphasise the surprising or minimum negative fact.
Keep the important meaning and tense of the original sentence.
The first word of each answer has been provided.

每題已提供答案的第一個字。

Using Even if to express an unchanged result under a possible condition
Even if + condition clause, + main clause
基本公式：條件子句在前
基本公式：條件子句在後
Main clause + even if + condition clause
Even if + subject + present simple, subject + will / can / may / must / should + base verb.
Even if + subject + past simple, subject + would / could + base verb.
Even if it rains, the event will continue.
即使下雨，活動仍會繼續。
Even if introduces a possible or imagined condition. The main action or result will remain the same if that condition happens.
Even if 用來提出一個可能或假設的情況。即使該情況真的發生，主要行動或結果仍然不會改變。
It shows that a result will not change. This structure clearly tells the listener that a difficulty will not stop the main action.
這個句型能清楚表示，即使出現困難，主要行動或結果仍然不會改變。
It combines a possible problem and a response. You can connect the possible difficulty and the decision in one sentence instead of using two separate sentences.
把「可能出現的問題」和「仍會採取的行動」連成一句，不需要分開表達。
It makes plans, promises and advice clearer. You can use even if to show determination, give firm advice or explain what should happen in a difficult situation.
使計劃、承諾和建議更清楚；可以用 even if 表達決心、作出承諾，或說明面對困難時仍應怎樣做。
It helps you answer possible objections. In discussions and essays, you can mention a possible problem and show why your main point still stands.
幫助回應可能的反對意見；在討論和作文中，可以先承認一個可能出現的問題，再說明自己的主要觀點為何仍然成立。
It gives you another way to connect ideas and helps you avoid repeatedly using may…but… or perhaps…but….

Using Provided that / Providing that to express a necessary condition
Main clause + provided that / providing that + condition clause
Provided that / Providing that + condition clause, + main clause
I was allowed to leave work early provided that I had worked an extra shift beforehand.
只要我事前多做一更，我便獲准提早下班。
provided that I had worked an extra shift beforehand
This structure means that something may happen, will happen or will be permitted only when a necessary condition is satisfied.
這個句型表示：只有在某個必要條件獲得滿足時，某件事才可以發生、才會發生或才會獲准進行。
It makes a necessary condition clear, so readers immediately know that something is not unconditional and a stated requirement must be met first.
清楚說明必要條件，讓讀者立即知道某件事並非無條件發生，而是必須先符合指定要求。
It is useful for permission and rules because it explains what someone may do and what requirement they must follow.
適合表達許可和規則，說明一個人可以做甚麼，以及必須遵守甚麼要求。
It helps you make clear offers and agreements by placing what you are willing to do and what the other person must do in one sentence.
幫助提出清楚的提議和協議，把你願意做的事情和對方必須做到的事情放在同一句內。
It combines two related ideas by joining what may happen with the condition that must be satisfied.
把兩個相關意思連成一句，把「可以做甚麼」和「需要符合甚麼條件」清楚連接。
It gives you an alternative to if, adds sentence variety and particularly emphasises that something is possible only if the condition is met.
避免反覆使用 if，增加句式變化，並特別強調「只有符合條件才可以」。
It is useful in formal communication such as work arrangements, applications and approvals, business agreements, school rules, refund terms and service requirements.
適合較正式的溝通，例如工作安排、申請和批准、商業協議、學校規則、退款條款及服務要求。

Provided that and Providing that have the same meaning: only if, on condition that, or as long as. Provided that is especially common in rules, agreements and formal writing; Providing that is also natural in British English and may sound slightly more conversational.
Provided that 和 Providing that 意思相同，均表示 only if、on condition that、as long as、「只要」、「條件是」或「前提是」。Provided that 在規則、協議及正式書面語中尤其常見；Providing that 在英式英語中亦十分自然，有時語氣稍為口語化。
The condition must be satisfied. Provided that / Providing that does not merely introduce an ordinary possibility; it emphasises a necessary condition.
這個條件必須得到滿足。Provided that / Providing that 不只是提出一個普通可能性，而是強調某件事發生的必要條件。
You can use the room if you clean it afterwards.
You can use the room provided that you clean it afterwards.
The condition may follow the main clause. When the main clause comes first, a comma is not normally needed before provided that / providing that.
條件可以放在主句後面。主句在前時，通常不需要在 provided that / providing that 前加逗號。

The condition may come first. When it begins the sentence, place a comma after the condition clause.

A future condition normally uses the present tense rather than will after provided that / providing that.
未來條件通常不用 will；當主句談及未來時，provided that / providing that 後通常使用現在式。
Correct: We will have a picnic provided that the weather stays dry.
Not normally used in this lesson: We will have a picnic provided that the weather will stay dry.
The structure may express a negative condition. Place not in the verb phrase of the condition clause.
可以表達否定條件；否定詞 not 放在條件子句的動詞部分。
You may use the computer provided that you do not download any games.
Retain the complete forms provided that and providing that in this lesson, even though provided and providing may sometimes be used alone as conjunctions.
本課保留完整的 that。Provided 和 providing 有時可以單獨用作連接詞，但本課統一練習 provided that 及 providing that。

Provided that / Providing that introduces a necessary condition that has not yet been satisfied. Given that introduces a fact treated as known or established and uses it to explain a decision or result.
Provided that / Providing that 表示一項尚待滿足的必要條件；Given that 表示一項說話者視為已知或已成立的事實，並以該事實解釋之後的決定或結果。兩個句型一般不能互相替換。

Given that we do not have a large enough budget, we have no choice but to choose the simpler plan.

A WH non-specific clause, also called a WH noun clause or embedded WH-clause, uses what, who, where, when, why, how, which or whose to introduce information that is not directly specified. The whole clause functions as one piece of information in the larger sentence.
WH 非指定句亦可稱為 WH 名詞子句（WH noun clause / embedded WH-clause）。它使用 what、who、where、when、why、how、which 或 whose，引入一段未直接指定的內容，並讓整個 WH 非指定句在大句子中充當一項資料。
It puts an unknown detail inside a complete sentence.
可以把未知的人、事物、地方、時間、原因或方法，直接放進一個完整句子中。
It reports a question without asking it directly, which is useful in explanations, reports, discussions and polite enquiries.
可以轉述一條問題，而不是直接向對方發問；這在解釋、報告、討論和禮貌查詢時都很實用。
It joins two short ideas into one smoother sentence.
能把「一條問題」和「知道、解釋、發現、決定」等意思合併，避免句子過短和零碎。
It avoids repeating vague phrases such as the thing, the person, the place, the reason or the way.
避免重複 the thing、the person、the place、the reason 或 the way；使用 what、who、where、why 或 how，句子會更直接。
It helps you explain ideas and evidence clearly in compositions, reports, presentations and spoken answers.
在作文、報告、簡報和口語回答中，能幫助清楚說明「真正發生甚麼」、「原因是甚麼」或「事情如何運作」。
Use statement word order in a WH non-specific clause.
WH 非指定句使用陳述句語序。
Direct question: Where does Maya work?
WH clause: I know where Maya works.
Incorrect: I know where does Maya work.
Do not retain do, does or did inside a WH non-specific clause.
不要在 WH 非指定句中保留 do、does 或 did。
Direct question: Why did he leave?
WH clause: We know why he left.
When the WH-word is itself the subject, place the verb directly after it; do not add he, she or it.
當 WH-word 本身是主語時，後面直接接動詞；不要另外加入 he、she 或 it。
What caused the delay is still unclear.
The punctuation is determined by the whole sentence. A statement ends with a full stop, while a complete question ends with a question mark.
問號由整個句子決定。陳述句使用句號；整體是一條問題時使用問號。
Do you know where he lives?

Choose the correct WH-word: what for a thing or content; who for a person; where for a place; when for a time; why for a reason; how for a method, degree or situation; which for choosing from known options; and whose for possession.
選擇正確的 WH-word：what 表示事物或內容；who 表示人；where 表示地點；when 表示時間；why 表示原因；how 表示方法、程度或情況；which 表示從已知選項中選擇；whose 表示所屬關係。
What she is and who she is are different. What she is normally asks about identity type, occupation or role; who she is normally asks for the person’s actual identity or name.
what she is 和 who she is 並不相同。what she is 通常問身分、職業、角色或類型；who she is 通常問那個人的真正身分或姓名。
A WH non-specific clause is not an ordinary relative clause. A relative clause describes an already specified noun, whereas a WH non-specific clause itself represents the unspecified person or thing.
WH 非指定句不是普通關係子句。關係子句描述已指定的名詞；WH 非指定句本身已代表未指定的人或事物。
Relative clause: I found the book that Tom bought.
WH non-specific clause: I know what Tom bought.

Using in case to express a precaution
Main clause showing a precaution + in case + subject + present simple / past simple
In case + subject + present simple / past simple, + main clause showing a precaution
People often take medicine with them on trips in case they get sick.
人們旅行時常會隨身帶備藥物，以防生病。
Use in case to show that an action is taken in advance as a precaution against a possible situation.
使用 in case 表示為可能發生的情況預先採取措施。
It clearly shows that an action is a precaution. The reader understands that someone is preparing for a situation that may or may not happen.
清楚表示某人正在為一個可能發生、也可能不會發生的情況預先作準備。
It connects the preparation and the possible problem in one complete sentence.
把預防措施和可能出現的情況連接成一個完整句子。
It makes the timing clearer: the preparation happens first and the possible event may happen later.
令時間關係更清楚：預防措施先發生，而另一個情況可能在之後發生。
It is useful in many real-life situations involving travel, health, safety, technology, work and daily arrangements.
適合用於旅行、健康、安全、科技、工作及日常安排等實際情境。
It gives you another way to explain a possible risk instead of repeatedly using because something might happen.
提供另一種解釋可能風險的方法，不需要反覆使用 because something might happen。
The main action is a precaution. The action in the main clause is normally performed before the possible situation happens.
主句中的行動是預防措施，通常會在可能發生的情況之前完成，目的是預先作好準備。
Take an umbrella in case it rains.
Use a complete clause containing a subject and a verb after in case.
in case 後面要接一個包含主語和動詞的完整子句。
Correct: in case the weather changes
Correct: in case you need help
Do not normally use will after in case. For a possible future event, use the present simple.
當句子表示未來可能發生的情況時，in case 後通常使用現在式，而不是 will。
Correct: Take a jacket in case it gets cold.
Incorrect: Take a jacket in case it will get cold.
Use the past simple for a past precaution. When the precaution was taken in the past, the in case clause normally uses the past simple.
如果預防措施在過去發生，in case 子句通常使用過去式。
She brought a map in case her phone stopped working.
In case can appear at the beginning or end. When the in case clause comes first, place a comma after it.
in case 子句可以放在主句後面，也可以放在句首；如果放在句首，子句後要使用逗號。
Keep the receipt in case you need it.
In case you need the receipt, keep it in a safe place.
In case is different from if. In case shows action taken before a possible situation as a precaution; if normally means that an action happens only when a condition becomes true.
in case 與 if 不同。in case 表示在某個情況可能發生之前先採取預防措施；if 通常表示只有在條件成真後才採取相關行動。
I will take an umbrella in case it rains.
I will use the umbrella if it rains.
In case is followed by a complete clause, whereas in case of is followed by a noun phrase. This lesson focuses on in case + complete clause.
in case 後接完整子句；in case of 後接名詞片語。本練習集中訓練 in case + 完整子句。

Using That way to express the result or benefit of an action
Action / advice / method. That way, + complete clause showing the result or benefit.
Sentence 1. That way, + subject + can / will / may / could / would + base verb + other information.
You should study this part first. That way, the rest will get easier.
你應該先讀這一部分。那樣的話，其餘部分就會變得較容易。
That way, the rest will get easier.
Use That way to show what result, convenience or benefit can come from the action, advice or method mentioned immediately before it.
使用 That way 說明前一句所提出的行動、建議或做法會帶來甚麼結果、方便或好處。
It makes the action-result relationship clear by showing what action to take first and what result may follow.
清楚顯示行動與結果的關係：先說明應採取甚麼行動，再帶出可能出現的結果。
It is useful for giving advice and instructions because you can state the suggestion first and then explain its practical benefit.

Using Had better for strong advice or a warning
Subject + had better + base verb + other information
Subject + had better not + base verb + other information
You had better save a copy.
Had better gives strong or urgent advice and often implies that a problem may occur if the advice is not followed.
Had better 表示較強烈或較緊急的建議，並通常暗示如果不照做，可能會出現問題。
It shows that the advice is serious and should be considered carefully.
讓對方立即明白這項建議並不是普通意見，而是需要認真考慮的提醒。
It can warn people about a possible problem and is particularly useful for warnings, safety reminders and urgent advice.
可以警告可能出現的問題，特別適合提出警告、安全提醒和緊急建議。
It can make a warning shorter and more direct.
可以用較短和直接的方式表達強烈建議。
It helps you choose the correct strength of advice by distinguishing ordinary advice, strong advice or warning, and a rule or requirement.
幫助選擇正確的建議強度，分辨普通建議、強烈建議或警告，以及規則或必要要求。
It is useful in everyday situations such as conversations, messages, work reminders, travel arrangements, health advice and safety warnings.
適合日常對話、短訊、工作提醒、旅遊安排、健康建議和安全警告。
Use the base form of the verb after had better. Do not add to.
Had better 後面使用動詞原形，不可加入 to。
Correct: You had better leave now.
Incorrect: You had better to leave now.
The negative form is had better not + base verb, not had not better.
否定式是 had better not + 動詞原形，不是 had not better。

Using Whether (or not) / If for indirect yes/no questions
Main clause + whether + subject + verb / modal verb + other information
Main clause + if + subject + verb / modal verb + other information
I’m not sure whether personality is primarily affected by genetics or not.
我不確定性格是否主要受基因影響。
whether personality is primarily affected by genetics or not
I’m not sure if personality is primarily affected by genetics or not.
if personality is primarily affected by genetics or not
Whether 和 if 可以引入間接的是非問題，表示「是否」、「會否」或「是不是」，常用於表示不確定、不知道、想知道、詢問、檢查、確認、記得或忘記，以及關心或不在乎。
It places a direct question inside a complete sentence.
把直接問題放進完整句子，讓你在同一句中說明自己不知道、想知道或正在確認甚麼。
清楚表達不確定情況，讓讀者知道答案可能是「是」，也可能是「否」。
It connects a question with a person’s thought or action.
幫助連接「一個問題」和「某人的想法或行動」，避免使用兩個分開的短句。
It makes speaking and writing smoother through reusable sentence frames.
讓說話和寫作更流暢；掌握 I’m not sure whether...、I don’t know if... 等句框後，不需要每次從零開始組織句子。
Whether can make formal expression clearer.
Whether 可以令正式表達更清楚，適合報告、會議和正式電郵。
If provides a natural everyday alternative.
If 提供自然的日常說法，在一般對話中語氣自然直接。
Whether and if have the same meaning in many indirect yes/no questions.
Whether 和 if 在很多間接是非問題中意思相同。
I do not know whether the shop is open.
I do not know if the shop is open.
Use statement word order after whether or if: subject + verb, not verb + subject.
Whether / if 後面使用陳述句語序：Subject + verb，而不是 Verb + subject。
I wonder whether he is ready.
I wonder if he is ready.
Whether and if can be followed by modal expressions such as can, should, may, will, need to and must.
Whether / if 可以配合 can、should、may、will、need to 和 must 等情態表達。
We must decide whether we should wait.
Please check if visitors may enter.
Or not may appear at the end with either whether or if. Whether or not may also stay together, but if or not is generally not used.
Or not 可以放在句末，並與 whether 或 if 搭配。Whether or not 也可以連在一起，但一般不說 if or not。
I do not know whether he will come or not.
I do not know if he will come or not.
Whether and if are not interchangeable everywhere. Normally use whether before a to-infinitive, after a preposition, and after verbs such as discuss or consider.
Whether 和 if 並非在所有情況下都可以互換。Whether + to-infinitive、介詞 + whether，以及 discuss / consider + whether 等結構一般應使用 whether。
I cannot decide whether to stay.
It depends on whether the shop is open.
We discussed whether the plan was practical.
Do not confuse if meaning ‘whether’ with conditional if meaning ‘if’. Conditional if cannot simply be replaced by whether.
不要把表示「是否」的 if 與條件句中表示「如果」的 if 混淆；條件句的 if 不能直接改為 whether。
I do not know if he is ready.
If he is ready, we can begin.
Common frames that can introduce whether or if include be sure, know, wonder, ask, check, find out, see, remember, forget, confirm, tell someone, care, matter, investigate and test.
常與 whether 或 if 搭配的句框包括 be sure、know、wonder、ask、check、find out、see、remember、forget、confirm、tell someone、care、matter、investigate 和 test。
Can you tell me whether the library is open?
Please confirm whether the payment has arrived.
Formal structures such as decide, discuss, consider, debate, depend on, think about and the question of normally favour whether.
Decide、discuss、consider、debate、depend on、think about、the question of、whether to + verb 和 whether A or B 等搭配通常較適合使用 whether。

Whether or not + subject + verb, + main clause
Whether + subject + verb + or not, + main clause
Main clause + whether or not + subject + verb

無論 John 來不來，我都會加入這個團隊。
Whether or not John is coming
Whether or not 表示有兩種可能，但無論哪種可能成真，主句的決定、結果、規則或行動都不會改變。
It clearly shows that the result will not change.
這個句型可以清楚告訴聽者：無論出現哪種情況，主要決定、行動或規則都不會改變。
你不需要寫出兩句相似的條件句，可以把兩種可能合併成一句。
It helps you express a firm decision.

It gives you more sentence variety.
Whether 句可以放在句首或句尾，使說話和寫作不會過於重複。
The result in the main clause does not change. Whether or not presents two possibilities, but the main decision, result, rule or action remains the same.
主句的結果不會改變。Whether or not 表示有兩種可能，但無論哪種可能成真，主句的決定、結果、規則或行動都不會改變。

Or not may appear immediately after whether or after the subject and verb.
Or not 可以放在兩個位置：Whether or not he agrees... 或 Whether he agrees or not....

Whether he agrees or not, we will continue.
Use normal statement word order after whether: subject + verb, not question word order.
Whether 後面使用「主語＋動詞」，不可使用問句語序。
Whether she is ready or not, we must begin.
When the whether-clause comes first, it normally takes a comma. When it follows the main clause, a comma is normally unnecessary.
Whether 句放在句首時，後面通常要加逗號；放在主句後面時，通常不需要逗號。

Do not confuse this structure with an ordinary if-condition. If makes the result depend on a condition; whether or not shows that the condition does not affect the result.
不要與普通 if 條件句混淆。If 表示主句結果取決於條件；Whether or not 表示結果不受該條件影響。
If John comes, I will join the team.
Whether or not John comes, I will join the team.
Here, whether does not introduce an object clause meaning ‘whether’. The sentence must show that the main clause remains true in both situations.
這裏的 whether 不是表示「是否」的賓語句；本課句型必須表達「兩種情況下，主句仍然成立」。

Noun + to + base verb + other information
Subject + be + noun phrase + to + base verb
Subject + have / need / find / provide + noun + to + base verb
There + be + noun + to + base verb
Sleeping is a good way to improve efficiency.

To-infinitive 放在名詞後，說明與該名詞有關的動作、目的、用途、責任、權利、機會或可能性。
It clearly explains the relationship between a noun and an action.
清楚說明物品、地方、機會、權利或責任與甚麼動作有關。
不需要每次都使用 which、that 或 where 等較長結構，也可以把資料放在名詞後面。
It helps you use practical fixed frames.
可直接使用 a chance to、a responsibility to、the right to 和 a way to 等實用句框。
It describes objects and places more precisely.
能說明物品的用途，或人們可以在某個地方進行甚麼活動。
It avoids excessive repetition of sentence structures.
可避免反覆使用 which、where、can、should 或 must，令寫作更有變化。
Use the base form of the verb after to.
To 後面必須使用原形動詞。

Common nouns followed by a to-infinitive include way, responsibility, right, opportunity, chance, need, reason, decision, choice, plan, time, place, environment, home, school, book, topic, question, task and method.
常與 to-infinitive 連用的名詞包括 way、responsibility、right、opportunity、chance、need、reason、decision、choice、plan、time、place、environment、home、school、book、topic、question、task 和 method。
Some nouns receive the action of the following infinitive: a book to read, a topic to discuss or problems to solve.
有些名詞代表後面動作的「承受者」，例如 a book to read、a topic to discuss 或 several problems to solve。
Keep a necessary preposition at the end of the infinitive phrase.
某些句子要保留句尾介詞，不可錯誤刪去。
Not every noun takes to + verb. Nouns such as benefit, advantage, disadvantage and downside normally take of + noun or gerund in the meanings shown here.
並非所有名詞都使用 to + 動詞。Benefit、advantage、disadvantage 和 downside 等名詞表達相關意思時，通常使用 of + 名詞／動名詞。
Some nouns permit more than one structure, such as a way to solve/of solving, a chance to speak/of speaking, and a method to reduce/of reducing/for reducing.
部分名詞可以使用多於一種結構；本練習的目標是把句子改寫成 名詞 + to-infinitive。
a way to solve the problem
Do not mistake prepositional to for an infinitive marker. To followed by a noun is a preposition; to followed by a base verb forms the target to-infinitive.
不要把介詞 to 誤認為 to-infinitive。To 後面是名詞時屬於介詞；後面是原形動詞時才屬於本課目標句型。

Using somewhere, nowhere and elsewhere to describe places
Subject + verb + somewhere + adjective / place phrase / to + base verb
Subject + verb + nowhere + adjective / place phrase / to + base verb
We need somewhere quiet to talk.
我們需要一個安靜的地方交談。
There is nowhere safe to leave the bag.
沒有安全的地方可以放下這個袋。
我們決定到別處吃東西。
Somewhere 表示某處，nowhere 表示沒有任何地方，而 elsewhere 表示另一個地方或方向。
It clearly distinguishes three different place meanings.
它能清楚區分 somewhere 的「某處」、nowhere 的「沒有任何地方」和 elsewhere 的「別處」。
它可取代 a place that is quiet、no place where I can go 或 in another location 等較長說法。
It lets you describe a place naturally.
你可以直接在 somewhere 或 nowhere 後加入形容詞，簡潔地描述地方。
It works with both real places and abstract ideas.
它既可描述房間、店舖和城市，也可描述意見、估算、證據和可能的答案。
It makes speaking and writing less repetitive.
它讓你不必反覆使用 a place、another place、no place 或 in the middle。
Use somewhere when a place exists, but its exact location is unknown, unimportant or not mentioned.
當某個地方確實存在，但確實位置不明、不重要或沒有說明時，使用 somewhere。
The keys are somewhere in the room.
Nowhere already carries a negative meaning. Do not normally add another negative word such as not.
Nowhere 本身已包含否定意思，通常不需要再加入 not。
Use elsewhere when referring to another place, source, area or direction.
當你表示另一個地方、資料來源、範圍或方向時，可以使用 elsewhere。
You may find the information elsewhere.
With somewhere and nowhere, the adjective normally comes after the place word. Elsewhere normally stands alone as a place adverb.
使用 somewhere 和 nowhere 時，形容詞通常放在它們後面。Elsewhere 通常獨立作地點副詞使用。
Somewhere and nowhere can be followed by to + base verb to describe a place where an action can happen.
Somewhere 和 nowhere 可以接 to + 動詞，表示進行某項活動的地方。
Somewhere and elsewhere can also express an abstract position, degree, answer or direction.
Somewhere 和 elsewhere 也可以表示觀點、程度、答案或證據所指的抽象位置。
The truth lies somewhere between the two accounts.

Using If only to express wishes, regrets and strong hopes
If only + subject + past form + other information
A wish or regret about the present
對現在情況的願望或遺憾
If only + subject + past simple / were + other information
If only + subject + had + past participle + other information
A hoped-for change in ability or circumstances
希望能力、可能性或情況有所改變
If only + subject + could / would + base verb + other information
If only I had more time.
要是我有更多時間就好了。
If only I had left earlier.
要是我當時早一點離開就好了。
If only 用來表達強烈願望、對現況的不滿或對過去事情的遺憾，通常暗示現實與願望不同。
It clearly shows that reality differs from the speaker’s wish.
讀者一看到 if only，便知道說話者希望事情不是現在這個樣子，或後悔過去沒有採取另一個做法。
It makes wishes and regrets more emphatic.
If only 通常比普通的 I wish 更能表達強烈感受，適合用於日常對話、故事和個人寫作。
It places the regret directly in the sentence’s main focus.
你可以用 If only... 開始句子，讓讀者立即知道你最在意或最希望改變的是甚麼。
It helps distinguish a present regret from a past regret.
過去式表示現在不符合願望；had + 過去分詞則表示對已經發生的事情感到後悔。
It avoids repeatedly using I wish or It is a pity that.
這個句型可避免反覆使用 I wish 或 It is a pity that，並更直接地表達說話者的遺憾。
Use the past tense for a present situation that is contrary to fact.
表達與現在事實相反的願望時使用過去式；這個過去形式並不是指過去。
If only I had more time.
Use had + past participle to express regret about the past.
對已經發生、現在無法改變的事情感到後悔時，使用 had + 過去分詞。
If only we had booked earlier.
Use could for an ability or possibility.
Could 用來表示希望擁有某種能力或可能性。
If only I could remember her name.
Would often expresses a wish for another person, thing or situation to change. Normally avoid If only I would for an action you can control.
Would 常表示希望某人、某事或某種情況改變；一般不要使用 If only I would... 表達自己有能力控制的行動。
If only the rain would stop.
This exercise uses were for wishes contrary to present fact.
口語中有時會聽到 was，但在正式及標準英文中，假設性的願望通常使用 were；本練習統一使用 were。
If only the room were warmer.
If only expresses a wish or regret; only if introduces a necessary condition.
If only 表達願望、遺憾或「只可惜」；only if 表達必要條件，意思是「只有在……的情況下才……」。
If only I had enough money.

Used to 描述過去經常重複的行為、長時間存在的情況，或過去真實但現在已經不同的事情。
It clearly shows that something was true in the past but may now be different.
Used to 能讓讀者立即知道某件事在過去是真實的，但現在可能已經改變。
It describes a past habit more concisely than a longer phrase such as when I was young or in the past.
你不需要每次都使用 when I was young、in the past、often 或 regularly 等較長表達。
It is suitable for childhood memories, former lifestyles and personal change.
這個句型很適合用於日常對話、故事、自我介紹和口語考試，描述童年、舊生活和個人改變。
It can describe both past actions and past states.
Used to 不只可以描述以前常做的事情，也可以描述以前的性格、想法、住所或環境。
It reduces repetition and adds structural variety when describing the past.
當你需要多次描述過去時，used to 能代替反覆使用 In the past、When I was young 或 Many years ago，使句子更自然。
Use the base form of the verb after used to.
Used to 後面必須使用動詞原形。
Used to describes a repeated past action, a continuing past situation or something that was true in the past but is different now.
Used to 可描述過去經常重複的行為、長時間存在的情況，或過去真實但現在已經不同的事情。
We used to visit our grandparents every Sunday.
This building used to be a school.
Do not use used to for an event that happened only once.
不要用 used to 描述只發生一次的事情；單次完成事件應使用一般過去式。
Use use to rather than used to after did or didn’t.
由於 did 或 didn’t 已經表示過去時間，否定句和疑問句使用 use to，而不是 used to。
I didn’t use to drink coffee.
Did you use to live here?
Used to can be followed by a stative verb such as be, have, know, like, believe or live.
Used to 可以配合表示狀態的動詞，例如 be、have、know、like、believe 或 live。

Used to + base verb describes a past habit or state; be used to + noun / V-ing means being accustomed to something.
Used to + 動詞原形表示以前常做或過去的情況；be used to + 名詞／V-ing 表示已經習慣某事。
Tim used to talk to strangers.
Tim is now used to talking to strangers.

Be used to 表示某人已經習慣某件事或某項活動，現在或當時不再覺得陌生、奇怪或難以適應。
It clearly shows that something no longer feels unfamiliar.

It is useful for describing adjustment to a new school, job, culture, schedule, transport or lifestyle.

Changing the verb be lets you describe being accustomed in the present, past or future.
只要改變 be 動詞，便可以說明現在、過去或將來是否習慣某事。
It can replace a longer explanation with a more direct and natural sentence.

In be used to, to is a preposition, so it is followed by a noun, pronoun or V-ing form.
在 be used to 中，to 是介詞而不是不定詞標記，因此後面應接名詞、代名詞或 V-ing。

Change the verb be to agree with the subject and time.
Be 動詞要配合主語和時間改變：現在使用 am、is 或 are；過去使用 was 或 were；將來使用 will be。

Place not after the verb be to form a negative sentence.
否定句使用主語 + be + not + used to + 名詞／V-ing。

Place the verb be before the subject to form a question.
問句把 be 動詞放在主語之前。
Are you used to speaking in public?
Be used to + noun / V-ing means being accustomed to something; used to + base verb describes a past habit or state.
Be used to + 名詞／V-ing 表示習慣某事；used to + 動詞原形表示過去經常做某事或過去的狀態。

Tim used to talk to strangers every day.
Be used to describes the state of already being accustomed; get used to describes the process of becoming accustomed.
Be used to 表示已經習慣的狀態；get used to 表示由不習慣逐漸變成習慣的過程。

Do not confuse be used to + noun / V-ing with the passive be used to + base verb, meaning ‘be employed for a purpose’.

Using Too + adjective + to + verb to express that something is too… to do

State who cannot perform the action

句子的主語是動作的承受者

too cold for us to sleep

Too + 形容詞 + to + 動詞 表示某種程度超出可接受的範圍，令動作不能完成、不適合進行或非常困難。
清楚說明「為甚麼不能做」，讓讀者立即知道哪個情況阻止了動作。
It clearly explains why an action cannot be performed.
把「情況」和「不能進行的動作」放在同一句中，不需要寫成兩句。
It combines the condition and the impossible action in one sentence.
與 so + adjective + that + cannot 相比，這個句型通常更簡潔。
It makes an explanation shorter and more direct.
適合表達物件、食物、道路、工作、價格和個人狀態等日常限制和安全問題。
It is useful for everyday limitations and safety problems.
學會這個句型後，可以用另一種自然方法表達相同意思，增加句式變化。
It adds sentence variety instead of repeatedly using because, so, cannot or could not.
Too 並不只是表示「非常」；它表示程度超出可以接受的範圍，並因此令某個動作不能完成、不適合進行或非常困難。
Too does not merely mean very; it shows that a degree prevents or seriously limits an action.

Use the base form of the verb after to.

Use for + someone when a different person performs the action.

Too + adjective + to and adjective + enough + to express opposite meanings.

Granted, + complete clause. However, + complete clause.
Granted, the short-term cost is high. However, the long-term return is stronger.

把較長的 so…that 句縮短。She was calm enough to explain everything. 與較長的 She was so calm that she could explain everything. 意思相近，但 enough to 句更直接。
It shortens a longer so…that sentence. She was calm enough to explain everything has a similar meaning to She was so calm that she could explain everything, but the enough to version is more direct.
可以表達正面和負面判斷。正面形式表示條件已經足夠；否定形式表示條件仍未達要求，對表達實際限制、問題和建議非常有用。

It can express positive and negative judgements. The positive form shows that a condition is sufficient, while the negative form shows that the requirement has not yet been met, which is useful for describing practical limits, problems and suggestions.

Negative: The screen is not large enough for everyone to see.
幫助你更準確地描述特質和動作。可以使用 patient enough、strong enough 和 clear enough 等形容詞結構描述人物或事物，亦可以使用 carefully enough、quickly enough 和 clearly enough 等副詞結構描述動作，增加句式變化並避免每句只使用 very、can 或 because。

It helps you describe qualities and actions more precisely. Adjective patterns such as patient enough, strong enough and clear enough describe people or things, while adverb patterns such as carefully enough, quickly enough and clearly enough describe actions. This adds sentence variety and avoids relying on very, can or because in every sentence.

Enough 放在形容詞或副詞之後，例如 calm enough、tall enough、quickly enough 和 carefully enough；不要寫 enough calm、enough tall 或 enough quickly。但是，enough 放在名詞前面，例如 enough time、enough money 和 enough confidence。因此，enough confidence 和 confident enough 屬於不同結構。

Place enough after an adjective or adverb, as in calm enough, tall enough, quickly enough and carefully enough; do not write enough calm, enough tall or enough quickly. However, enough comes before a noun, as in enough time, enough money and enough confidence. Therefore, enough confidence and confident enough are different structures.
To 後面使用動詞原形。正確形式包括 strong enough to lift、clearly enough to understand 和 fast enough to catch；不要寫 strong enough to lifted、clearly enough to understanding 或 fast enough to caught。

Use the base form of the verb after to. Correct forms include strong enough to lift, clearly enough to understand and fast enough to catch; do not write strong enough to lifted, clearly enough to understanding or fast enough to caught.
形容詞和副詞的位置不同。形容詞通常放在 be 後面，描述人物或事物；副詞放在動作動詞後面，描述動作進行的方式。
Adjectives and adverbs occupy different positions. An adjective normally follows be and describes a person or thing, while an adverb follows an action verb and describes how the action is performed.
Adjective: She is patient enough to wait.
Adverb: She waited patiently enough to remain calm.
動作由另一個人完成時，使用 for + person。主句和 to 動詞由同一人完成時，不需要加入 for + person。
Use for + person when another person performs the action. When the subject of the main clause also performs the to-infinitive action, for + person is unnecessary.
Same person: Ben ran fast enough to catch the bus.
Another person: The bag was light enough for Leo to carry.
某些句子需要保留句末介詞，例如 swim in、walk on 和 record the interview in；不要隨意刪去這些介詞。
Some sentences require a final preposition, as in swim in, walk on and record the interview in. Do not remove these prepositions.
The water was warm enough to swim in.
The path was safe enough to walk on.
The room was quiet enough to record the interview in.
否定形式表示程度未達要求。
The negative form shows that the required degree has not been reached.
The coffee is not cool enough to drink.
The instructions were not clear enough to follow.
Enough to 和 too…to 的意思相反。adjective / adverb + enough to 表示程度足夠，動作可以進行；too + adjective / adverb + to 表示程度過高或過低，動作不能進行。

Enough to and too…to have opposite meanings. Adjective / adverb + enough to shows that the degree is sufficient and the action is possible, while too + adjective / adverb + to shows that the degree is excessive or insufficient and the action is not possible.
Enough: The box is light enough to carry.
Too: The box is too heavy to carry.
To + 動詞不一定表示「目的」。在 He is tall enough to reach the shelf. 中，to reach the shelf 表示身高令這項動作成為可能，而不是解釋他「為甚麼」這麼高。
To + verb does not always express purpose. In He is tall enough to reach the shelf, to reach the shelf shows that his height makes the action possible; it does not explain why he is tall.

否定疑問句以 be 動詞、助動詞或情態動詞的否定形式開始。
幫助確認你已經預期的事情。當你認為某件事很可能是真的，否定疑問句可以幫助你要求對方確認。
It helps you check what you already expect. When you believe something is probably true, a negative question lets you ask another person to confirm it.
幫助邀請對方認同。當你希望對方考慮並認同你的看法時，可以使用否定疑問句；把看法變成問題也讓對方參與討論。
It helps you invite agreement. You can use a negative question when you want the listener to consider and agree with your opinion.
Statement: It would be better to leave early.
Question: Wouldn’t it be better to leave early?
幫助表達驚訝。當實際情況與你的預期不同時，否定疑問句可以自然地表達驚訝。
It helps you express surprise. A negative question can show that the situation is different from what you expected.
幫助清楚提出疑慮。否定疑問句可以把注意力帶到一個可能被忽略的問題上，在討論、會議、辯論及意見寫作中特別實用。
It helps you raise a concern clearly. Negative questions can draw attention to a problem that people may have overlooked.
Aren’t we forgetting the main issue?
提供自然的建議方式。你不一定要直接命令別人，也可以把建議變成問題，讓對方考慮。
It gives you a natural way to make suggestions. Instead of giving a direct command, you can present an idea as a question for the listener to consider.
Shouldn’t we check the information first?
令問句不會過分重複。掌握不同的否定疑問句，可以讓你以更多方式要求確認、表達驚訝及發展論點。
It makes questions less repetitive. Learning different negative question forms gives you more ways to ask for confirmation, express surprise and develop an argument.
把否定助動詞放在主語前面。
Put the negative auxiliary before the subject.
Statement: It isn’t ready. Question: Isn’t it ready?
Statement: They don’t agree. Question: Don’t they agree?
在 don’t、doesn’t、didn’t 及情態動詞後面，主要動詞使用原形。
Use the base verb after do and modal verbs.
Incorrect: Didn’t they took the bus?
Correct: Didn’t they take the bus?
在 hasn’t、haven’t、hadn’t 後面，使用過去分詞。
Use a past participle after have.
Incorrect: Hasn’t he finish the work?
Correct: Hasn’t he finished the work?
表示某處「不是有……嗎」時，單數名詞使用 Isn’t there，複數名詞使用 Aren’t there。
Use Isn’t there or Aren’t there for existence.
否定疑問句經常顯示說話者的預期。說話者可能已經預期答案是「是」，並希望對方確認或同意。
Negative questions often show an expectation. The speaker may already expect the answer to be yes and want the listener to confirm or agree.
回答否定疑問句時，要根據事實回答，而不是只看問題中有沒有 not。
Answer a negative question according to the fact, not merely according to whether the question contains not.
Isn’t the shop open? Yes, it is. / No, it isn’t.
否定疑問句與附加問句不同。附加問句把短問句放在句尾；完整的否定疑問句把否定助動詞放在句首。兩者都可要求確認，但否定疑問句通常更直接地表達預期、驚訝、提醒或質疑。

A negative question is different from a tag question. A tag question places a short question at the end, while a complete negative question begins with the negative auxiliary. Both can request confirmation, but a negative question often expresses expectation, surprise, a reminder or a challenge more directly.
Tag question: The room is ready, isn’t it?
Negative question: Isn’t the room ready?
否定疑問句可以表示友善建議，也可以表示不滿或批評；說話時應注意語氣。
Pay attention to tone. A negative question can express a friendly suggestion, dissatisfaction or criticism.
Friendly suggestion: Wouldn’t it be better to ask for help?
Possible criticism: Haven’t you finished the work yet?

清楚表示兩個人或事物在某方面程度相同。

這個句型能幫助你避免作出過分絕對的判斷，並表明事情可能存在例外。

句首的 By 表示方法或手段；With 表示條件、資源或所處情況；From 表示資料、證據或判斷的來源。
By + -ing 能把方法和結果直接連接，清楚說明事情怎樣完成。
By + -ing directly links a method to its result and shows how something was accomplished.
With + 名詞詞組能簡潔地先交代資源、條件或情況，再提出主要意思。
With + noun phrase concisely presents an important resource, condition or situation before the main point.
From + 名詞詞組能交代結論來自哪項資料、證據或觀察，令判斷更有邏輯。
From + noun phrase identifies the data, evidence or observation behind a conclusion, making the reasoning clearer.
這些句型把方法、條件、證據和結果放在同一句中，減少零散短句及重複連接語。

Beginning with By, With or From adds sentence-opening variety instead of always starting with a person or thing.
By 後面的動詞必須使用 gerund 動名詞，即 -ing 形式。
A verb after By must take the gerund (-ing) form.

With 後面使用名詞詞組，而不是完整句子。
Use a noun phrase rather than a complete clause after With.
From 後面的內容應提供證據、線索、經驗或資料，說明判斷的來源。

Subject + be + role, position or status, and as such, + responsibility, right or expected action.

as such, you are responsible for the project’s success.
As such 可表示前述事實帶來的直接結果，也可代替前面已說明的身份、職位或性質。
As such 能清楚表示後面的內容是由前面的情況直接引起。
As such clearly shows that what follows is a direct result of the preceding situation.
它能清楚連接某人的身份和該身份帶來的責任。
It clearly connects a person’s role with the responsibility that role brings.
可以避免重複同一身份，使句子更加流暢。
It avoids repeating the same role or identity and makes the sentence smoother.
在作文、報告、電郵和簡報中，能自然連接一項情況和它的影響。
In essays, reports, emails and presentations, it naturally links a situation with its effect.
它提供 therefore、so、because of this 和 as a result 以外的另一種表達方法。
It provides an alternative to therefore, so, because of this and as a result.
當前一句描述事實或情況，而後一句是直接結果時，可以在第二句開首使用 As such,。
Use As such, at the beginning of the second sentence when it states a direct result of the preceding fact or situation.
The road is blocked. As such, drivers must use another route.
前面已說明身份、職位或角色時，as such 可代替重複該身份並帶出責任、權利或行動。
After a role, position or status has been stated, as such can replace repetition of that identity and introduce its responsibility, right or expected action.
You are the team leader, and as such, you must guide the other members.
放在新句開首時後面通常加逗號；放在句中時常寫成 and, as such, 或較簡單的 and as such,。
At the beginning of a sentence, As such is normally followed by a comma; mid-sentence it commonly appears as and, as such, or the simpler and as such,.

The building is a historic site and, as such, must be protected.
As such 表示因此或以這個身份；such as 表示例如，兩者不可混淆。
As such means therefore or in that capacity; such as means for example.

前後內容必須有直接因果或身份關係，不要用 As such 連接無關資料。

Complete clause 1, so much so that + complete result/evidence clause 2
He loved the city, so much so that he moved there.

so much so that he moved there
第一個分句表達情況、感受或行動的程度非常強烈；第二個分句帶出明顯結果或具體證據。
能有力地強調第一個情況並非一般程度，而是足以帶來明顯結果。
This structure tells the listener that the first situation was strong enough to cause a surprising or noticeable result.
不只說感受很強烈，還能加入具體行動，作為程度的清楚證明。
Instead of simply stating a strong feeling, you can add an action that proves how strong it was.
可以把情況及其結果清楚合併，不需要寫成兩句分散短句。
Instead of writing two separate sentences, you can connect the situation and its result clearly.
在說話或寫作時，可先提出概括說法，再加入明顯例子或後果，使解釋更完整。
In speaking and writing, you can first make a general statement and then add a strong example or consequence.
它提供 so + adjective + that 以外的另一種程度和結果句式，增加變化。
This structure gives you another way to express degree and result instead of repeatedly using so + adjective + that.
So much so that 回指前面的整個完整意思，不直接修飾單一形容詞或名詞。
So much so that refers back to the whole preceding clause rather than directly modifying one adjective or noun.
She trusted him, so much so that she gave him the only key.
第二個分句必須顯示第一個情況的程度有多強，成為該強烈程度的結果或證明。
The second clause should show how serious, strong or extreme the first idea was.
The road was icy, so much so that several cars could not move.
兩個意思合併成一句時，通常在 so much so that 前使用逗號。
Use a comma before so much so that when the two ideas appear in one sentence.

前面的分句本身應是完整陳述，that 後面亦必須包括主語和動詞。
Clause 1 should already contain a complete statement, and the clause after that must also contain a subject and verb.

So much so that 已表示程度很深，改寫時通常刪去 very、extremely、so、such 和 to such an extent 等重複程度字眼。
Words such as very, extremely, so, such and to such an extent are normally removed because so much so that already expresses extreme degree.
The room was quiet, so much so that we could hear the clock.
Such...that 直接修飾名詞詞組；so much so that 則先完成整個陳述，再加入結果或證明。
Such...that directly describes a noun phrase; so much so that refers back to a completed clause and adds a striking result or proof.
It was such a difficult question that nobody could answer it.
The question was difficult, so much so that nobody could answer it.
Such that 通常直接連接 structured、designed、influence 或 effect 等詞，表示安排方式或影響結果，而不是回指獨立完成分句。
Such that is normally grammatically connected to words such as structured, designed, influence or effect rather than commenting on a separate completed clause.
We structured the schedule such that everyone gets a lunch break.
So that 說明預期目的；so much so that 提出實際結果或證據，而不是目標。
So that explains an intended purpose; so much so that presents a result or evidence, not an intended goal.

I studied hard, so much so that I forgot to eat.
So + adjective/adverb + that 直接加強形容詞或副詞；so much so that 回指整個分句，再補充結果。
So + adjective/adverb + that directly intensifies an adjective or adverb; so much so that refers back to the whole clause and then adds a result.

Dad was angry, so much so that he broke his phone.

Using Not so much A as B for a more accurate emphasis
Subject + be + not so much + A + as + B
Subject + do / does / did + not so much + base verb A + as + base verb B

Not so much A as B 不一定完全否定 A，而是指出 B 更準確、更重要或更接近真正原因。
可以承認 A 有一點道理，同時指出 B 才是更準確的重點，表達更細緻。
It lets you acknowledge that A has some truth while showing that B is the more accurate emphasis.
當事情有兩個可能原因時，能清楚突出真正原因或核心問題。
When two causes are possible, it clearly highlights the real cause or central issue.

It combines A and the more important B in one sentence, creating a tighter expression.
在討論、作文或報告中，能較有禮貌地修正看法，避免武斷地說 A 完全錯誤。
In discussion, essays or reports, it corrects a view politely without bluntly claiming that A is entirely wrong.
特別適合分析真正原因、主要問題、人物感受、政策影響、行為目的和不同解釋。
It is especially useful for analysing real causes, central problems, feelings, policy effects, purposes and competing explanations.
可取代反覆使用 A matters, but B matters more，使作文和口語更成熟自然。
It replaces repetitive wording such as A matters, but B matters more and adds a more mature, natural pattern.
B 是更準確或更重要的重點；A 可能有一點道理，但 B 更接近真正原因。
B is the more accurate or important point; A may contain some truth, but B is closer to the real reason.

A 和 B 應使用相同或相近的平行文法形式，例如名詞配名詞、形容詞配形容詞。
A and B should use the same or closely parallel grammatical form, such as noun + noun or adjective + adjective.

Using once to show what happens after a stage is reached
Once you understand the pattern, it becomes easier.
一旦你明白這個規律，事情便會變得更容易。
讓事情的先後次序更清楚 這個句型能清楚說明哪一個動作先發生，以及其後會發生甚麼。
It makes the order of events clear. This structure clearly shows which action must happen first and what happens afterwards.
可以把兩個步驟合併成一句 你不需要使用「先……，然後……」寫成兩句，也可以運用 once 自然地連接兩個步驟。 第二句較緊密，而且能立即顯示兩件事的關係。

It can combine two steps in one sentence. Instead of writing two separate sentences with first and then, you can connect the steps naturally with once. The combined version is tighter and makes the relationship between the two events immediately clear.
表示完成一個階段後，另一件事才變得可行 讀者能立即明白使用機器之前必須完成甚麼。
It shows that something becomes possible after a stage is completed. The reader can immediately see what must be completed before the machine can be used.
Once the safety check is complete, the machine can be used.
適合說明指示和計劃 你可以使用 once 說明工作流程、食譜、行程、課堂指示和其他有先後次序的安排。
It is useful for instructions and plans. You can use once to explain procedures, work arrangements, recipes, travel plans, classroom instructions and other arrangements with a clear sequence.
比 if 更能表達預期和確定性 當你預期第一件事將會發生時，once 能讓你集中說明其後的安排，而不是討論事情會否發生。
It can sound more certain than if. When you expect the first event to happen, once helps you focus on what should happen next rather than questioning whether the event will happen.
Once 強調「先完成一件事，然後發生另一件事」 Once 通常帶有「到了某個階段之後」的意思。 車門打開是第一個事件；乘客進入是其後發生的事情。

Once emphasizes that one event is completed or a stage is reached before the next event occurs. It often means ‘after a certain point has been reached’: the door opening is the first event, and the passengers entering is what happens afterwards.
Once the door opens, the passengers can enter.
表達將來時，once 子句通常不使用 will 在時間子句中，即使意思涉及將來，once 後通常使用現在式或現在完成式。
For future meaning, do not normally use will in the once-clause. Even when the meaning concerns the future, use the present simple or present perfect after once.
Once you finish the report, I will check it.
Once you have finished the report, I will check it.
Once 子句放在前面時，通常使用逗號 Once 子句放在後面時，通常不需要逗號。
Use a comma after an initial once-clause; a final once-clause normally needs no comma.
Once the rain stops, we can leave.
We can leave once the rain stops.
Once 可以配合不同時態 Present 現在： Future 將來： Past 過去： Past perfect 過去完成：
Once can be used in present, future, past and past-perfect contexts.
Once I understand a topic, I remember it more easily.
Once the shop opens, we will go inside.
Once the meeting ended, everyone went home.
Once the final guest had arrived, the host began the speech.

Once 與 When 的分別 When 是較廣泛和中性的時間連接詞，可以表示： ● 某件事發生的時候； ● 兩件事同時發生； ● 每逢某件事發生； ● 將來某個時間點。 Once 則更強調第一件事已經發生、完成，或到達某個階段，然後第二件事才發生。 這裏兩件事在同一段時間發生，不適合改用 once。 這裏強調先完成閱讀，然後才還書。 在部分將來句中，when 和 once 都可以使用，但 once 更突出「第一個階段完成後」的意思。

Once emphasizes completion before a later event, unlike the broader and more neutral time linker when. When can mark the time of an event, simultaneous events, repeated occasions or a future time point. Once stresses that the first event has happened or been completed, or that a stage has been reached, before the second event occurs. It is therefore unsuitable when two events merely happen at the same time. In some future sentences either when or once is possible, but once highlights completion of the first stage.
When I was reading, the phone rang.
Once I finished reading, I returned the book.
Once 與 If 的分別 If 表示一個未必會發生的條件。 Once 通常表示說話者預期或相信這件事會發生，只是不知道確實時間。 完成報告仍帶有不確定性。 說話者預期對方會完成報告，重點是完成之後要做甚麼。 簡單來說： ● When：當……的時候，屬中性時間關係。 ● If：如果……，事情可能發生，也可能不發生。 ● Once：一旦……／……之後，通常預期第一件事會發生，並強調其後的結果。

Once normally presents an expected event, whereas if presents an uncertain condition. With if, the event may or may not happen; with once, the speaker expects it to happen but does not know exactly when, and the focus is on what follows. In short, when expresses a neutral time relationship, if presents a possible condition, and once presents an expected first event and emphasizes its subsequent result.

Distinguish this structure from related linkers: the moment or the minute emphasizes that the second event follows immediately, whereas by the time says that something has already happened or been completed before a reference point and need not be immediate. Once emphasizes that an event is complete or a condition is met before another event becomes possible, but the moment or the minute specifically stresses an almost nonexistent time gap. When identifies a time without necessarily implying an immediate second event. If introduces a condition that may or may not occur, while the moment or the minute expresses a time relationship and what follows immediately when the event occurs.

在本練習中不可省略 that 本課的目標句型是完整的 now that。 本練習不使用： 後者在某些語境可能出現，但不屬於本課要求練習的完整目標句型。 Now that 與 now 的分別 Now that 是連接詞，後面接完整子句。它連接一個新情況和由此產生的結果，意思接近「既然現 在……」。 這句有兩個互相關聯的意思： ● 約翰已經完成工作； ● 因此，他現在可以和瑪麗談話。 Now 是時間副詞，只表示「現在、此刻」。它通常修飾一個動作，並不自動表達原因或結果。 這兩句只說明事情在甚麼時間發生，沒有表示一個新情況帶來另一個結果。 簡單比較 now = 在甚麼時間？ now that = 既然出現了甚麼新情況，結果是甚麼？ 因此，不能只因為句子中出現「現在」，便使用 now that。句子必須同時包含： 1. 一個現在已經成立或改變的情況； 2. 由該情況帶來的結果、決定或行動。

Keep that in the target structure for this lesson. Although a form without that may occur in some contexts, it is not the complete target pattern practised here. Do not confuse now that with now: now that is a conjunction followed by a complete clause and links a newly established situation to its result, decision or action; now is a time adverb meaning ‘at this moment’ and does not itself express cause or result. Thus now asks when something happens, whereas now that asks what new situation has arisen and what follows from it. Use now that only when the sentence contains both a situation that is now established or changed and a resulting action, decision or outcome.
Now that the work is complete, we can go home.
Now that John has finished his work, he can talk to Mary.
I want to eat ice cream now.
John is talking to Mary now.
Now that John is free, he can talk to Mary.

It combines a fact and a comment in one sentence, allowing you to report information while adding a reaction such as regret, relief or surprise instead of writing a separate comment sentence.

It expresses tone more precisely. Different adverbs convey different degrees of certainty and emotion: clearly points to evident proof, apparently retains uncertainty, perhaps signals possibility, and thankfully conveys relief. Readers can therefore identify the speaker’s stance immediately.

Use a sentence adverb that comments on the whole statement. Common choices include attitude adverbs such as honestly, frankly and admittedly; positive or negative reactions such as fortunately, thankfully, unfortunately, regrettably and luckily; surprise or expectation markers such as surprisingly, unexpectedly and understandably; certainty markers such as clearly, obviously, apparently and perhaps; and result markers such as ultimately and eventually.

Do not confuse sentence adverbs with adverbs of manner. A sentence adverb comments on the whole statement; in the parenthetical example, honestly signals that the speaker is frankly stating an opinion. An adverb of manner describes only how an action is performed; honestly in the second example describes how the manager answered and is therefore not the parenthetical insertion practised here.

Do not confuse this agreement pattern with the correlative neither...nor structure. The target pattern links two clauses and says that the second subject shares the first subject’s situation, using neither or nor + auxiliary + subject. Correlative neither...nor joins two subjects, objects, verbs or other parallel elements into one structure meaning ‘neither one nor the other’. Thus neither...nor groups two items without agreement inversion, while neither or nor + auxiliary first states one situation, then says that another subject shares it, and requires auxiliary-subject inversion.

neither...nor... 不使用這種「助動詞＋主語」的附和倒裝結構。

「Ellipsis 省略句：and + subject + auxiliary + too _ either」
Using ellipsis with too and either to avoid repetition
First clause, and + subject + auxiliary / be verb / modal verb + too
First negative clause, and + subject + auxiliary / be verb / modal verb + not + either
I liked the first chapter, and she did too.

你不需要把相同的動作或描述重複寫兩次。 第二句更簡潔，但意思完全相同。
It avoids unnecessary repetition. You do not need to repeat the same action or description twice; the elliptical version is more concise but has exactly the same meaning.
當兩個人或事物有相同的動作、狀態或意見時，英語母語人士經常使用這個句型，因此句子會更 自然。
It makes sentences sound more natural. Native speakers frequently use this structure when two people or things share the same action, condition or opinion.
這個句型能立即讓讀者明白，第二個主語與第一個主語有相同的情況。
It connects related information clearly. The structure immediately shows that the second subject shares the same situation as the first subject.
你可以使用 and，把兩個內容重複的短句自然地連接起來。
It helps you combine short sentences. Instead of writing two repetitive sentences, you can connect them smoothly with and.
掌握正確的助動詞後，你便可以迅速作出回應，不需要重新說出整個長句。
It improves speaking fluency. Once you know which auxiliary verb to use, you can respond quickly without repeating a long sentence.
一般動詞使用 do、does 或 did 一般現在式： 一般過去式：
Use do, does or did after an ordinary lexical verb.
Tom plays tennis, and Amy does too.
Tom played tennis, and Amy did too.
be 動詞須按照第二個主語改變 不能因為第一個分句使用 am，便在第二個分句繼續使用 am。

情態動詞可以直接保留

完成式、進行式及被動句保留第一個助動詞

肯定句使用 too，否定句使用 either 肯定： 否定：

I enjoy reading, and she does too.
I do not enjoy horror films, and she does not either.

By no means, under no circumstances and never do not have exactly the same meaning. By no means strongly rejects a claim, judgement or possibility and says that the description is completely wrong. Under no circumstances states a rule, prohibition, warning or promise with no exceptions. Never says that something did not happen at any time in a period or will not happen at any future time.
By no means is the problem simple.
Under no circumstances may visitors enter this room.
Never have I visited that country.
Never will I forget your kindness.
Never 常與不同時態配合 人生經驗：Present Perfect 過去某個時間之前：Past Perfect 對未來的承諾或決心：will 習慣或一般情況：do / does

Never can be used with different tenses: the present perfect for life experience, the past perfect for a time before another past event, will for a future promise or determination, and do or does for habits or general situations.
Never have I tried this dish before.
Never had she travelled alone before that trip.
Never will we share your personal information.
Never does he complain about small problems.

Using somehow to express an unknown method, cause or unexpected success
Subject + somehow + main verb + other information
Subject + modal / auxiliary verb + somehow + base verb + other information

她不知怎樣還是設法準時完成了考試。
自然表達「不知道原因或方法」 Somehow 能讓你清楚表示自己不知道事情為何或如何發生，而不需要作出猜測。
It expresses uncertainty naturally. It helps you say that you do not know how or why something happened without making an unsupported guess.
縮短較長的說法 你可以用 somehow 取代較長的說法，例如： 第二句更簡短，意思仍然清楚。
It shortens a long explanation. Somehow can replace a longer statement such as ‘I do not know how she did it, but she finished the work’, making the sentence shorter while keeping the meaning clear.
表達「雖然困難，最後仍成功」 當某人克服困難完成一件事時，somehow 能突出結果來得不容易。
It shows success despite difficulty. When someone overcomes difficulty to complete a task, somehow emphasizes that the result was not easy to achieve.
We had very little time, but we somehow completed the project.
令故事和對話更自然 Somehow 常用於分享奇怪、意外或難以解釋的經歷，因此能令日常對話和故事更生動。

It helps avoid repetition by providing a concise, natural alternative to repeatedly saying I do not know how, I do not know why, for some unknown reason or in a way nobody could explain.

準確控制語氣的強弱 Somewhat 可以表示「有這個情況，但程度並不很強」，避免把說法說得過分絕對。 這句比 The plan is extremely risky 溫和得多。

It controls the strength of tone precisely. Somewhat says that a condition exists but is not very strong, avoiding an overly absolute claim; The plan is somewhat risky is much milder than The plan is extremely risky.
讓批評或不同意見聽起來較有禮貌 在學校、工作或正式討論中，直接說某件事「很差」可能過於尖銳。使用 somewhat 可以柔化語 氣。 這種說法既能指出問題，又不會顯得過分直接。

It makes criticism or disagreement sound more polite. At school, at work or in formal discussion, a direct negative judgement may sound too sharp; somewhat softens the tone, allowing you to identify a problem without sounding excessively blunt.
幫助表達細微的比較 Somewhat 可以配合比較級，表示兩者確實有差別，但差距不大。
It helps express subtle comparisons. With a comparative, somewhat indicates that a real difference exists but is not large.
This model is somewhat cheaper than the other one.
避免重複使用 a little 或 a bit 學生經常重複使用 a little 和 a bit。學會 somewhat 後，可以令說話和寫作更有變化。 兩句意思相近，但第二句語氣較中性，也較適合報告、作文和工作場合。

It avoids repeatedly using a little or a bit and adds variety to speech and writing. The meanings are similar, but somewhat is more neutral and better suited to reports, essays and workplace contexts.
幫助你謹慎地表達觀察和判斷 當你不想把一個判斷說得太肯定時，可以使用 somewhat。 這表示結果確實令人意外，但程度並非非常強烈。

It helps you state observations and judgements cautiously when you do not want to sound too certain. For example, somewhat surprising confirms that the result was surprising but not to a very strong degree.
Somewhat 表示有限或中等程度 Somewhat 的意思通常是： ● 有點 ● 稍微 ● 頗為 ● 在某程度上 它所表達的程度通常比 very 或 extremely 弱。 第二句的語氣較溫和，沒有第一句那麼強烈。

Somewhat expresses a limited or moderate degree, meaning a little, slightly, fairly or to some extent. It normally expresses a weaker degree than very or extremely, so the second comparison sentence sounds milder and less forceful.
Somewhat 通常放在所修飾的字前面
Place somewhat before the word it modifies.

不要把 somewhat 和 very 重疊使用
Do not combine somewhat with very.
Somewhat 與 somehow 的分別 雖然兩個字的拼法相似，但意思和功能完全不同。 Somewhat：表示程度 它回答： 「程度有多大？」 Somehow：表示不明方式、原因或設法完成某事 「怎樣做到？」或「不知為何會這樣？」 快速判斷方法 ● 表達「有點、稍微、某程度上」：使用 somewhat ● 表達「不知怎樣、不知何故、設法」：使用 somehow

Although somewhat and somehow look similar, their meanings and functions are completely different. Somewhat expresses degree and answers ‘How much?’ or ‘To what degree?’. Somehow expresses an unknown manner or reason, or success in managing to do something, and answers ‘How?’, ‘By what means?’ or ‘For some unknown reason’. It limits a statement precisely by showing that a judgement holds only within a specified scope and preventing an overly absolute claim.

適合正式分析和評論 在作文、報告、簡報及商業文件中，insofar as 可以幫助你作出較審慎和有分寸的判斷。 它特別適合分析： ● 一項措施在哪些方面有效； ● 一項論點在哪些部分成立； ● 一項規則在哪些情況下適用。

It suits formal analysis and commentary. In essays, reports, presentations and business documents, insofar as supports cautious, measured judgements about the respects in which a measure is effective, the parts of an argument that hold, or the situations in which a rule applies.
可以縮短較長的限制說法 比較： 兩句意思相近，但第二句更集中地把「有用的程度」和「縮短輪候時間」連接起來。
It can shorten a longer statement of limitation. In the comparison, both versions have similar meanings, but insofar as links the degree of usefulness more directly to the reduction in waiting time.
讓論述不會過度誇大 使用 insofar as 可以提醒讀者：你提出的是有限度的結論，而不是聲稱它在所有情況下都正確。 這能令正式寫作顯得更謹慎、更準確，也更有說服力。
It prevents an argument from sounding exaggerated by signalling that the conclusion is limited rather than universally true, making formal writing more cautious, accurate and persuasive.
Insofar as 的核心意思是「在……範圍或程度內」 使用 insofar as 時，說話者通常不是完全肯定整件事情，而是指出主句只在某個範圍內成立。 這句並不是說整個計劃在所有方面都成功。

Insofar as means ‘within a stated scope or degree’. It usually limits the main statement rather than affirming the whole matter without qualification; the example says that the plan succeeds in one respect, not in every respect.
The plan is successful insofar as it reduces waiting time.
Insofar as 可以放在句首或句中 句首： 句首的從句後通常使用逗號。 句中：
An insofar as-clause may come first or later in the sentence. An initial clause is normally followed by a comma.

Insofar as 常用於較正式的語境 這個句型常見於： ● 作文及學術討論； ● 報告及分析； ● 商業政策； ● 法律或行政文件； ● 正式會議及評論。 在日常會話中，as far as、only if 或 provided that 通常較常見。 例如，Insofar as I know 文法上可以成立，但日常英文通常較常說：

Insofar as is common in formal contexts, including essays and academic discussions, reports and analysis, business policies, legal or administrative documents, formal meetings and commentary. In everyday conversation, as far as, only if or provided that is usually more common; for example, As far as I know is more usual in daily English than Insofar as I know.
Insofar as 與 As long as 的分別 As long as 通常提出一項普通而充分的條件。只要條件成立，主句結果便可以成立。 Insofar as 則通常限制一項判斷、權利、同意或有效性的範圍。 因此，insofar as 比 as long as 更強調「只限於這個程度或方面」，而不是單純表示「只要」。

Insofar as limits scope, whereas as long as normally states an ordinary sufficient condition under which the main-clause result can hold. Insofar as restricts the extent of a judgement, right, agreement or validity and therefore emphasizes ‘only to this degree or in this respect’, not merely ‘provided that’.

In that identifies a specific respect, unlike the broader causal linkers because, since and as. Those linkers normally explain the ordinary cause of an action, event or result and answer ‘Why did this happen?’. In that explains the particular respect in which a description, evaluation or comparison is true and answers ‘In what particular way is this true?’, so the forms are not interchangeable in every sentence. Since can also mean ‘from a past time’, and as can also mean ‘when’ or ‘in a particular manner’; in that has none of those time or manner meanings.
I stayed at home because it was raining.
Why did I stay at home?
The plan is risky in that it depends on only one supplier.
In what particular way is the plan risky?

Using imperative clauses for commands, instructions and requests
Please + base verb + object / other information
Do not + base verb + object / other information
Always / Never + base verb + other information
If / When / Before / After / Once + clause, + imperative
命令句可以直接指出對方需要做甚麼，不需要先使用 you must、you need to 或 you are required to 等較長說法。 第二句更直接，讀者可以立即找到需要完成的動作。

It makes an instruction direct and clear. Instead of using a longer sentence with you must, you need to or you are required to, an imperative states the required action immediately, so readers can find it at once.
命令句非常適合用於食譜、使用說明、課堂指示、路線指引及緊急程序，因為每一步都可以由清 楚的動作開始。

It is useful for giving step-by-step instructions. Imperatives are common in recipes, manuals, classroom instructions, directions and emergency procedures because each step can begin with a clear action.
命令句可以按照情況調整語氣： 因此，命令句不一定代表不禮貌；重點在於你所使用的字詞及說話情境。

It helps you control the strength of your message. Please makes a request more polite, do not clearly prohibits an action, never gives a particularly strong warning, and always emphasizes an important habit or rule. Imperatives are therefore not inherently impolite; their force depends on the wording and context.
Please makes a request more polite.
Do not clearly prohibits an action.
Never gives a particularly strong warning.
Always emphasises an important habit or rule.
由於命令句通常省略主語 you 和情態動詞，因此可以用較少文字表達完整指示。
It makes sentences shorter. Because the subject you and modal verbs are usually omitted, an imperative can express the same complete instruction in fewer words.
You should read the instructions carefully.

It can connect an action with a condition or time. You can place if, when, before, after or once before an imperative to explain exactly when the action should be performed, which is especially useful for safety instructions, work procedures and practical advice.
If you feel dizzy, sit down immediately.

Always use the base form of the verb; it does not change for number or tense. The verb be also remains in its base form.

Put do not before the base verb for a negative imperative: do not + base verb.

It places the most notable thing first. What + noun foregrounds the person or thing you most want to emphasize; in the comparison, a beautiful view appears immediately and receives greater prominence.

令說話和故事更加生動 這個句型很常用於日常對話、描述經歷、講故事及回應別人的消息。 它能讓說話聽起來更有感情，而不是只像列出資料。

It avoids repeatedly using openings such as This is very, It was very or The thing is very by reorganizing the statement as a What-exclamation and adding structural variety to speech and writing.

突出最值得注意的例子 這個句型讓你先表達一個整體意思，再立即指出當中需要特別注意的例子。 讀者可以立即知道哪一類人是句子的重點。
It highlights the most notable example by stating a general point and then identifying the example that deserves particular attention, so readers immediately see which group is the focus.
