把兩個短句合併成一句 你不需要分開寫一個一般句和一個例子句。 使用 especially 後，句子更簡潔，兩個意思之間的關係亦更清楚。

It combines two short sentences in one. Instead of separating a general statement from its example, especially produces a more concise sentence and makes the relationship between the two ideas clearer.
避免重複使用 for example 當你只是想突出某一個重要例子時，可以使用 especially，而不需要每次都寫 for example。 這能增加句式變化，令說話和寫作不會過於重複。
It avoids repeatedly using for example when you want to highlight one important instance, adding variety to speech and writing.
清楚指出重要時間、人物或情況 Especially 不只可以介紹物件，也可以指出某個時間、群體或情況特別重要。
It clearly identifies an important time, person or situation; especially can introduce not only things but also times, groups and circumstances that deserve particular attention.
You should be careful, especially when crossing the road.
適合日常說話和正式寫作 Especially 可以自然地用於： ● 日常對話 ● 學校作文 ● 工作電郵 ● 報告 ● 簡報 ● 意見和建議 它能幫助你由一般觀點發展到更具體的重點。

It suits everyday speech and formal writing, including daily conversation, school essays, workplace emails, reports, presentations, opinions and advice. It helps develop a general view into a specific focus.
先說一般情況，再突出一個例子 Especially 前面的內容通常是一個較廣泛的類別、情況或原則；especially 後面的部分則是當中特 別值得注意的例子。 Oranges 屬於 fruit，因此兩部分的邏輯關係正確。

State a general situation first, then highlight one example. The material before especially normally names a broad category, situation or principle, and what follows identifies a particularly notable member; oranges, for example, logically belong to the broader category fruit.

Especially 後面可以接不同形式 Especially 後面可以接： ● 名詞：especially science ● 名詞詞組：especially young children ● 介詞詞組：especially in winter ● 動名詞詞組：especially reading novels ● when 子句：especially when you are tired ● if 子句：especially if the road is wet ● those who 子句：especially those who live alone
Especially can be followed by several grammatical forms: a noun, noun phrase, prepositional phrase, gerund phrase, when-clause, if-clause or those who-clause.
when 子句：especially when you are tired
if 子句：especially if the road is wet
those who 子句：especially those who live alone
Especially 前面通常使用逗號 當 especially 放在主要陳述之後，加入補充例子或特別情況時，一般在 especially 前使用逗號。
A comma normally comes before especially when it follows the main statement and adds an example or special situation.
The road is dangerous, especially after heavy rain.
Especially 不一定表示「唯一」或「最」 Especially 表示「尤其、特別是」，突出某個例子，但不一定表示它是唯一的例子。 這句表示說話者特別喜歡爵士樂，但不代表他只喜歡爵士樂。
Especially does not necessarily mean only or the most. It highlights one example without implying that it is the sole example; liking jazz especially does not mean liking only jazz.
Especially 和 specially 不同 Especially 表示「尤其、特別是」。 Specially 通常表示某物是「為某個特別目的而專門」製作或安排的。 本課只練習 especially。

Especially and specially have different uses. Especially means ‘particularly’ and highlights a notable example, while specially normally means ‘for a particular purpose’ and describes something deliberately made or arranged for that purpose. This lesson practises only especially.
I enjoy cold drinks, especially lemonade.
This room was specially designed for young children.

Based on identifies the information or criterion used to make a judgement or decision, whereas because of normally gives the direct cause of an event. It separates your own opinion from somebody else’s statement, preventing external information from being presented as your own view and making the message more accurate and reliable.

Using put simply to restate a complex idea clearly
Put simply, the system failed because nobody took responsibility.
簡單來說，這個制度失敗，是因為沒有人負責。
這個句型能提醒聽者或讀者：接下來就是整段內容最重要的意思。
It makes the main point immediately clear. This structure tells the listener or reader that the most important message is coming next.
當你解釋技術性、複雜或陌生的內容後，可以用這個句型把內容說得更容易明白。
It makes difficult explanations easier to understand. You can use it after discussing a technical, complicated or unfamiliar subject to restate the content more accessibly.
你不需要重複所有細節，也可以用一句清楚的句子說出核心意思。
It helps you shorten a long explanation. Instead of repeating every detail, you can present the central idea in one clear sentence.
這個句型能把詳細解釋和最後總結清楚分開，讓說話、作文、報告和簡報更有組織。
It helps organize speaking and writing by clearly separating a detailed explanation from its final summary, improving the structure of speech, essays, reports and presentations.
它讓你不必經常重複使用 in other words、basically 或 the main point is。 Compare 比較
It gives you another way to express a summary and avoids repeatedly using in other words, basically or the main point is.
The company spends more money than it earns. In other words, it is losing money.
Put simply, the company is losing money because it spends more than it earns.
Put simply 通常放在句首
Put simply normally appears at the beginning of a sentence.
Put simply, the plan will not work.

Put does not mean ‘place’ in this expression; it means ‘express’ or ‘explain’. Put simply is close to In simple terms, In other words, To put it simply and Simply put, but every answer in this exercise must use the specified form Put simply, ....

Using in other words to give an equivalent clearer restatement
Statement 1. In other words, equivalent or clearer restatement
The reform was not rejected. In other words, people were willing to give it a chance.
這場改革並沒有被否決。換言之，人們願意給它一個機會。
讓較難的概念更容易明白 你可以先提出一個較抽象或較專業的詞語，再用日常語言解釋。讀者即使不熟悉該詞語，也可以 掌握意思。

It makes difficult ideas easier to understand. You can introduce an abstract or technical term and then explain it in everyday language, allowing readers unfamiliar with the term to grasp its meaning.
The fee is non-refundable. In other words, you will not get your money back.
清楚顯示兩個說法意思相同 沒有連接語時，讀者可能以為第二句是一項新資料。加入 In other words 後，讀者會知道第二句 是在解釋第一句。 第二個版本更清楚顯示兩句之間的關係。

It shows that two statements express the same message. Without the linker, readers may mistake the second sentence for new information; with In other words, they know it explains the first, and the relationship becomes clearer.
在對話中重新解釋自己的意思 當別人聽不明白時，你可以使用 In other words，換一種方式表達，而不需要重新開始整段說 話。
It helps you explain yourself again in conversation. If someone does not understand, you can express the same point in another way without restarting the whole explanation.
避免逐字重複 你可以保留相同意思，但改用較簡單、具體或直接的字詞，使說話和文章不會顯得機械或重複。

It helps you avoid repeating exactly the same words by preserving the meaning while choosing simpler, more concrete or more direct language, so speech and writing do not sound mechanical or repetitive.
令解釋更有條理 這個句型能把「主要概念」和「簡單解釋」連接起來，適合用於作文、報告、簡報、會議和日常說明。
It makes explanations easier to follow by linking a main concept to a simple explanation, which is useful in essays, reports, presentations, meetings and everyday explanations.
In other words 的意思是「換言之」或「也就是說」。後面的內容必須重述前面的基本意 思，而不是加入完全不同的新觀點。
In other words means ‘to put it another way’ or ‘that is to say’. What follows must restate the same basic idea rather than introduce an entirely different new point.
當 In other words 放在新句子的開首時，In 要使用大寫，並在 words 後加逗號：
At the beginning of a new sentence, capitalize In and put a comma after words.

Using the second conditional for unreal or unlikely situations
If + subject + were / past tense, subject + would / could / might + base verb
Subject + would / could / might + base verb + if + subject + were / past tense
If + subject + were not / did not + base verb, subject + would / could / might + base verb
If I were the school principal, I would create a quiet study room.
如果我是校長，我會設立一間安靜的自修室。
If I were the school principal
這個句型能立即讓聽者知道，你正在想像另一種情況，而不是描述目前的事實。
It clearly separates facts from imagination. This structure tells the listener immediately that you are imagining a different situation rather than describing a real fact.
你可以清楚說明：如果某個條件有所改變，可能會出現甚麼不同結果。 第二句把「假設條件」和「可能結果」直接連接起來，兩者的關係更加清楚。

It connects an imagined condition with its result. You can clearly explain how changing one condition might produce a different result, and the conditional version links the imagined condition directly to the possible consequence.
你可以使用這個句型談論夢想、不太可能出現的情況、想像中的決定，以及可以如何改善問題。
It helps you discuss dreams and possible solutions. You can use this structure to talk about dreams, unlikely possibilities, imaginary decisions and possible improvements.
使用 If I were you, I would... 提出建議，通常比直接命令對方更加婉轉。
It provides a polite way to give advice. If I were you, I would ... is usually gentler than directly telling someone what to do.
這個句型適合用於對話、作文、討論和簡報，因為它能幫助你分析不同可能性，而不只是描述目 前的情況。

It helps you develop deeper answers. This structure is useful in conversations, essays, discussions and presentations because it helps you explore possibilities instead of describing only existing facts.
過去式不一定表示過去 在這個句型中，過去式用來表示情況並非目前的事實，或未來發生的機會不大。 這句談的是想像中的現在或未來，而不是過去。

The past form here does not necessarily refer to past time. It signals that the situation is not a present fact or is unlikely in the future; the example imagines a present or future situation rather than describing the past.
If I won the lottery, I would travel around the world.
Be 動詞通常使用 were 在標準的完全假設句中，I、he、she、it 等主語後面都使用 were。 本練習不使用 If I was you。
Use were with be in the standard fully hypothetical form after I, he, she, it and other subjects. This lesson does not use If I was you.
Do not use would in the if-clause.

結果部分可以使用 would、could 或 might Would 表示在該假設下會出現的結果。 Could 表示能力或機會。 Might 表示可能性，但並不肯定。
Use would, could or might in the result clause. Would gives the expected result under the imagined condition, could expresses ability or opportunity, and might expresses an uncertain possibility.
注意逗號的位置 If 子句放在前面時，兩部分之間需要逗號。 If 子句放在後面時，通常不需要逗號。
Use a comma when the if-clause comes first; when it follows the result clause, no comma is normally needed.
不要與其他條件句混淆 真實或有可能發生： 完全假設或可能性較低： 與過去事實相反： 本課只練習第二種句型。

Do not confuse this unreal conditional with other conditional patterns. A present-form if-clause describes a real or possible condition, the past-form second conditional describes a wholly imagined or less likely situation, and if + past perfect describes a condition contrary to past fact. This lesson practises only the second pattern.

清楚顯示原因與結果 這個句型讓讀者立即明白前面的事情造成了甚麼後果。
It shows cause and result clearly by telling readers immediately what consequence the preceding event produced.
The road was flooded, delaying all the buses.
把兩個相關意思合併起來 你可以把兩句短句合併成一句，避免文章出現太多零碎句子。
It combines two related ideas in one sentence and avoids a passage made up of too many fragmented short sentences.
The wind blew the door shut, trapping us outside.
避免重複使用 so 和 as a result 學生經常重複使用： , V-ing 提供另一種自然的因果表達方法，令句式更多變。
It avoids repeating so, therefore, as a result and because of this, providing another natural way to express cause and result and increasing sentence variety.
令事件發展更加連貫 這個句型把一件事及其後果緊密連接，特別適合描述故事、意外、變化和事件經過。
It makes events flow more naturally by tightly linking an event to its consequence, which is especially effective for stories, accidents, changes and sequences of events.
The child knocked over the glass, spilling juice over the table.
適合用於故事、報告和解釋 你可以使用這個句型： ● 描述一件事帶來的即時結果； ● 解釋某項決定造成的影響； ● 報告問題或意外的後果； ● 在作文中連接前因後果。

It is useful in stories, reports and explanations for describing an immediate result, explaining the impact of a decision, reporting the consequence of a problem or accident, and linking causes and effects in an essay.

V-ing 部分說明「結果」，而不是「目的」 結果： 目的： causing the boxes to fall 是實際發生的結果。 to avoid the cyclist 是司機想達到的目的。
The -ing phrase expresses a result, not a purpose. Causing the boxes to fall describes what actually happened as a consequence, whereas to avoid the cyclist describes the driver’s intended goal.

The driver turned the wheel to avoid the cyclist.

必須清楚指出誰或甚麼造成結果 正確： 改寫： 不自然： 最後一句錯誤地表示「道路從單車上掉下來」。
Make it clear who or what causes the result. The natural rewrite makes the icy road the cause of Ben’s fall; the unnatural version incorrectly suggests that the road itself fell off a bicycle.
V-ing 部分沒有獨立時態 時間主要由前面的主句動詞表示。
The -ing phrase has no independent tense; the verb in the preceding main clause supplies the time reference.

Do not confuse this result phrase with a reduced relative clause. A reduced relative such as waiting outside modifies a noun, whereas a result participle clause such as sending the students back to class states the consequence of the main event.

Using thereby + -ing to state a direct result
Main clause, thereby + verb-ing + other information
She woke up earlier, thereby avoiding the morning traffic.
她提早起床，從而避開了早上的交通擠塞。
讀者可以立即看出哪個行動帶來後面的結果。
It makes the cause-and-result relationship clear, so the reader can immediately see which action produced the result.
你不需要再用 so 或 as a result 寫另一個完整分句，也可以簡潔地交代結果。 第二句較緊湊，並把「流程自動化」與「降低成本」的因果關係直接連接起來。

It combines two ideas more concisely. Instead of adding another complete clause with so or as a result, you can express the consequence with thereby + V-ing; the result is tighter and links the cause directly to its effect.
這個句型通常可以避免重複相同的主語，令句子更流暢。
It reduces unnecessary repetition by often removing the need to repeat the same subject, making the sentence flow more smoothly.
在作文、報告及職場寫作中，當你要解釋一項決定、方法或改變帶來甚麼影響時，thereby 十分實 用。
It is useful in essays, reports and workplace writing, especially when explaining how a decision, method or change produces an effect.
你可以準確說明一個行動是「減少、改善、容許、防止、促成」還是「創造」某個結果。

It helps you describe results precisely by showing whether an action reduces a problem, improves a situation, allows another action, prevents a difficulty, enables someone to do something or creates a new result.
thereby 通常放在主句之後，前面加上逗號。
Place thereby after the main clause, normally preceded by a comma.
常見組合： thereby 後面必須使用 V-ing，不可直接使用原形動詞。
Use the -ing form after thereby. Common combinations include thereby reducing, improving, allowing, preventing, making and creating; do not use the base form directly after thereby.
The company automated the process, thereby reducing costs.
主句說明行動或情況，而 thereby 部分則說明該行動或情況所帶來的結果。 兩部分之間必須有清楚的因果關係，不能只是先後發生的兩件事。

The thereby phrase expresses a result. The main clause states an action or situation, and the thereby phrase states the result it produces. The two parts must have a clear cause-and-result relationship rather than merely describing two events in sequence.
時態由主句動詞表達；thereby 後面的動詞仍然使用 V-ing。
The main verb carries the tense; the verb after thereby remains in the -ing form.
當結果涉及另一個人或事物時，可使用 allowing、enabling、helping、giving、making 或 preventing 等連接動詞。

Use a bridge verb when another person or thing receives the result. Useful choices include thereby allowing someone to, enabling someone to, helping someone, giving someone, making it easier for someone to, and preventing someone from.
thereby making it easier for someone to...
The school installed more lights, thereby making the corridor safer.
so 後面接「主語＋完整動詞」，用來連接兩個完整分句，語氣較日常和直接。 thereby 後面接 V-ing，把結果濃縮成分詞短語。它的語氣通常較正式，並強調「透過前面的行動 ，從而產生這個結果」。 重要： 並非所有 so 分句都可以直接刪去主語來改寫。有時需要加入 causing、making、 allowing、enabling 或 preventing 等動詞。

Thereby is different from so. So is followed by a subject and finite verb, links two complete clauses, and is common in everyday speech and writing. Thereby is followed by an -ing form, compresses the result into a participial phrase, usually sounds more formal, and specifically says that the preceding action produced the result. A so-clause cannot always be converted simply by deleting its subject; a bridge verb such as causing, making, allowing, enabling or preventing may be needed.

Using thereafter to introduce a later event or state
Earlier event or period. Thereafter, + subject + verb + later event or state
The first phase ended in June. Thereafter, attention shifted to training.
第一階段於六月結束。其後，重點便轉到培訓上。
讓事情的先後次序更清楚 Thereafter 能讓讀者立即明白，第二件事是在第一件事之後發生的。
It makes the order of events clear. Thereafter tells readers directly that the second event happened after the first.
避免反覆使用 then 和 after that 學生描述一連串事件時，經常重複使用 then。Thereafter 提供另一種表達方式，使文章不會顯得 單調。 兩句意思相同，但第二句較適合正式記錄。

It helps you avoid repeating then and after that. Students often repeat then when describing a sequence; thereafter provides an alternative and prevents monotonous writing. The compared sentences have the same meaning, but the version with thereafter better suits a formal record.
適合報告、程序說明和歷史敘述 你可以使用 thereafter 清楚描述項目、調查、實驗或歷史事件的不同階段。
It is useful for reports, procedures and historical writing. You can use thereafter to describe different stages of a project, investigation, experiment or historical event.
連接兩個句子，同時避免句子過長 你可以把過長的句子分成兩句，再使用 thereafter 顯示兩者的關係，使內容更容易閱讀。

It connects two sentences without making one sentence too long. Instead of placing many events inside one long sentence, you can divide the information into two shorter sentences and connect them with thereafter, making it easier to read.
可以帶出下一個階段或其後持續的情況 Thereafter 既可以描述其後發生的新事件，也可以表示某種情況從那時起一直持續。
It can introduce a new stage or a continuing situation. Thereafter can describe either a later event or something that remained true from that time onwards.
The company changed its policy. Thereafter, employees were allowed to work from home.
Thereafter 必須指向前面清楚提及的事件 如果前面沒有清楚的事件，讀者便不知道 thereafter 指「甚麼之後」。
Thereafter must refer to a clearly stated earlier event, time or stage. If no such event has been mentioned, readers cannot tell what thereafter means ‘after’.
The examination ended. Thereafter, the students left the hall.
本練習把 Thereafter 放在第二句句首 使用以下格式： Thereafter 後面要加逗號。
In this exercise, put Thereafter at the beginning of the second sentence in the format ‘Sentence 1. Thereafter, sentence 2.’ and follow it with a comma.
Thereafter 後面必須接完整句子 正確： 錯誤： Thereafter 後面需要有主語和完整動詞。
Follow Thereafter with a complete sentence containing a subject and a finite verb, not an -ing fragment.
Thereafter 不一定表示「立即」 Thereafter 表示某件事在較早事件之後發生，但不一定是立即發生。 如要強調「立即」，通常使用 immediately afterwards 或 as soon as。

Thereafter does not necessarily mean immediately. It says that something happened after an earlier event, but not necessarily at once; use immediately afterwards or as soon as when immediacy must be emphasized.
The course ended in May. Thereafter, the students continued to use the online library.
Thereafter 比 then 和 after that 較正式 ● then：常用於日常說話 ● after that：日常說話和一般寫作都很常見 ● thereafter：較常見於報告、程序說明、正式記錄和歷史敘述 Thereafter 並非在所有情況下都比 then「更好」，但在較正式的文章中十分實用。

Thereafter is more formal than then or after that. Then is common in everyday speech, after that is common in both everyday speech and general writing, and thereafter is more typical of reports, procedural accounts, formal records and historical narratives. It is not better than then in every context, but it is useful in formal writing.
after that：日常說話和一般寫作都很常見
thereafter：較常見於報告、程序說明、正式記錄和歷史敘述
否定意思放在 Thereafter 後面的句子內 Thereafter 本身沒有特別的否定形式。
Put any negative meaning inside the sentence that follows Thereafter; thereafter itself has no special negative form.
The patient left the hospital. Thereafter, she did not require further treatment.

In this structure, All normally means “the only thing”. Here, all does not usually mean “all people” or “all things”; it is closer to “the only thing that ...”, “the only action that ...”, or “everything that ...”. For example, All I need is your help means The only thing I need is your help.

All must be followed by an incomplete clause. In All I need is some water, need is missing its object: I need what? The answer is some water. Thus, All I need means “everything I need” or “the only thing I need”.

本練習使用 is 或 was 整個 All + 子句 被視為一項資料或一件事情，因此本練習使用單數動詞： 即使後面的重點部分是複數，本練習仍以 is / was 作為標準答案。

Use is or was in this exercise. The whole All + clause is treated as one piece of information or one thing, so this exercise uses a singular verb. Even when the focused element that follows is plural, is or was remains the standard answer: All I need is two pens; All she wanted was two tickets.
All I need is two pens.
All she wanted was two tickets.
時態必須配合句子的時間 現在的情況通常使用 is： （我想要的只是一點安寧。） 過去的情況通常使用 was： （我當時想要的只是一點安寧。）
The tense must match the time of the sentence. Present situations normally use is, as in All I want is some peace. Past situations normally use was, as in All I wanted was some peace.

使用 did 時，was 後面接原形動詞 因為 did 已經表達過去時，所以後面的行動使用原形動詞。

When the All-clause uses did, follow was with the base form of the verb. Because did already marks the past tense, the following action remains in the base form: All Grace did was smile, not All Grace did was smiled.

The focused element can take different forms: a noun (All I need is a pen), a pronoun (All I want is you), a to-infinitive (All she wants is to go home), a base-form verb (All he did was wait), a that-clause (All we know is that the door is locked), or other information (All I remember is where we met).

Using alternative questions to offer stated choices
Be + subject + option A + or + option B?
一般現在式或一般過去式
Do / Does / Did + subject + base verb + option A + or + option B?
情態動詞或其他助動詞
Modal / Auxiliary verb + subject + verb + option A + or + option B?
Wh-word + question form, + option A + or + option B?
Is the problem technical or political?
這個問題是技術性的，還是政治性的？
清楚列出可供選擇的項目 這個句型能直接列出所有主要選項，讓對方立即知道需要在甚麼項目之間作出選擇。
It makes the available choices clear This structure tells the listener exactly which possibilities they should consider.
把兩條問題合併成一句 你不需要連續提出兩條是非問句，而可以把它們合併成一句較簡潔的問題。 （這個問題是技術性的嗎？它是政治性的嗎？） （這個問題是技術性的，還是政治性的？）

It combines two questions into one Instead of asking two separate yes-or-no questions, you can ask one shorter alternative question. Compare: Is the problem technical? Is it political? Is the problem technical or political?
Is the problem technical? Is it political?
Is the problem technical or political?
讓對方作出較具體的回答 一般問句可能只得到 Yes 或 No，但選擇問句會引導對方直接說出所選的項目。
It encourages a specific answer A yes-or-no question may produce only “yes” or “no”. An alternative question encourages the listener to name the exact option.
加快討論和決策 由於選項已經清楚排列在問題中，對話、會議或決策過程通常可以更快地繼續。
It helps people make decisions more quickly The choices are already organised inside the question, so the conversation can move forward more efficiently.
適用於多種真實情境 無論是點餐、安排會議、服務顧客、進行問卷調查、討論計劃或分析問題，都可以使用選擇問句。
It is useful in many real situations Alternative questions are useful when ordering food, arranging meetings, serving customers, conducting surveys, discussing plans and solving problems.
讓不同選項排列得更整齊 在 or 的兩邊使用相同的文法結構，可以讓讀者或聽者更容易比較不同選項。
It helps organise alternatives in a balanced way Using the same grammatical form on both sides of or makes the alternatives easier to compare.
選擇問句通常不能只回答 Yes 或 No 對方通常需要選出其中一項，而不是只回答 Yes 或 No。 （問題：你想喝茶還是咖啡？） （回答：咖啡，謝謝。）

An alternative question normally cannot be answered with Yes or No alone. The listener is expected to choose one of the stated options. For example, the usual answer to Would you like tea or coffee? is an option such as Coffee, please.
The listener should normally choose one of the stated options.
Question: Would you like tea or coffee?
助動詞要放在主語前面
Place the auxiliary verb before the subject.
Does Leo want the red shirt or the green shirt?
Leo does want the red shirt or the green shirt?
Do、Does、Did 及情態動詞後使用原形動詞
Use the base form after do, does, did and modal verbs.
Does she walk or take the bus?
Does she walks or takes the bus?
兩個選項應使用平行結構 兩邊最好使用相同類型的詞語或句子成分。
Use parallel structures for the alternatives. The two sides should use the same type of word or sentence element, such as adjective + adjective, noun + noun, or verb phrase + verb phrase.
Is the task easy or difficult?
Would you like tea or coffee?
Should we wait here or return home?
相同的字詞通常不需要重複 （湯姆步行上學，還是乘巴士上學？）
Shared words normally do not need to be repeated. For example, Does Tom walk to school or take the bus? is preferable to repeating Does Tom and to school in both alternatives.
Does Tom walk to school or does Tom take the bus?
Does Tom walk to school or take the bus?
如果兩個選項需要不同的助動詞，可以保留完整分句 （客人已經到達，還是仍在途中？） 這裏不能共用同一個助動詞，因為第一部分使用 have，第二部分使用 are。

Keep complete clauses when the alternatives need different auxiliaries, as in Have the guests arrived, or are they still travelling? The two alternatives cannot share one auxiliary because the first uses have and the second uses are.
Have the guests arrived, or are they still travelling?
口語中的語調 說話時，前面的選項通常使用升調，最後一個選項則使用降調。
In speech, the earlier alternative normally has rising intonation and the final alternative has falling intonation.
Would you like tea ↗ or coffee ↘?
本課不集中練習 or not 這句在文法上正確，但 or not 有時帶有催促、不耐煩或要求明確答覆的語氣，因此不列入本課的 主要練習範圍。

This lesson does not focus on or not. A question such as Are you coming or not? is grammatical, but or not can sometimes sound urging or impatient, or demand a definite answer, so it is outside the main practice in this lesson.

Using declarative questions for confirmation, surprise or follow-up
Subject + verb / auxiliary verb + other information + ?
幫助你迅速確認資料 當別人剛剛告訴你一件事時，你可以直接重複重點並加上問號，不需要重新組織一條完整的一般 問句。 （會議已經取消了？）

It helps you confirm information quickly. When someone has just told you something, you can repeat the key information with a question mark instead of reorganising it as a full standard question: The meeting has been cancelled?
自然表達驚訝 陳述式問句可以讓聽者立即感受到你對消息感到意外。 （你一直步行回家？）
It shows surprise naturally. A declarative question lets the listener immediately hear that the news has surprised you: You walked all the way home?
You walked all the way home?
令追問聽起來更像自然對話 當你正在與別人交談時，這個句型可以讓追問簡短、直接，不會像正式訪問問題一樣生硬。
It makes follow-up questions sound conversational. During a conversation, the structure keeps a follow-up short and direct without making it sound as stiff as a formal interview question.
表示你對答案已有一定猜測 一般問句可以完全中立地索取資料，而陳述式問句通常表示你已經相信某件事可能是真的，只是 希望對方確認。 Compare 比較： （你讀完整本書了嗎？） 這是一條較中立的一般問題。 （你讀完整本書了？） 這句帶有確認或驚訝的語氣。

It shows that you already have an idea of the answer. A standard question can request information neutrally, whereas a declarative question normally suggests that you already think something may be true and only want confirmation. Did you finish the whole book? is neutral; You finished the whole book? conveys confirmation or surprise.
Did you finish the whole book?
保留陳述句語序 一般問句通常把助動詞放在主語之前： 陳述式問句不使用這種倒裝：
Keep statement word order. A standard question normally places the auxiliary before the subject, as in Did you call her? A declarative question does not use this inversion: You called her?
必要時移除 do、does 或 did 當一般問句使用 do、does 或 did 時，改寫後通常要移除這些助動詞，並把主要動詞改成正確形 式。

Remove do, does or did when necessary. When a standard question uses one of these auxiliaries, the declarative question normally removes it and changes the main verb to the correct form: Does Ben work here? becomes Ben works here?; Did Emma leave early? becomes Emma left early?
be 動詞、情態動詞及完成式助動詞放在主語後
Keep be verbs, modal verbs and perfect auxiliaries after the subject be Is she coming? She is coming? Can you swim? You can swim? Have they finished? They have finished?
使用上揚語調 在說話時，句尾聲調通常上揚，讓聽者知道這是一條問題，而不是普通陳述句。
Use rising intonation. In speech, the voice normally rises at the end so that the listener recognises the utterance as a question rather than an ordinary statement.
主要用於確認、驚訝或追問 陳述式問句通常表示說話者已經聽到、看到或猜到某些資料，現在想確認是否正確。 這句通常表示說話者對「你勝出了」感到驚訝，並希望確認消息。

Use declarative questions mainly for confirmation, surprise or follow-up questions. They normally show that the speaker has heard, seen or guessed some information and now wants to check whether it is correct. You won the competition? usually expresses surprise at the news and asks for confirmation.
較常用於對話 陳述式問句常見於日常對話、電影對白及即時追問。正式問卷、正式訪問或需要完全中立地索取 資料時，一般問句通常較合適。

Declarative questions are more common in conversation, film dialogue and immediate follow-up questions. Standard questions are generally more suitable in formal questionnaires or interviews, or when requesting information in a completely neutral way.

Supposing that + subject + present simple, + what / how / where + will / can / should + subject + base verb?
較想像性或較不可能發生的情況
Supposing that + subject + past simple, + what / how / where + would / could + subject + base verb?

這個句型讓你在問題真正發生前先想像相關情況，並討論應該採取甚麼行動。
It helps you discuss possible problems You can use this structure to imagine a problem before it happens and discuss what action should be taken.
聽者會立即明白你正在討論一個假設可能性，而不是表示事情一定會發生。
It makes the hypothetical meaning clear The listener immediately understands that you are discussing an imagined possibility rather than stating that something will definitely happen.
當你以 Supposing that ... 開始時，便可以有條理地詢問行動、選擇、結果或解決方法。
It provides a useful speaking frame Once you begin with Supposing that ..., you can continue by asking about an action, choice, result or solution.
這個句型能把假設情況和相關問題連接成一句完整句子，讓兩者的關係更加清楚。
It connects a situation and its consequence The structure places the imagined condition and the related question in one complete sentence.
The structure places the imagined condition and the related question in one complete sentence.
當你不想反覆使用 if 時，可以使用 Supposing that ...，令討論、簡報或口語回答有更多句式變 化。 Compare 比較 （如果計劃失敗怎麼辦？我們會怎樣做？） （假如計劃失敗，我們下一步會是甚麼？） 第二句把假設情況和需要討論的行動連接起來，問題更加完整和集中。

It gives you an alternative to repeating if and adds sentence variety to discussions, presentations and spoken answers. Compare What if the plan fails? What will we do? with Supposing that the plan fails, what would be our next step? The second version connects the hypothetical situation with the action to be discussed, making the question more complete and focused.
What if the plan fails? What will we do?
Supposing that the plan fails, what would be our next step?
用來提出一個假設情況 Supposing that ... 的意思接近「假如……」或「假設……」。說話者先請對方想像一個情況，然後 討論可能的結果或下一步行動。 （假如店舖已經關門，我們會到哪裏？）

Use Supposing that ... to introduce a hypothetical situation. It means roughly “suppose that” or “what if”. The speaker first asks the listener to imagine a situation and then discusses a possible result or next action, as in Supposing that the shop is closed, where will we go?
Supposing that the shop is closed, where will we go?
談及未來時，條件部分通常不用 will 在 Supposing that 後面，通常使用現在式表示未來可能發生的情況。

When discussing the future, do not normally use will in the condition. After Supposing that, use the present tense for a possible future situation: Supposing that it rains tomorrow ..., not Supposing that it will rain tomorrow ....
Supposing that it rains tomorrow, what will we do?
Supposing that it will rain tomorrow, what will we do?
過去式可以令假設聽起來更不確定 當情況較不可能發生，或純粹屬於想像時，可以使用過去式，並在主句使用 would 或 could。 （假如你遺失了手機，你會怎樣做？）

A past form can make a supposition sound less certain. When the situation is less likely or purely imaginary, use a past form in the supposing-clause and would or could in the main clause, as in Supposing that you lost your phone, what would you do?
Supposing that you lost your phone, what would you do?
主句的情態動詞要配合原意 主句可以使用： will：詢問將會發生的事； can：詢問可能的方法或能力； should：詢問適當的做法； would：討論想像中的結果； could：討論假設情況中的可能方法。

Choose a modal in the main clause that preserves the intended meaning: will asks what will happen; can asks about a possible method or ability; should asks about the appropriate action; would discusses an imagined result; and could discusses a possible method in a hypothetical situation.
本練習必須保留 that 在日常對話中，人們有時會說 Supposing ...，省略 that。不過，本練習的目標句型是完整的 Supposing that ...，因此答案不可省略 that。

Keep that in every answer in this exercise. In everyday conversation, speakers sometimes omit it and say Supposing ..., but the target form here is the full Supposing that ..., so that must not be left out.

Do not confuse Supposing that with Provided that. Supposing that asks someone to imagine a situation, as in Supposing that the train is cancelled, what will we do? Provided that means “only if a condition is met”, as in You can travel provided that you have a valid ticket.

Using Assuming that to introduce an accepted assumption
Assuming that + subject + verb, + main clause
Main clause, + assuming that + subject + verb
Assuming that the data is accurate, the strategy seems reasonable.
假設數據準確，這項策略看來是合理的。
清楚說明推論所依據的條件 這個句型能先告訴讀者「以下結論是基於甚麼前提」，讓兩個意思之間的關係更清楚。 （假設道路暢通，我們便會在中午前到達。） 讀者可以立即明白，準時到達的預測是以道路暢通為前提。

It makes the condition underlying an inference clear. The structure tells the reader which premise supports the following conclusion. In Assuming that the road is clear, we will arrive before noon, the reader can immediately see that the prediction of arriving on time depends on the road being clear.
Assuming that the road is clear, we will arrive before noon.
避免把未經證實的事情說成事實 當資料仍未完全確認時，你可以使用這個句型，表明你的結論只是建基於某個假設。 （假設報告正確，上月的銷售額便有所上升。） 這比直接說「Sales increased」更加謹慎和準確。

It helps you avoid presenting unverified information as fact. When information has not been fully confirmed, the structure shows that the conclusion rests on an assumption. Assuming that the report is correct, sales increased last month is more cautious and accurate than simply saying Sales increased.
Assuming that the report is correct, sales increased last month.
適合用於計劃和解決問題 你可以先設定一個可能成立的條件，再討論下一步行動。 （假設所有人都同意，我們便可以在下星期開始這個項目。） 這種表達方式適合會議、團隊討論、商業計劃及日常安排。

It is useful for planning and problem-solving. You can establish a condition that may hold and then discuss the next action. Assuming that everyone agrees, we can begin the project next week is suitable in meetings, team discussions, business planning and everyday arrangements.
Assuming that everyone agrees, we can begin the project next week.
把較長的說法縮短 兩句意思相同，但第二句省略了 If we assume，表達更加直接。

It can shorten a longer expression. If we assume that the data is accurate, the strategy seems reasonable and Assuming that the data is accurate, the strategy seems reasonable have the same meaning, but the second omits If we assume and is more direct.
If we assume that the data is accurate, the strategy seems reasonable.
Assuming that the data is accurate, the strategy seems reasonable.
增加句式變化 你可以把假設放在句首，先突出前提；也可以把它放在句末，先說出主要結論。 這能避免每個條件句都以 if 開始，令說話和寫作不會過於重複。

It gives you another way to organise a sentence. Put the assumption first to foreground the premise, or place it last to state the main conclusion first. This also avoids beginning every conditional sentence with if and makes speaking and writing less repetitive.
Assuming that the weather improves, we will leave tomorrow.
We will leave tomorrow, assuming that the weather improves.
That 後面必須接完整子句 that 後面需要有主語和動詞。 （假設天氣好轉，我們明天便會出發。）
That must be followed by a complete clause containing a subject and a verb: Assuming that the weather improves, we will leave tomorrow, not Assuming that better weather ....
Assuming that the weather improves, we will leave tomorrow.
Assuming that better weather, we will leave tomorrow.
談及未來時，假設子句通常使用現在式 即使事情會在未來發生，assuming that 後面通常使用現在式，而主句可以使用 will、may、can 或 should。

When referring to the future, normally use the present tense in the assumption clause. Even when the event is in the future, assuming that is usually followed by a present form, while the main clause may use will, may, can or should.
Assuming that the train arrives on time, we will reach the airport early.
Assuming that the train will arrive on time, we will reach the airport early.
放在句首時，後面通常加逗號 放在句末時，主句與假設部分之間也通常使用逗號：
When the assumption comes first, normally place a comma after it. When it comes at the end, a comma also normally separates the main clause from the assumption.
Assuming that the shop is open**,** we can buy some bread.
We can buy some bread**,** assuming that the shop is open.
可以使用否定形式 （假設不下雨，比賽便會繼續。）
A negative assumption is possible. For example: Assuming that it does not rain, the match will continue.
Assuming that + subject + does not / is not / cannot...
Assuming that it does not rain, the match will continue.
Assuming that 不表示前提一定是真的 這個句型只是暫時把某件事當作真實，以便繼續討論。它並不是在確認該事情一定會發生。 （假設數字正確，公司便錄得盈利。） 說話者仍然可能需要核實這些數字。

Assuming that does not mean the assumption is certainly true. It treats something as true temporarily so that the discussion can continue; it does not confirm that the event will happen. In Assuming that the figures are correct, the company made a profit, the figures may still need to be checked.
Assuming that the figures are correct, the company made a profit.

Assuming that 與 Supposing that 的分別 兩者都可以表示「假設／假如」，而且在不少句子中可以互換。不過，它們通常有以下語氣差別： 較常用於把某個條件當作一個暫時的工作前提，再進行分析、計算、計劃或判斷。它的語氣通常 較中性，也較常見於會議、報告和正式討論。 （假設數據準確，這項策略看來是合理的。） 這句的重點是：先暫時接受數據準確，再判斷策略是否合理。 通常較有「假如真的發生……會怎樣？」的探索意味，語氣往往較口語化，尤其常用來提出假設性 問題。 （假如計劃失敗，我們下一步會是甚麼？） 這句的重點是：想像一個可能出現的情況，並探索應對方法。 簡單分辨 Assuming that：先接受一個前提，再作推論。 Supposing that：提出一個假想情況，再探索可能結果。 這是常見的語氣傾向，並非絕對的文法規則。 在本練習中，所有答案必須保留完整形式 assuming that，不可省略 that。

Assuming that and Supposing that can both mean “assuming” or “supposing” and are interchangeable in many sentences, but they tend to differ in tone. Assuming that more often treats a condition as a temporary working premise for analysis, calculation, planning or judgement; it is usually more neutral and more common in meetings, reports and formal discussion. In Assuming that the data is accurate, the strategy seems reasonable, the data is provisionally accepted before the strategy is judged. Supposing that more often has the exploratory sense of “what if this really happens?”, is often more conversational, and is especially common in hypothetical questions. In Supposing that the plan fails, what would be our next step?, the speaker imagines a possible situation and explores a response. Put simply, Assuming that accepts a premise and then draws an inference, while Supposing that presents an imagined situation and explores a possible result. This is a common tendency, not an absolute grammatical rule. In this exercise, every answer must retain the full form assuming that; do not omit that.
Assuming that the data is accurate, the strategy seems reasonable.
Supposing that the plan fails, what would be our next step?

It supports deeper evaluation: why an achievement is more remarkable, a mistake more serious, an experience more meaningful, a result more surprising or an action more admirable. It is therefore useful in everyday speech, stories, essays, reports, reviews and presentations.

It turns a difficulty into a stronger reason for action This structure helps you explain that a problem, risk or weakness is not a reason to give up. Instead, it makes preparation or action even more necessary.

It makes advice sound more convincing Instead of simply saying “You should do this,” you can first provide a clear reason and then explain why the action is especially necessary. Compare: The deadline is close, so we should start now. The deadline is close. That is all the more reason to start now.

這個句型適合用於討論、作文、報告和工作溝通，特別適合回應反對意見、分析風險或加強建議。
It is useful in discussions, essays, reports and workplace communication, especially when responding to an objection, analysing a risk or strengthening a recommendation.
除了反覆使用 because、so 或 therefore，你也可以利用這個句型，把一個情況和應採取的行動連 接起來。
It gives you another way to connect ideas Instead of repeatedly using because, so or therefore, you can use this structure to connect a situation with an action.
這個句型表示「原本的情況令某個行動變得更有理由」 它通常用來說明： 某個問題並不是放棄的理由； 某個困難反而令準備、行動或小心處理變得更加必要； 前面的事實進一步加強後面的建議。 例如： （路程很長。正因如此，我們更有理由仔細規劃。） 路程很長並不是「不要出發」的理由，而是「更應仔細規劃」的理由。

This pattern means that an existing situation gives even stronger justification for an action. It can show that a problem is not a reason to give up, that a difficulty makes preparation, action or caution more necessary, or that a preceding fact strengthens a recommendation. That or This must clearly refer to the preceding situation, normally a fact, problem, risk or difficulty. In The road is dangerous. Do not use this pattern for an ordinary result: it must express stronger justification. The road was wet, so the car moved slowly gives an ordinary result; The road was wet. That was all the more reason to drive slowly says the wet road strengthened the reason for careful action. Also distinguish all the more reason to + verb from all the more + adjective/adverb. Reason is a noun followed by the action that should be taken and answers “Why should someone do this?”; The risk is high. That is all the more reason to check everything carefully means that the reason for acting is stronger. All the more + adjective/adverb directly increases the degree of a quality or manner, as in The task was difficult, but that made the final success all the more meaningful. In short, all the more reason to + verb means there is stronger reason to act, whereas all the more + adjective/adverb means a quality or manner has a greater degree. The task was difficult. That is all the more reason to continue strengthens the reason to continue; The task was difficult, which made our success all the more meaningful strengthens the degree of meaningfulness.
The road was wet, so the car moved slowly.
The road was wet. That was all the more reason to drive slowly.
A. All the more reason to + verb
The risk is high. That is all the more reason to check everything carefully.
B. All the more + adjective / adverb
The task was difficult, but that made the final success all the more meaningful.

This lesson does not teach the other meaning of all the same. In It is all the same to me, the phrase means “it makes no difference to me”, not “nevertheless”; that meaning is outside this exercise. Also distinguish three similar structures. All the same means “nevertheless” or “even so” and links ideas with an unexpected contrast: The risks were obvious. All the same, they moved forward. The point is that the difficulty did not prevent the later event. All the more + adjective/adverb means that a degree increases; it does not mean “nevertheless”: The task was difficult, but that made the final success all the more meaningful. The point is that a quality becomes stronger. All the more reason to + verb means that an earlier situation provides a stronger reason to act: If mistakes are costly, that is all the more reason to prepare well. The core distinction is: All the same—a difficulty exists but something still happens; all the more + adjective/adverb—a degree increases; all the more reason to + verb—the reason for an action becomes stronger.
It is all the same to me.
The risks were obvious. All the same, they moved forward.
B. All the more + adjective / adverb

C. All the more reason to + verb

That is all the more reason to + base verb.

Distinguish All the while from similar structures. All the while means that something continues throughout a period: She remained calm all the while. All the more + adjective/adverb increases the degree of a quality or manner, as in The difficulty made the success all the more meaningful; it concerns degree, not duration. All the more reason to ... says that a situation creates stronger justification for an action, as in The road is dangerous, so that is all the more reason to drive carefully; it expresses a reason, not “throughout”. All the same means “nevertheless” or “even so” and introduces a concession or contrast, as in The journey was tiring. All the same, we enjoyed it; it does not describe duration.

Now is the best time to
Using Now is the best time to for timely action
Now + is + the best time + to + base verb + other information
Now is the best time to study.
現在是讀書的最佳時機。
這個句型能立即突出「現在」的重要性，讓聽者明白不應錯過目前的時機。
It clearly emphasises timing This structure immediately tells the listener that the present time is especially important or suitable.
（現在開始儲蓄。） （現在是開始儲蓄的最佳時機。） 第二句同樣能提出明確建議，但語氣不像命令般直接，較容易讓別人接受。

It gives advice without sounding like a direct order Compare: Start saving money now. Now is the best time to start saving money. The second sentence still gives strong advice, but it sounds less like a command.
The second sentence still gives strong advice, but it sounds less like a command.
你可以把「現在最適合」和「應該做甚麼」合併成一句，令表達更簡潔。
It combines timing and action in one sentence Instead of writing: You should begin now. This is the most suitable time. You can write: Now is the best time to begin.
You should begin now. This is the most suitable time.
這個句型適合用來鼓勵別人開始計劃、解決問題、作出改變、把握機會，或及時採取行動。
It is useful for persuasion You can use this structure when encouraging someone to: begin a plan； solve a problem； make a change； take advantage of an opportunity； act before it is too late.
act before it is too late.
記住這個固定框架後，你可以在說話時快速加入不同動作，更容易組織完整答案。

It provides a useful speaking frame Once you remember: Now is the best time to... you can quickly add your own action: Now is the best time to ask. Now is the best time to prepare. Now is the best time to make a change.
Now is the best time to ask.
Now is the best time to prepare.
Now is the best time to make a change.
在這個句型中，best 是形容詞，用來形容名詞 time。 因此，完整句型並不是 Now is the best + adjective + to...，而是： Now is the best time to + 動詞原形
The complete pattern is “Now is the best time to + base verb”. In this structure, best is an adjective describing the noun time. Write Now is the best time to study, not Now is the best to study.
In this structure, best is an adjective describing the noun time.
在 to 後面必須使用動詞原形。
Use the base form after “to” Correct： Now is the best time to start. Incorrect： Now is the best time to starting. Incorrect： Now is the best time to started.

“Now” does not always mean this exact second. It may refer to this moment, today, this week, the present stage or the current situation.

It means that the present is the most suitable time.
（現在並不是討論這件事的最佳時機。）

Using Not that ..., but ... to correct a possible misunderstanding
Not that the idea is bad, but it needs more careful planning.
並不是說這個想法不好，而是它需要更周詳的規劃。
這個句型可以幫助你較有禮貌地修正誤解。你不需要直接說對方錯了，而可以先澄清自己並非那 個意思，再說明真正的重點。
It helps you correct a misunderstanding politely Instead of directly telling someone that they are wrong, you can first clarify what you do not mean and then explain your real point.
你可以先表示某件事並非完全不好，再指出需要改善的地方，令批評聽起來不會過分直接。 （並不是說你的答案錯了，而是它需要更多支持細節。）
It makes criticism sound less harsh You can acknowledge that something is not completely bad before mentioning the problem. Not that your answer is wrong, but it needs more supporting detail.
You can acknowledge that something is not completely bad before mentioning the problem.
Not that your answer is wrong, but it needs more supporting detail.
如果不使用這個句型，你可能需要使用兩句分開的句子，才能完成澄清和解釋。 第二個版本能更流暢地連接兩個意思。

It combines clarification and explanation Without this structure, you may need two separate sentences. Compare: I am not saying that the plan is bad. I am saying that it needs more time. Not that the plan is bad, but it needs more time. The second version connects the two ideas more smoothly.
I am not saying that the plan is bad. I am saying that it needs more time.
Not that the plan is bad, but it needs more time.
The second version connects the two ideas more smoothly.
當一件事有優點，但同時存在限制、條件或問題時，這個句型可以幫助你表達較全面和平衡的看 法。
It helps you present a more balanced opinion The structure is useful when something has strengths but also has a limitation, condition or problem.
你可以在對話、作文、會議和給予意見時使用這個句型，以澄清立場、回應批評、解釋決定或提出 較婉轉的意見。
It is useful in speaking, essays, meetings and feedback You can use it to clarify your opinion, respond to criticism, explain a decision or give careful feedback.
在 Not that 後面通常要使用包含主語和動詞的完整子句。

Use a complete clause after Not that A clause normally contains a subject and a verb. Not that the restaurant is expensive, but it is too far away. Not that the expensive restaurant, but it is too far away.
Not that the restaurant is expensive, but it is too far away.
Not that the expensive restaurant, but it is too far away.
（並不是說我不喜歡這份工作，而是我需要更有彈性的時間安排。）

The second part gives the real point The information after but should explain what the speaker actually thinks, means or wants to emphasise. Not that I dislike the job, but I need a more flexible schedule.
Not that I dislike the job, but I need a more flexible schedule.
這句並非表示成本完全不重要，而是表示安全才是更重要的考慮。

Not that does not always mean that the first idea is completely false It often means: that is not the main point; that is not the real reason; that is not what I am trying to say. Not that the cost is unimportant, but safety should come first. The speaker is not saying that cost is completely unimportant. The speaker is saying that safety is the more important consideration.
that is not the main point;
that is not the real reason;
that is not what I am trying to say.

Statement A. Even so, Statement B
The market was unstable. Even so, some investors remained confident.
市場並不穩定。即使如此，一些投資者仍保持信心。
它能清楚顯示反差 讀者可以立即明白：即使有前面的困難，後面的結果仍然發生。
It makes the contrast clear The reader can immediately understand that the second result happened despite the first difficulty.
它能自然連接兩個完整意思 你不需要把兩句話分開而不說明關係；even so 能清楚指出兩者之間的讓步關係。
It connects two complete ideas naturally Instead of leaving two short sentences unrelated, even so clearly shows how they are connected.
它能加強第二個意思 把 even so 放在主要結果前，可以突出「事情仍然發生」或「情況仍然成立」。
It gives the second idea more emphasis Placing even so before the main result draws attention to what still happened or remained true.
它能避免重複使用 but 和 however 在說話、作文、報告和簡報中，你可以用另一種自然方式表達轉折。
It helps you avoid repeating but and however You gain another natural way to express contrast in speaking, essays, reports and presentations.
它提供一個容易使用的說話框架 你可以先說明困難，稍作停頓，再用 Even so, ... 說出仍然成立的重點。 第二個版本把困難和出乎意料的結果分開呈現，因此後面的重點更加突出。

It provides a useful speaking frame You can first mention a difficulty, pause, and then continue with Even so, ... Compare The market was unstable, but some investors remained confident. The market was unstable. Even so, some investors remained confident.
You can first mention a difficulty, pause, and then continue with Even so, ...
The market was unstable, but some investors remained confident.
The market was unstable. Even so, some investors remained confident.
Even so 承接前面整個意思 Even so 是承接前面整個意思，而不是只修飾其中一個字。
Even so refers back to the whole preceding idea, not merely to one word in the previous sentence.
Even so refers back to the whole idea in the previous sentence.
注意標點 在本練習中，Even so 前面使用句號，後面使用逗號。

In this exercise, place a full stop before Even so and a comma after it.

前後都必須是完整句子 Even so 前後兩部分都必須是完整句子。
Both the part before Even so and the part after it must be complete sentences.
必須有「儘管如此，仍然……」的意思 只有當第二個意思出乎意料，或在第一個情況下仍然成立時，才使用 even so。
Use Even so only when the meaning is “despite that, this still happens”. The second idea must be unexpected or remain true despite the first situation.
Even though 與 Even so 的句式不同 Even though 後面直接接子句；even so 則承接前面已經完成的句子。

Even though and Even so use different structures. Even though is followed directly by a clause: Even though the market was unstable, some investors remained confident. Even so refers back to an already complete sentence: The market was unstable. Even so, some investors remained confident.
Even though + subject + verb, main clause
Even though the market was unstable, some investors remained confident.
The market was unstable. Even so, some investors remained confident.

There seem to be + plural noun + other information

It avoids presenting uncertain information as fact. When you have noticed signs but do not yet have all the information, the structure makes your statement more accurate. It avoids repeatedly using I think. I think there is a problem can become There seems to be a problem, keeping the focus on the possible problem rather than repeatedly emphasising the speaker's opinion.

to be 後面通常接名詞或名詞詞組 正確： 錯誤： 應改為：
To be is normally followed by a noun or noun phrase, such as a problem, something wrong or several possible reasons.

Using Get + object + to-infinitive to cause or persuade
Subject + get + object + to + base verb + other information
清楚表示「誰促使誰做甚麼」 這個句型能清楚交代促成事情的人，以及實際執行動作的人。 （經理安排員工出席會議。） 讀者可以立即看出：經理負責促成事情，而員工負責出席。
It clearly identifies who causes an action and who actually performs it. In The manager got the staff to attend the meeting, the manager brings the action about and the staff do the attending.
The manager got the staff to attend the meeting.
表示行動成功產生了結果 Ask someone to do something 只表示提出要求，不一定代表對方真的照做。 （她要求他道歉。） Get someone to do something 通常表示她成功令對方採取行動。 （她成功說服他道歉。）

It shows that a request or attempt successfully produced the intended action. Ask someone to do something only reports a request and does not prove compliance: She asked him to apologise. Get someone to do something normally shows that the persuasion succeeded: She got him to apologise.
適合表達說服、合作和解決問題 日常生活中，我們經常需要別人幫忙、改變決定或完成工作。這個句型可以用來描述這些實際情 況。 因此，它很適合用於日常對話、學校、工作和顧客服務情境。
It is useful for describing persuasion, cooperation, practical help and problem-solving in daily life, school, work and customer service.
get a customer to try something
get a company to give a refund
get a landlord to repair something
可以代替較長的解釋 （我與湯姆談了幾次。最後，他同意加入我們的團隊。） （我成功說服湯姆加入我們的團隊。） 這個句型能把「提出要求、進行說服和成功產生結果」濃縮在一個完整句子中。

It can replace a longer explanation. I spoke to Tom several times. Finally, he agreed to join our team becomes I got Tom to join our team. The structure compresses the request, persuasion and successful result into one complete sentence.
I spoke to Tom several times. Finally, he agreed to join our team.
I got Tom to join our team.
不只可以用於人，也可以用於物件 這個句型亦可以表示設法令機器或物件正常運作。 （技術員令打印機重新運作。） 這種用法在描述科技問題、維修和日常困難時非常實用。

It can refer not only to people but also to making a machine or object work: The technician got the printer to work again. This use is especially useful for technology problems, repairs and everyday difficulties.
The technician got the printer to work again.
受詞是執行動作的人或事物 （老師讓學生練習。） 實際進行練習的是 the students，不是 the teacher。
The object is the person or thing that performs the action. In The teacher got the students to practise, the students—not the teacher—do the practising.
The teacher got the students to practise.
Get 必須按照時態改變 （我通常會叫弟弟幫助我。） （我昨天叫弟弟幫助我。） （我明天會叫弟弟幫助我。）
Change get to match the tense: get/gets in the present, got in the past, will get in the future, can/should/could get after a modal, and forms such as is trying to get in a continuous construction.
Modal verb：can get / should get / could get
I usually get my brother to help me.
I got my brother to help me yesterday.
I will get my brother to help me tomorrow.
To 後面使用動詞原形 在這個句型中，to 不可以省略。
Use the base form after to, and do not omit to in this pattern: She got him to apologise, not She got him to apologised or She got him apologise.
人稱代名詞必須使用受詞形式 （老師讓我們留下來。）
Use the object form of a personal pronoun: me, him, her, us or them. Write The teacher got us to stay behind, not got we to stay behind.
The teacher got us to stay behind.
The teacher got we to stay behind.
否定形式 （教練說服球員不要太早復操。） 否定的是受詞所做的動作，而不是 get。
For a negative action, use get + object + not to + base verb, as in The coach got the player not to return too soon. The negative applies to the action performed by the object, not to get.
Subject + get + object + not to + base verb
The coach got the player not to return too soon.
Get someone to do 與 make someone do 不同 Get + object + to + verb 通常表示說服、鼓勵、安排或設法促成某件事。 （她說服他道歉。） Make + object + verb 通常帶有較強的強迫意味，而且不使用 to。 （她迫使他道歉。）

Get someone to do differs from make someone do. Get + object + to + verb normally means persuade, encourage, arrange or manage to bring about an action: She got him to apologise. Make + object + verb has a stronger sense of compulsion and takes no to: She made him apologise.
不要與 get to + verb 混淆 本課目標句型 （老師說服學生參加旅行。） 在 get 和 to 之間有受詞 the students。 另一個不同句型 （學生可能有機會享受一次長洲之旅。） 這裏的 get to enjoy 表示「有機會享受」或「得以享受」。get 和 to 之間沒有受詞，因此不屬於本課 的目標句型。

Do not confuse get + object + to + verb with get to + verb. In The teacher got the students to join the trip, the object the students appears between get and to, so this is the target causative pattern. In The students may get to enjoy a trip to Cheung Chau, get to enjoy means “have the opportunity to enjoy”; there is no object between get and to, so it is a different structure.
The teacher got the students to join the trip.

How it differs from “Try as ... might” 與「Try as ... might」的分別 Be that as it may 是固定連接語，意思是「那也許是真的；即便如此……」。它回應前面整個觀點，並不表 示努力。 Try as he might, ... 的意思是「無論他怎樣努力……」，描述某人的努力：原形動詞 + as + 主語 + might, + 結果句。 比較：計劃成本很高。即便如此，我們仍必須繼續。／無論他怎樣努力，他都無法清楚解釋那個錯誤。

How it differs from “Try as ... might” Be that as it may is a fixed linking phrase meaning “That may be true; even so ...”. It reacts to a whole previous point and does not describe effort. Be that as it may Try as he might, ... means “No matter how hard he tried, ...”. It is a concessive clause about a person's effort: base verb + as + subject + might, + result clause. Try as he might, ... Compare: The plan is costly. Be that as it may, we must continue. / Try as he might, he could not explain the mistake clearly.

Of 後面須使用名詞或名詞詞組，不能直接接完整句子。 錯誤：In case of it rains, stay indoors. 正確：In case of rain, stay indoors.

Using On condition that for a firm requirement
Main clause + on condition that + subject + verb + other information
On condition that + subject + verb + other information, + main clause
The funds will be released on condition that the results are made public.
資金將在結果公開的條件下發放。
清楚表達必要條件 這個句型能讓對方立即明白：相關條件不是普通建議，而是必須遵守的要求。 （禮堂可以使用，條件是緊急出口保持暢通。）

It makes a necessary condition or firm requirement clear. The listener immediately understands that the condition is not merely advice but a requirement that must be met: The hall may be used on condition that the emergency exits remain clear.
The hall may be used on condition that the emergency exits remain clear.
適合表達許可和協議 當你准許別人做某事，但同時需要對方遵守規則時，這個句型非常實用。 （你可以借用我的手提電腦，條件是你今晚歸還。）

It is useful for permission and agreements. When allowing someone to do something while requiring compliance with a rule, use a sentence such as You may borrow my laptop on condition that you return it tonight.
You may borrow my laptop on condition that you return it tonight.
把安排和條件連接起來 你可以把一項安排和它的必要條件放在同一句內，不需要使用兩句分開說明。

It connects an arrangement and its condition Without the target structure: The company will offer flexible hours. Employees must complete their weekly duties. Using the target structure: The company will offer flexible hours on condition that employees complete their weekly duties.
The company will offer flexible hours. Employees must complete their weekly duties.
The company will offer flexible hours on condition that employees complete their weekly duties.
讓正式寫作更加準確 這個句型常見於規則、通知、商業協議、政策、報告和正式電郵，能清楚說明一項安排成立的前 提。
It makes formal writing more precise. The structure is common in rules, notices, business agreements, policies, reports and formal emails, where it clearly states the prerequisite for an arrangement.
可以突出重要條件 把 On condition that... 放在句首，可以先讓讀者注意最重要的要求。 （在每名參加者都簽署表格的條件下，活動將會進行。）

It allows you to emphasise an important condition. Placing On condition that ... first makes the reader notice the requirement before the arrangement: On condition that every participant signs the form, the activity will proceed.
On condition that every participant signs the form, the activity will proceed.
That 後面必須接完整子句 On condition that 後面通常需要有主語和動詞。 （你可以進入，條件是你出示門票。）
That must be followed by a complete clause, normally with a subject and verb: You may enter on condition that you show your ticket, not on condition that your ticket.
You may enter on condition that you show your ticket.
You may enter on condition that your ticket.
條件可以放在主句之前或之後 條件放在後面時，前面通常不需要逗號： 條件放在句首時，條件子句後面要加逗號：
The condition can come before or after the main clause. When it follows the main clause, a comma is normally unnecessary. When it comes first, place a comma after the condition clause.
You may borrow the camera on condition that you handle it carefully.
On condition that you handle it carefully, you may borrow the camera.
表達將來條件時，條件子句通常使用現在式 即使主句使用 will，on condition that 後面通常使用現在式，而不是 will。
For a future condition, normally use the present tense in the condition clause. Even if the main clause uses will, on condition that is normally followed by a present form, not will.
The event will proceed on condition that the weather remains safe.
The event will proceed on condition that the weather will remain safe.
可以表達否定條件 在條件子句的動詞前加入 not，便可以說明某件事不可以發生。 （你可以使用房間，條件是你不發出任何聲響。）
A negative condition is possible. Put not before the verb in the condition clause to state what must not happen: You may use the room on condition that you do not make any noise.
You may use the room on condition that you do not make any noise.
兩部分的主語可以不同 主句和條件子句不必由同一個人執行。 主句主語：the landlord 條件子句主語：the tenant

The two clauses may have different subjects; the same person need not perform both actions. In The landlord will allow a pet on condition that the tenant keeps the flat clean, the main-clause subject is the landlord and the condition-clause subject is the tenant.
The landlord will allow a pet on condition that the tenant keeps the flat clean.

On condition that 比普通 if 更強、更正式 If 可以表達一般條件： On condition that 表示較明確、較嚴格的要求，常用於許可、協議、政策、交易或正式安排： Provided that 和 providing that 與它意思相近；as long as 通常較適合日常會話。 On the condition that 也是正確形式，但本練習統一使用 on condition that。

On condition that is stronger and more formal than ordinary if. If can state a general condition, whereas on condition that expresses a clear, strict requirement and is common in permissions, agreements, policies, transactions and formal arrangements. Provided that and providing that have similar meanings; as long as is usually more conversational. On the condition that is also grammatical, but this exercise consistently uses on condition that.

You may use the equipment on condition that you follow the safety rules.

This is why / That is why
Using This is why / That is why to connect reason and result
Reason or situation. This is why + subject + verb + result
Earlier or previously mentioned reason. That is why + subject + verb + result
People need clear leadership. This is why communication matters so much.
人們需要清晰的領導。這就是為甚麼溝通如此重要。
The team lacked trust. That is why the project moved slowly.
團隊缺乏信任。那就是為甚麼項目進展緩慢。
清楚顯示原因與結果 這個句型把原因和結果分成兩個清楚步驟，讀者能立即明白兩者的關係。 （路面結冰。那就是為甚麼司機減速。）
It makes cause and result very clear by presenting them in two distinct steps, so the reader immediately understands their relationship: The road was icy. That is why the driver slowed down.
The road was icy. That is why the driver slowed down.
幫助你有條理地解釋事情 你可以先完整交代背景，再說明結果。即使原因比較長，句子仍然容易理解。
It helps you organise an explanation. You can present the full background first and then state the result, so the explanation remains easy to follow even when the reason is long.
突出事情產生的結果 This is why 和 That is why 會提醒讀者：「接下來就是前面情況所造成的結果。」
It gives extra attention to the result. This is why and That is why signal to the reader that the next information is the consequence of the preceding situation.
避免反覆使用 because 和 so 兩句意思相近，但第二種寫法能改變句子的組織方式，令說話和寫作不會過分重複。
It gives you an alternative to because and so Compare: The team moved slowly because it lacked trust. The team lacked trust. That is why it moved slowly.
The team moved slowly because it lacked trust.
The team lacked trust. That is why it moved slowly.
適合口語、作文和簡報 當你需要解釋決定、問題、行為或結果時，這個句型能提供一個容易掌握的表達框架。
It is useful in speaking, essays and presentations. When explaining a decision, problem, behaviour or result, the pattern provides an easy-to-use organisational frame.
原因放在前面，結果放在後面 第一句先交代原因或情況，第二句才使用 This is why 或 That is why 引出結果。 （道路水浸。那就是為甚麼巴士停止行駛。）

Place the reason first and the result second. The first sentence states the cause or situation; the second uses This is why or That is why to introduce the result: The roads were flooded. That is why the buses stopped running.
The roads were flooded. That is why the buses stopped running.
why 後面必須接完整句子 This is why / That is why 後面應接「主語＋動詞」。
Why must be followed by a complete clause with a subject and verb. Write This is why the shop is closed, not This is why the shop's closure.
This is why the shop is closed.
This is why the shop’s closure.
This 和 That 的分別 This is why 通常指向剛剛提出、與目前情況較接近的原因。 （房間需要更多光線。這就是為甚麼我們正在拉開窗簾。） That is why 通常回指較早發生或已經提及的事情。 （火車誤點。那就是為甚麼里奧遲到了。） 在很多日常情況中，兩者都可以成立；以上分別主要反映說話者如何看待前面的原因。

Choose This or That according to the reference. This is why normally points to a reason just mentioned or felt to be close to the current situation: The room needs more light. This is why we are opening the curtains. That is why normally refers back to something earlier or already mentioned: The train was delayed. That is why Leo arrived late. In many everyday contexts either is possible; the distinction mainly reflects how the speaker views the preceding reason.
The room needs more light. This is why we are opening the curtains.
The train was delayed. That is why Leo arrived late.
不要在 why 後面再加 because
Do not add because after why. Write The road was closed. This is why we took another route, not This is why because the road was closed.
This is why because the road was closed.
The road was closed. This is why we took another route.

「While you're at it」表達「既然都在做了，就順便……」
Context sentence. + While you're at it, + related request / suggestion / command
You are printing the class notes. While you're at it, print an extra copy for me.
你正在列印課堂筆記。既然你都在列印了，順便幫我多印一份吧。
本課練習目標句型：Context sentence. + While you're at it, + related request / suggestion / command。
聽者會立即明白第二項要求與正在進行的事情有關。
It makes the connection clear. The listener immediately understands that the second request belongs to the task already happening.
「it」會指回第一項工作，因此你不需要把同一件事完整重複一次。
It avoids repeating the whole first action. The word “it” points back to the first task, so you do not need to explain that task again.
英語使用者常用這個句型加上一項實際的小要求，令對話不會顯得生硬。
It sounds natural in everyday conversation. Fluent speakers often use it to add one small, practical request without making the conversation feel stiff.
當兩件事可以在同一地點、同一趟路程或使用同一工具完成時，這個句型非常實用。
It helps combine tasks efficiently. It is useful when two actions can be done in the same place, during the same trip or with the same tool.

片語後面可以配合 could you、please、直接指示或 don't forget to，按情況調整語氣。 Compare 比較 Longer / 較長 You're going to the printer. Since you're going to the （你正要去打印機那邊。既然你要去打印機那邊，可以幫 我打印一份嗎？） Target / 目標 You're going to the printer. While you're at it, could （你正要去打印機那邊。既然你都要去了，可以順便幫我 打印一份嗎？）

It lets you control the level of politeness. After the phrase, you can use “could you”, “please”, a direct instruction or “don't forget to”, depending on the situation. Compare: Longer: You're going to the printer. Since you're going to the printer, could you print one for me? Target: You're going to the printer. While you're at it, could you print one for me?
「it」必須有清楚所指。聽者要知道它代表前面哪一項工作。
Give “it” a clear meaning. The listener must know which first task “it” refers to.
第二項工作要有關連，例如在同一地點、同一趟路程、使用同一工具或屬於同一項工作。
Keep the second task related. The extra action should fit the same place, trip, tool or job.
這個片語後面要加逗號：While you're at it, ...
Use a comma after the phrase. Write: “While you're at it, ...”
本練習使用縮寫形式 you're。完整形式 you are 也正確，但縮寫在日常對話中較自然。
Use “you're” in this worksheet. “You are” is also grammatical, but the contraction sounds more natural in conversation.

「The trouble ／ problem ／ issue with ... is that ...」指出問題所在
Using “The trouble / problem / issue with ... is that ...”
The trouble / problem / issue with + noun / noun phrase / V-ing + is / was that + complete clause
The trouble with simple slogans is that they hide complex realities.
簡單口號的問題在於，它們掩蓋了複雜的現實。
本課練習目標句型：The trouble / problem / issue with + noun / noun phrase / V-ing + is / was that + complete clause。
清楚指出問題究竟在哪裏 你不只是籠統地說某件事「不好」，而是能清楚說明它的具體缺點。 （時間表很差。） （時間表的問題在於，兩堂課在同一時間進行。）

It identifies exactly where the problem lies. Instead of saying vaguely that something is “bad”, you can state its specific weakness. Less clear: The timetable is bad. Clearer: The problem with the timetable is that two lessons take place at the same time.
把事物和問題原因連接起來 這個句型先提出要討論的事物，再用 that 說明問題，因此讀者很容易掌握兩者的關係。 （網站的問題在於，文字很難閱讀。）

It connects a thing with the cause of its problem. The structure first introduces the thing being discussed and then uses that to explain the problem, making the relationship easy to follow. Example: The issue with the website is that the text is difficult to read.
幫助你作出有理據的評價 在作文、討論、會議或簡報中，只說一個計劃「不好」並不足夠。這個句型能幫助你進一步解釋理 由。 （建議書的問題在於，它沒有解釋項目將如何獲得資金。）

It helps you make a reasoned evaluation. In an essay, discussion, meeting or presentation, merely calling a plan “bad” is not enough; this structure helps you explain why. Example: The problem with the proposal is that it does not explain how the project will be funded.
令批評較客觀，減少針對個人的感覺 你可以把焦點放在制度、做法或安排上，而不是直接責怪某個人。 （你把會議安排得很差。） （會議時間的問題在於，幾名團隊成員都未能出席。）

It makes criticism more objective and less personal by focusing on a system, practice or arrangement instead of directly blaming someone. Direct and personal: You planned the meeting badly. More objective: The issue with the meeting time is that several team members are unavailable.
讓你按照情況調整語氣 你可以使用 trouble 表達實際困難，使用 problem 作一般評論，或使用較溫和、正式的 issue 因此，這個句型適合用於： ● 日常對話； ● 英文作文； ● 問題分析； ● 工作會議； ● 報告及簡報； ● 產品或服務評價。

It lets you adjust the tone to the situation. Use trouble for a practical difficulty, problem for a general criticism, or the milder, more formal issue. This makes the structure suitable for daily conversation, essays, problem analysis, workplace meetings, reports, presentations, and evaluations of products or services.
with 後面接名詞、名詞詞組或 -ing 形式 名詞或名詞詞組： （這個計劃的問題在於，它的成本太高。） 動名詞： （不停工作、不作休息的問題在於，你會感到疲倦。） with 後面不能直接放一個完整句子。

Use a noun, noun phrase or -ing form after with. Noun or noun phrase: The problem with this plan is that it costs too much. Gerund: The problem with working without a break is that you become tired. Do not put a complete clause directly after with. Incorrect: The problem with people work too long is that they become tired. Correct: The problem with people working too long is that they become tired.
The problem with this plan is that it costs too much.
The problem with working without a break is that you become tired.
Incorrect: The problem with people work too long is that they become tired.
Correct: The problem with people working too long is that they become tired.
that 後面必須是完整句子 that 後面通常要有主語和動詞。 ● Subject 主語：two lessons ● Verb 動詞：happen

Use a complete clause after that. The clause normally needs a subject and a verb. In “The issue with the timetable is that two lessons happen at the same time”, two lessons is the subject and happen is the verb.
The issue with the timetable is that two lessons happen at the same time.
使用 is 還是 was 使用 is 表達現在、一般情況或仍然存在的問題。 使用 was 表達過去某個情況中的問題。

Choose is or was according to time. Use is for a present or general situation, or for a problem that still exists: The problem with the machine is that it makes too much noise. Use was for a problem in a past situation: The problem with the old machine was that it made too much noise.
The problem with the machine is that it makes too much noise.
The problem with the old machine was that it made too much noise.
trouble、problem 和 issue 的分別 常用來指出最令人困擾的實際困難，語氣自然，在日常說話中很常見。 意思最普遍、最中性，適合日常說話、作文、討論和報告。 語氣通常較溫和或較正式，常用於學校、工作、制度或技術討論。 三者的意思有時可以重疊。本練習的答案會根據原句用詞提供一個最合適的示範答案。

Distinguish trouble, problem and issue. The trouble with ... often identifies the most troublesome practical difficulty and sounds natural in everyday speech: The trouble with this bag is that it is difficult to carry. The problem with ... is the broadest and most neutral choice for conversation, essays, discussions and reports: The problem with the plan is that it costs too much. The issue with ... is usually milder or more formal and is common in school, workplace, institutional and technical discussions: The issue with the system is that it sometimes loses information. Their meanings can overlap, so the model answers choose the most suitable word for each prompt.
The trouble with this bag is that it is difficult to carry.
The problem with the plan is that it costs too much.
The issue with the system is that it sometimes loses information.

Use the advanced contrast form when correcting a misunderstanding about the problem: The problem with + noun + is not that + clause, but that + clause. Example: The problem with the article is not that it is long, but that its argument is unclear.
The problem with + noun + is not that + clause, but that + clause.
The problem with the article is not that it is long, but that its argument is unclear.
the problem with 和 the problem of 並不完全相同 指出 X 本身有甚麼缺點或困難。 （這個計劃的問題在於，它的成本太高。） 通常把 X 當作一個需要處理的廣泛問題或社會議題。 （政府必須處理空氣污染問題。）

The problem with and the problem of are not identical. The problem with X identifies a defect or difficulty in X itself: The problem with the plan is that it is too expensive. The problem of X usually presents X as a broad problem or social issue that needs to be addressed: Governments must address the problem of air pollution.
The problem with the plan is that it is too expensive.
Governments must address the problem of air pollution.
不要與 have trouble + -ing 混淆 （我難以理解這條問題。） 這裏的 have trouble + -ing 表示「做某事有困難」，不是本課所學的句型。

Do not confuse this structure with have trouble + -ing. In “I have trouble understanding this question”, have trouble + -ing means that someone finds an action difficult; it is not the target structure in this lesson.

本課練習目標句型：The reason why + subject + verb + is that + subject + verb。
這個句型把「發生了甚麼事」和「事情發生的原因」清楚分開，讓讀者更容易理解兩者的關係。
It clearly separates the situation from its cause The first part tells the reader what happened. The second part explains why it happened.
以 The reason why... 開始句子，可以提醒聽者或讀者：接下來的內容將會解釋一個重要原因。
It places attention on the explanation Beginning with The reason why... tells the listener that an important explanation is coming.
在討論、作文、報告和簡報中，這個句型可以幫助你有條理地解釋事情發生的原因。
It helps organise answers and paragraphs This structure is useful when answering questions about causes in discussions, essays, reports and presentations.

It gives you an alternative to repeatedly using because Compare: Many policies fail because they ignore human behaviour. The reason why many policies fail is that they ignore human behaviour. The second sentence presents the problem first and then gives a focused explanation.

It provides a useful speaking frame Once you remember: The reason why _____ is that _____ you can quickly insert your own situation and explanation.
why 後面的部分應說明「甚麼事情需要解釋」。

Put the situation after why The clause after why states the situation that needs to be explained. Correct: The reason why the shop is closed is that it is a public holiday. Incorrect: The reason why is that the shop is closed it is a public holiday.

即使句中有 why，也不需要使用問句語序。

Use normal statement word order after why The clause after why is not a direct question. Correct: The reason why he left early is that he felt unwell. Incorrect: The reason why did he leave early is that he felt unwell.

本課練習目標句型：What matters is ... / What I mean is ... / What surprised me most was ... / What concerns me is ...。
這個句型能立即指出句子中最值得留意的重點，讓讀者不會錯過你的主要訊息。 第二句把焦點更明確地放在「準確性」之上。

It directs attention to the key point This structure immediately tells the listener or reader which part of the message deserves the most attention. Compare: Accuracy is more important than speed. What matters is not speed, but accuracy. The second sentence places stronger focus on accuracy.
當別人可能誤解你的說話時，你可以使用 What I mean is ... 進一步澄清真正意思。 （我不是說這個計劃毫無用處。我的意思是，它需要更充分的準備。）

It helps you explain yourself clearly You can use What I mean is ... when your first statement may be unclear or misunderstood. Example: I am not saying that the plan is useless. What I mean is that it needs more preparation.
這個句型能把主要觀點與背景資料分開，讓讀者清楚知道哪一項才是核心。
It separates the main point from background information Instead of giving several ideas equal importance, the structure shows which idea is central.
使用 What surprised me most was ... 和 What concerns me is ...，可以準確指出究竟哪件事 令你感到驚訝或擔心。
It makes reactions and concerns more precise What surprised me most was ... and What concerns me is ... help you identify the exact fact that caused your reaction.
這些句型能提供不同的句子開頭，避免重複使用相同表達，使說話、作文、報告及簡報更有變化。

It gives you more sentence variety These structures provide an alternative to repeatedly beginning sentences with: ● The important thing is ... ● I mean ... ● I was surprised by ... ● I am worried about ...
雖然這些句子以 What 開始，但它們是陳述句，而不是問句。句末不應使用問號。

「What makes...」表達成因、關鍵因素與定義
What makes + person / thing + adjective / base verb / noun complement + is + key factor
What makes + person / thing + adjective / base verb / noun complement?
What makes a leader effective is not power, but good judgement.
令一位領導者有效的，不是權力，而是良好的判斷力。
本課練習目標句型：What makes + person / thing + adjective / base verb / noun complement + is + key factor。
這個句型能清楚指出，究竟是哪一項因素帶來某個結果。 讀者可以立即知道，令房間舒適的關鍵因素是自然光。
It clearly identifies the key cause This structure tells the listener or reader exactly which factor produces a result. ● What makes the room comfortable is the natural light.
關鍵答案通常放在 is 後面，因此能得到更明顯的強調。 句子的焦點並非只是「計劃成功」，而是成功背後的「周詳準備」。
It places emphasis on the most important factor The key answer normally appears after is, so it receives more attention. ● What makes the plan successful is careful preparation.
not A, but B 能先否定一個常見想法，再指出真正原因。

It helps you make clear comparisons The pattern not A, but B allows you to correct a common misunderstanding and highlight the real reason. ● What makes customers stay loyal is not low prices, but good service.
與其反覆使用 because，你可以使用 What makes... is...，把原因放在句子的焦點位置。

It gives you an alternative to repeated “because” sentences Compare: ● People trust this service because the staff reply quickly. ● What makes people trust this service is that the staff reply quickly. The second sentence focuses more strongly on the reason.
這個句型可以成為現成的表達框架，幫助你分析人物、服務、機構、產品、政策或社會議題。

It provides a useful speaking and writing frame You can use the structure when analysing people, services, organisations, products, policies or social issues. ● What makes a good leader? ● What makes this policy effective? ● What makes people trust an organisation?
在受詞後可以直接使用形容詞，不需要加入 to be。

Use an adjective directly after the object What makes + object + adjective ● What makes the room comfortable? ● What makes the lesson interesting? Do not add to be. ● Incorrect: What makes the room to be comfortable? ● Correct: What makes the room comfortable?
Use an adjective directly after the object
Incorrect: What makes the room to be comfortable?
Correct: What makes the room comfortable?
在 makes + 受詞 後使用原形動詞，不使用 to。

Use the base verb without “to” What makes + object + base verb ● What makes people laugh? ● What makes the machine stop? Do not use to + verb. ● Incorrect: What makes people to laugh? ● Correct: What makes people laugh?
Incorrect: What makes people to laugh?
名詞亦可以用來說明某人或某事物成為甚麼。
A noun complement may also be used What makes + object + noun complement ● What makes her a good teacher? ● What makes this building a landmark?
A noun complement may also be used
What makes her a good teacher?
What makes this building a landmark?
在本課的陳述句中，整個 What makes... 部分視為一個整體，因此使用 is。
Use “is” after the complete What-clause ● What makes the room special is its natural light. ● What makes the programme successful is its simple design.
What makes the room special is its natural light.
What makes the programme successful is its simple design.
在這類問句中，what 本身是主語，因此不需要使用 do 或 does。
Do not add “do” or “does” in questions ● Incorrect: What does make this place special? ● Correct: What makes this place special?
Do not add “do” or “does” in questions
Incorrect: What does make this place special?
Correct: What makes this place special?

本課練習目標句型：Following + noun / noun phrase, + complete main clause。
清楚交代事情的先後次序 這個句型能讓讀者立即知道哪件事先發生，以及之後發生了甚麼。
It makes the order of events clear This structure tells the reader which event happened first and what happened afterwards.
