It can shorten a longer time clause Instead of using a complete clause beginning with after, you can sometimes use a shorter noun phrase. Compare: After the meeting ended, Daniel sent the notes. Following the meeting, Daniel sent the notes.
讓兩件事情自然連接 句首片語先交代背景事件，讓讀者更容易理解接下來發生的事情。
It connects two events smoothly The opening phrase prepares the reader for the event that happened next.
增加句首變化 你不需要每句都以主語或 after 開始，因此作文和報告的句式不會過分重複。
It gives you another way to begin a sentence Instead of repeatedly beginning sentences with the subject or with after, you can begin with Following.
適合報告、新聞及職場寫作 當你描述事件、決定、巡查、會議、公布或正式程序時，這個句型特別實用。
It is useful in reports, news and workplace writing This structure is common when describing events, decisions, inspections, meetings, announcements and official procedures.
Following 在這個句型中表示 after （會議結束後，我們返回辦公室。） 在這個句型中，following 是介詞，意思是「在……之後」。
In this structure, following is a preposition meaning after: Following the meeting, we returned to the office.
Following the meeting, we returned to the office.
Following 後面必須接名詞或名詞片語 如原句使用完整子句，通常需要把事件改成名詞片語：

Following must be followed by a noun or noun phrase. Correct: Following the meeting, we returned to work. Incorrect: Following the meeting ended, we returned to work. If the source has a full clause, usually turn the event into a noun phrase: After the meeting ended → Following the end of the meeting; After the results were announced → Following the announcement of the results.
Correct: Following the meeting, we returned to work.
Incorrect: Following the meeting ended, we returned to work.
After the meeting ended → Following the end of the meeting
After the results were announced → Following the announcement of the results
句首片語後要加逗號 當 Following + 名詞片語 放在句首時，片語後面通常要加逗號。
Put a comma after an opening Following + noun phrase: Following the inspection, the building reopened.
Following the inspection**,** the building reopened.
Following 主要表示先後次序 Following 本身表示「某事之後」，不一定表示前一件事直接造成後一件事。 （會議結束後，丹尼爾發出了筆記。） 這句只清楚說明事情的先後次序。

Following mainly shows sequence. It means that one event happened after another, but it does not necessarily mean the first event caused the second. “Following the meeting, Daniel sent the notes” states the order clearly without claiming causation.
Following the meeting, Daniel sent the notes.
不要使用 following after Following 本身已包含 after 的意思，因此不需要再加入 after。
Do not use following after, because following already contains the meaning of after. Incorrect: Following after the meeting, we returned to work. Correct: Following the meeting, we returned to work.

本課練習目標句型：The instant + subject + verb, + main clause。
這個句型能清楚表示一件事在另一件事發生時立即出現，不會令人誤以為兩件事之間相隔了一 段時間。 （我看到訊息時，打電話給她。） （我一看到訊息，便立即打電話給她。） 第二句更清楚地表示「看到訊息後立即致電」。

It makes the timing extremely clear. This structure shows that one event happened immediately when another occurred, so the reader will not assume there was a gap between them. Compare: When I saw the message, I called her. The instant I saw the message, I called her. The second sentence states more clearly that the call was immediate.
你可以把兩個緊接發生的動作自然地連成一句，不需要寫成兩個零碎的短句。

It connects two actions naturally You can join two closely connected actions in one complete sentence instead of writing two separate sentences. The alarm rang. Noah woke up immediately. → The instant the alarm rang, Noah woke up.
這個句型能把讀者的注意力帶到事情發生的那一刻，令故事、經歷或事件描述更加生動。
It makes stories more vivid The structure draws attention to the exact moment when something changed or happened.
你可以用這個句型說明某件事發生後應立即採取甚麼行動，因此特別適合指示、安排、警告及未 來計劃。 （你一到達便立即致電給我。）
It is useful for instructions and future plans You can use it to tell someone what to do immediately after something happens. Call me the instant you arrive.
除了反覆使用 as soon as，你亦可以使用 the instant，令說話和寫作的句式更多變。
It gives you an alternative to “as soon as” Instead of repeatedly using as soon as, you can use the instant to create more sentence variety.
“The instant” 表示事情立即發生 The instant 的意思接近 as soon as 或 the moment，表示第二件事在第一件事發生時立即出 現。 （門一打開，狗便立即跑了出去。） 它不只是表示兩件事在相近時間發生，而是強調兩者之間幾乎沒有時間間隔。

“The instant” shows that something happens immediately. It is close in meaning to as soon as or the moment and shows that the second event occurs as soon as the first one happens: The instant the door opened, the dog ran outside. It emphasises that there is almost no interval between the two events, not merely that they occur around the same time.

本課練習目標句型：Situation or expected event. In the meantime, + complete clause。
這個句型能清楚說明，在另一件事情完成之前，人們可以做甚麼。
It clearly shows what happens during a wait This structure tells the listener or reader what can happen before another event is completed.
你不只可以說某件事情仍未完成，還可以進一步說明如何善用等待時間。
It connects a delay with a useful action Instead of mentioning only that something is delayed, you can explain how the waiting time can be used.
你不需要反覆使用 while we are waiting for...，也可以直接連接「等待」和「期間進行的事情」。 （維修需要兩小時。在此期間，我們可以吃午餐。）

It can shorten a repeated explanation Instead of repeatedly using while we are waiting for..., you can use In the meantime to connect the ideas more directly. Compare: The repair will take two hours. While we are waiting for the repair to be completed, we can have lunch. The repair will take two hours. In the meantime, we can have lunch.
第一句交代尚待完成的事情，第二句交代等待期間的安排，讓內容更有條理。
It makes a sequence easier to follow The first sentence explains what is pending. The second sentence explains what happens during that period.
你可以在交通、煮食、維修、學習、醫療結果、項目進度和工作安排等情況中使用這個句型。
It is useful in many real situations You can use this structure when discussing travel, cooking, repairs, schoolwork, medical results, projects and workplace arrangements.
前文必須建立一段等待時間 第一句通常表示： ● 某件事情仍未完成； ● 某人仍未回來； ● 某項結果尚未公布； ● 某件事情稍後才會發生。 （技術人員正在維修打印機。在此期間，我們可以使用樓上的打印機。）

The preceding context must establish a waiting period: something is unfinished, someone has not returned, a result has not been announced, or an event will happen later. Example: The technician is repairing the printer. In the meantime, we can use the printer upstairs.

Use a comma after an opening “In the meantime”. Pattern: In the meantime, + complete clause. Correct: In the meantime, we can prepare the documents. Incorrect: In the meantime we can prepare the documents.

後面必須接完整句子 In the meantime 後面通常要有主語和動詞。 正確： 不完整：

Follow “In the meantime” with a complete clause, normally containing a subject and verb. Correct: In the meantime, the students can revise their notes. Incomplete: In the meantime, revising their notes.
In the meantime, the students can revise their notes.
In the meantime, revising their notes.
它不是 then 或 afterwards In the meantime 表示第二件事情在等待期間發生。 Then 和 afterwards 則表示第二件事情在前一件事情完成後才發生。 （蛋糕正在焗製。在此期間，我們可以清洗碗碟。） （蛋糕焗好後，我們便把它吃掉。）

Do not use “In the meantime” as though it meant then or afterwards. “In the meantime” shows that the second action occurs during a waiting period; then and afterwards show that it occurs only after the first action is complete. Compare: The cake is baking. In the meantime, we can wash the dishes. The cake finished baking. Afterwards, we ate it.
The cake is baking. In the meantime, we can wash the dishes.
The cake finished baking. Afterwards, we ate it.
它與 meanwhile 並不完全相同 Meanwhile 可以單純描述兩件同時發生的事情，甚至可以把焦點轉到另一個地方或人物。 In the meantime 通常更強調「在等待某件事情發生或完成的這段空檔」。 本練習只訓練以下形式：

“In the meantime” and meanwhile are not identical. Meanwhile can simply describe simultaneous events or shift attention to another place or person. “In the meantime” more specifically emphasises the available interval while someone waits for an event to happen or finish. 這個句型能讓讀者立即明白，兩件事情正在同時或同一段期間內發生。
It clearly shows that two things are happening during the same period The reader can immediately understand that the two events are taking place at the same time or within the same period.
當兩個部分都包含較多資料時，你可以把它們分成兩個完整句子，使內容更容易理解。 第二個版本把兩項工作分開說明，讓讀者更容易掌握每個團隊正在做甚麼。

It makes detailed information easier to follow Instead of placing two long ideas inside one sentence with while, you can separate them into two complete sentences. Compare: While the marketing team is planning the campaign, the design team is creating promotional materials. The marketing team is planning the campaign. Meanwhile, the design team is creating promotional materials.
你可以把讀者的注意力由一個人物、團隊或地點轉移到另一個，同時保持兩件事情之間的時間關 係。
It helps organise stories, reports and updates You can move the reader’s attention from one person, group or place to another without losing the connection between the events.
Meanwhile 亦可以突出兩種不同甚至相反的情況正在同時發展。
It can highlight a contrast between two developments Meanwhile can show that two different or even opposite situations are developing at the same time.
適當使用 Meanwhile，可以避免反覆使用 while 或 at the same time，令作文、報告、簡報和工作 匯報的句式更有變化。
It gives you an alternative to repeatedly using while or at the same time Using Meanwhile appropriately creates more sentence variety in stories, essays, reports, presentations and workplace updates.
Meanwhile 前後通常都是完整句子 本練習使用以下標準格式： Meanwhile 前面使用句號，而 Meanwhile 後面使用逗號。
Meanwhile normally links two complete sentences. This exercise uses the standard punctuation: Sentence A. Meanwhile, sentence B. Put a full stop before Meanwhile and a comma after it.
兩件事情不必在完全相同的一秒發生 Meanwhile 可以表示： ● 兩個動作正在同時進行； ● 兩項工作在同一段期間內進行； ● 等待某件事情完成期間，另一件事情正在發生。 （圖書館正在翻新。與此同時，讀者可以使用隔壁的自修室。）

The two events need not happen at exactly the same second. Meanwhile can show two actions in progress at once, two tasks taking place within the same period, or another event occurring while people wait for something to finish. Example: The library is being renovated. Meanwhile, readers can use the study room next door.

本課練習目標句型：Subject + will / may / should + verb + in due course。
這個句型能清楚表達事情不會立即發生，但會在完成必要程序後，於適當時候發生。
It clearly means “not now, but at the proper time” This structure tells the reader that something will happen later, after the necessary time or process.
你不需要生硬地叫對方等待，也可以禮貌地讓對方知道事情並未被忘記。 （請等待。我們現在不能回答你。） （你會在適當時候收到答覆。） 第二句較平和，也較適合正式溝通。

It gives polite reassurance. Instead of simply telling someone to wait, you can reassure them that the matter has not been forgotten. Compare: Please wait. We cannot answer you now. You will receive an answer in due course. The second version is calmer and better suited to formal communication.
使用 soon 可能令人以為事情很快便會完成。使用 in due course 則不會作出不必要的快速承 諾。
It avoids making a false promise Using soon may make people expect a quick result. In due course does not promise that the action will happen immediately.
這個片語適合用於公告、報告、商業電郵及行政溝通，能令語氣保持正式和中立。
It is useful in formal writing. The phrase suits notices, reports, business emails and administrative communication, and helps maintain a formal, neutral tone.
你不需要每次都詳細解釋「完成正常程序後，事情便會在適當時候發生」，可以用 in due course 簡潔地表達相同概念。 第二句更加簡潔，但仍保留「按正常程序在適當時候處理」的意思。

It can shorten a longer explanation. Instead of repeatedly explaining that something will happen after the normal steps have been completed, you can use in due course. Compare: We will contact you later, after the usual procedures have been completed and when the time is appropriate. We will contact you in due course. The second sentence is more concise while preserving the idea that the matter will be handled at the proper time through the normal process.
它不表示確實的日期或時間 In due course 表示事情會在適當時候發生，但沒有說明確實是哪一天或多久之後。 （有關決定將會在適當時候公布。） 這句沒有承諾公布日期。

It does not give an exact date or time. In due course says that something will happen at the proper time, but not on which day or after how long. “The decision will be announced in due course” does not promise an announcement date.
The decision will be announced in due course.
它不等於 soon Soon 表示「很快」，但 in due course 不一定表示很快。 （文件很快便會歸還。） （文件會在完成正常程序後，於適當時候歸還。） 第二句沒有承諾事情會迅速完成。

It does not mean soon. Soon means “in a short time”, whereas in due course does not necessarily promise speed. Compare: The documents will be returned soon. The documents will be returned in due course. The second sentence says that the documents will be returned at the proper stage after the normal process, without promising that this will happen quickly.
The documents will be returned soon.
The documents will be returned in due course.
它常用於正式或半正式場合 這個片語常見於： ● 商業電郵； ● 公司通知； ● 政府或學校公告； ● 顧客服務回覆； ● 行政和法律程序； ● 正式書面溝通。 在非常輕鬆的日常對話中，人們較常使用 later、when the time is right 或 when everything is ready。

It is common in formal or semi-formal contexts, including business emails, company notices, government or school announcements, customer-service replies, administrative and legal procedures, and formal writing. In casual conversation, later, when the time is right, or when everything is ready is more common.
它可以放在句末或句首 句末位置最常見： （你會在適當時候收到回覆。） 放在句首時，後面通常加逗號： （在適當時候，你會收到回覆。）

It can come at the end or beginning of a sentence. The end position is most common: You will receive a reply in due course. At the beginning, it is normally followed by a comma: In due course, you will receive a reply.
You will receive a reply in due course.
In due course, you will receive a reply.
它不等於 in time In time 表示「及時、趕得及」，即在太遲之前完成。 （我們及時到達，趕上了會議。） In due course 表示「按照正常進度，在適當時候」。 （會議紀錄會在適當時候派發。）

It does not mean in time. In time means early enough, before it is too late: We arrived in time for the meeting. In due course means at the proper time as the normal process continues: The meeting notes will be distributed in due course.
We arrived in time for the meeting.
The meeting notes will be distributed in due course.
它不等於 due date Due date 是截止日期。 （付款限期是星期五。） （付款會按正常程序在適當時候處理。）

Do not confuse it with due date, which means a deadline. “The payment is due on Friday” gives the deadline; “The payment will be processed in due course” says it will be handled at the appropriate stage of the normal process.
The payment is due on Friday.
The payment will be processed in due course.
不要加入 the。正確：in due course。錯誤：in the due course。
Do not add “the”. Correct: in due course. Incorrect: in the due course.
如有明確限期，應直接說明日期 In due course 適合在確實時間尚未確定，或事情必須先經過正常程序時使用。 如對方需要知道明確期限，應直接說： （我們會在星期五前回覆。） 而不是只說： （我們會在適當時候回覆。）

If there is a definite deadline, state the date directly. Use in due course when the exact time is not yet known or the matter must first go through the normal process. If the other person needs a clear deadline, say “We will reply by Friday” rather than only “We will reply in due course.”
We will reply in due course.

本課練習目標句型：Subject + be + up to something。
可以在不知道全部真相時表達懷疑 有時你看見一些可疑線索，但仍然不知道對方具體在做甚麼。這個句型讓你表達懷疑，而不需要 編造細節。 （孩子們正在收藏一個盒子。他們可能在暗中做些甚麼。）

It lets you express suspicion without knowing the whole truth. When you notice suspicious clues but do not know exactly what someone is doing, the structure expresses the suspicion without inventing details. Example: The children are hiding a box. They may be up to something.
能把較長的說法縮短 不用這個表達時，你可能要說： 使用這個句型後，可以簡化為： 這個版本更短、更自然，也較適合日常對話。

It shortens a longer statement. Instead of “I think they are secretly planning or doing something, but I do not know exactly what it is”, say “I think they are up to something.” The shorter version is more natural in everyday conversation.
可以準確控制說話者的確定程度 你可以配合 must、probably、may、might、could 等字詞，表示不同程度的懷疑。 一定在搞鬼 很可能在暗中行動 可能在暗中做些甚麼 這能避免把一個不確定的猜測說成已經證實的事實。

It lets you control the speaker’s degree of certainty with must, probably, may, might or could: must be up to something (strong deduction); is probably up to something (probable judgement); might be up to something (possibility). This prevents an uncertain suspicion from being presented as a proven fact.
能自然地連接「線索」和「推斷」 這個句型特別適合先描述異常行為，再提出你的判斷。 （學生突然安靜下來。他們一定在搞鬼。） 第一句提供線索，第二句說明你的推斷，令意思容易理解。

It naturally connects a clue with an inference. The structure is especially useful after a description of unusual behaviour: The pupils suddenly became silent. They must be up to something. The first sentence supplies the clue and the second states the inference.
適合製造懸念和故事氣氛 在故事、對話或敘述中，be up to something 可以讓讀者知道某個角色正在秘密行動，但暫時不 透露完整計劃。 （那名男子一直注視後門。他似乎在暗中策劃甚麼。） 這能令故事更有懸念。

It creates suspense and atmosphere. In stories, dialogue and narration, be up to something can show that a character is acting secretly without revealing the full plan: The man kept watching the back door. He seemed to be up to something. Withholding the details makes the story more suspenseful.

She might be up to something. He has been up to something. Incorrect: The children is up to something. She might is up to something.

Something 表示具體行動仍然不清楚 使用這個表達時，說話者通常只看見一些線索，但不知道對方的完整計劃。 （學生把一些顏料藏起來。他們一定在搞鬼。） 說話者懷疑學生正在策劃某件事，但未必知道他們具體打算做甚麼。

Something means that the specific activity is still unknown. The speaker normally sees clues but does not know the full plan. In “The students are hiding some paint. They must be up to something”, the speaker suspects a secret plan without necessarily knowing exactly what the students intend to do.

可以用不同字詞控制懷疑程度 Strong deduction 強烈推斷 Moderate judgement 中等程度判斷 Possibility 可能性 比較： （他們一定在搞鬼。） （他們可能在暗中做些甚麼。） 第一句的確定程度較高。

Use different words to control the degree of suspicion. Strong deduction: must be up to something; is definitely up to something; is clearly up to something. Moderate judgement: is probably up to something; seems to be up to something; appears to be up to something. Possibility: may be up to something; might be up to something; could be up to something. Compare: They must be up to something. They might be up to something. The first sentence expresses greater certainty.

這個表達通常帶有非正式語氣 Be up to something 很常見於： ● 日常對話； ● 故事； ● 電影對白； ● 描述可疑行為； ● 開玩笑地猜測別人在準備驚喜。 在正式報告或嚴肅指控中，這個表達可能不夠具體。正式場合通常應直接說明已知事實。

Be up to something is normally informal. It is common in everyday conversation, stories, film dialogue, descriptions of suspicious behaviour and joking guesses that someone is preparing a surprise. In a formal report or serious accusation, it may be too vague; state the known facts directly instead.
不一定表示嚴重的壞事 這個表達可以表示有人正在做壞事，但亦可以用於較輕鬆或帶玩笑意味的情況。 （我一進去，所有人便停止說話。他們可能正在暗中準備甚麼。） 他們可能正在準備驚喜，而不一定是在做壞事。

The expression does not necessarily suggest serious wrongdoing. It can describe something bad, but it also suits light-hearted or joking situations. “Everyone stopped talking when I entered. They might be up to something” could mean that they are preparing a surprise, not necessarily doing something wrong.

Do not confuse this target meaning with other uses of up to. “What are you up to?” is often a neutral question about what someone is doing. “It is up to you” means that you are responsible for the choice. “The room can hold up to fifty people” means at most fifty. “He is not up to the task” means that he is not capable of handling it. 讓你的看法聽起來有根據 這個句型能表示你的判斷並非純粹來自個人感覺，而是有證據、事實或合理情況支持。 （我認為這些數字可能有錯。） （有充分理由相信這些數字可能有錯。） 第二句更清楚地表示這個判斷有一定根據。

適合提出審慎的判斷 你可以用它表達「相信」、「預期」、「懷疑」或「質疑」，而不需要把事情說成百分之百確定。 （有充分理由懷疑這個帳戶已受到入侵。） 這種說法能保持審慎，避免在證據不足時作出過分肯定的結論。

It suits cautious judgements. You can use it with believing, expecting, suspecting or questioning without claiming absolute certainty: There is good reason to suspect that the account has been compromised. This wording avoids an overly definite conclusion when the evidence is incomplete.
提出建議時不會過分強硬 它可以說明某項行動是合理的，而不是直接命令別人。 較直接： （你必須檢討預算。） 較客觀： （有充分理由檢討預算。） 第二句把焦點放在理由上，因此語氣較客觀。

It makes a suggestion less forceful by presenting an action as reasonable instead of issuing a direct command. More direct: You must review the budget. More objective: There is good reason to review the budget. The second sentence focuses on the grounds for acting.
能把背景和結論清楚連接起來 你可以先提出證據、情況或問題，再說明甚麼行動是合理的。 （鑑於成本上升，有充分理由檢討預算。） 讀者可以立即明白「成本上升」和「檢討預算」之間的關係。

It clearly connects context with a conclusion. State the evidence, situation or problem first and then identify the reasonable action: Given the rising costs, there is good reason to review the budget. The relationship between rising costs and reviewing the budget is immediately clear.

Distinguish the related expressions. A. There is good reason to ... is a complete structure asserting that sufficient grounds exist for an action or belief: There is good reason to be cautious. B. For good reason is an adverbial phrase that comments that a preceding action, attitude or description is justified: She was cautious, and for good reason. The road is considered dangerous, and for good reason. It normally comments on what came before rather than introducing the next action. C. For no good reason means without any valid reason and often criticises an unjustified action: He cancelled the appointment for no good reason. She became angry for no good reason. D. The direct opposite of There is good reason to ... is There is no good reason to ...: There is no good reason to panic. In short: There is good reason to ... means sufficient grounds exist; There is no good reason to ... means they do not; for good reason says an action is justified; for no good reason says it is unjustified.

本課練習目標句型：There is every reason to believe that + complete clause。
表達強烈但審慎的信心 這個句型表示你有充分證據支持自己的判斷，但沒有把事情說成百分之百肯定。因此，它比直接 使用 definitely 或 certainly 更審慎。

It expresses strong but careful confidence. The structure shows that substantial evidence supports the judgement without presenting it as one hundred per cent certain, so it is more cautious than definitely or certainly.
清楚連接證據和結論 你可以先提出證據，再使用這個句型帶出合理結論，讓讀者清楚理解你的判斷從何而來。
It connects evidence with a conclusion. You can present the evidence first and then use this structure to introduce a reasonable conclusion, making the basis of the judgement clear.
比反覆使用 “I think” 更客觀 後者把重點放在證據和理據上，而不是只表達個人感覺。

It sounds more objective than “I think” because it focuses on evidence and reasoning rather than personal feeling. Instead of “I think the treatment is working”, write: There is every reason to believe that the treatment is working.
適合作文、報告和簡報 這個句型可以用來提出有根據的預測、分析研究結果、評估計劃，或根據現有資料作出判斷。
It is useful in essays, reports and presentations for making evidence-based predictions, analysing research findings, evaluating plans, or drawing judgements from available information.
幫助控制說法的肯定程度 這個句型比 may、might 或 perhaps 更有信心，但仍然保留合理的審慎態度。 Comparison 對比例子 （測試結果理想，所以我認為治療正在發揮作用。） （我們有充分理由相信治療正在發揮作用，因為測試結果理想。） 第二句更清楚地把證據和結論連接起來。

It helps control the strength of a claim. It expresses more confidence than may, might or perhaps while retaining reasonable caution. Compare: The test results are positive, so I think the treatment is working. There is every reason to believe that the treatment is working because the test results are positive. The second sentence connects the evidence and conclusion more clearly.
使用 There is，不要使用 There are Reason 是單數名詞，因此必須使用 is。
Use There is, not There are, because reason is singular. Correct: There is every reason to believe that the plan will work. Incorrect: There are every reasons to believe that the plan will work.
Correct: There is every reason to believe that the plan will work.
Incorrect: There are every reasons to believe that the plan will work.
that 後面必須接完整子句 完整子句需要包含主語和動詞。

Follow that with a complete clause containing a subject and verb. Correct: There is every reason to believe that the team will win. Incorrect: There is every reason to believe that the team’s victory.
Correct: There is every reason to believe that the team will win.
Incorrect: There is every reason to believe that the team’s victory.
every reason 並非逐字表示「每一個理由」 在這個固定表達中，every reason 表示「非常充分的理由」或「有力的理據」。
Every reason idiomatically means very strong or compelling grounds, not a literal count of every possible reason.
這個句型表達強烈信心，但不是絕對肯定 它比以下句子更有信心： （有理由相信這個計劃會成功。） 但它沒有以下句子那麼絕對： （這個計劃肯定會成功。）

「It would be wrong to say that ...」禮貌而精確地否定過度概括
Using “It would be wrong to say that ...”
It would be wrong to say that + complete clause
It would be wrong to say that all young people are careless with money.
若說所有年輕人都不懂得小心理財，便不正確。
本課練習目標句型：It would be wrong to say that + complete clause。
這個句型能讓你修正 all、always 和 never 等過度概括的說法，而不需要完全否定整個觀點。
It helps you correct an overgeneralisation This structure allows you to challenge words such as all, always and never without rejecting the whole topic.
與其直接說「你錯了」，這個句型讓你把焦點放在說法本身，避免令人覺得你在批評說話者。 第二種說法較冷靜、客觀，也較容易讓對方接受。

It makes disagreement sound less aggressive. Instead of saying “You are wrong”, you can focus on the statement rather than attacking the speaker. Compare: You are wrong. Not every teenager is irresponsible. It would be wrong to say that every teenager is irresponsible. The second approach is calmer, more objective and easier for another person to accept.
你可以承認某個問題確實存在，同時指出它並不適用於所有人或所有情況。
It helps you express a balanced opinion You can acknowledge that a problem exists while showing that it does not apply to every person or situation.
在作文、討論及簡報中，當你需要分析某項主張、證據、調查、政策或社會問題時，這個句型尤其 實用。
It is useful in essays, discussions and presentations This structure is especially useful when evaluating claims, evidence, surveys, policies and social issues.
這個句型能幫助你控制立場的強度，清楚指出哪一項結論過於武斷，而不是用另一個極端說法反 駁。
It helps you control the strength of your claim Instead of making another extreme statement, you can explain exactly which conclusion goes too far.
記住 It would be wrong to say that… 這個框架後，你在討論中便能迅速組織一個謹慎而有條理 的回應。
It provides a ready-made speaking frame Once you remember “It would be wrong to say that…”, you can organise a careful response quickly during a discussion.
That 後面必須接完整句子 正確： 不完整：
Follow that with a complete clause. Correct: It would be wrong to say that all students dislike homework. Incomplete: It would be wrong to say that all students disliking homework.

Wrong here means inaccurate, unfair, misleading, too general or unsupported, rather than morally wrong.

Would softens the tone. Compare the direct “That statement is wrong” with the more tactful “It would be wrong to say that every employee is satisfied.” The second version still makes a clear judgement, but it frames it as a careful evaluation and therefore suits discussions, meetings, essays and formal analysis better.

The structure often corrects absolute claims. Common absolute words include all, every, always, never, no one, completely, only, everyone and in every case. Example: Not every expensive product is reliable. → It would be wrong to say that every expensive product is reliable.

「It is fair to say that ...」作出合理而審慎的判斷
Using “It is fair to say that ...”
It is fair to say that + complete clause
It is fair to say that the reform has produced mixed results.
可以合理地說，這場改革帶來了好壞參半的結果。
本課練習目標句型：It is fair to say that + complete clause。
讓判斷聽起來更平衡 這個句型能讓你提出明確看法，同時避免顯得過分武斷或自以為是。 你不是說自己的判斷一定正確，而是表示根據目前的資料，這個結論是合理的。

It makes a judgement sound more balanced. You can state a clear view without sounding overly dogmatic or self-important: the wording presents the conclusion as reasonable on the available information, not as unquestionably correct.
幫助你控制說法的強弱 直接陳述有時會令人以為你正在宣稱一件事是絕對事實。 使用 It is fair to say that...，可以清楚表示這是一個有根據的判斷，而不是百分之百確定的事 實。 比較： （這項改革帶來了好壞參半的結果。） （可以合理地說，這項改革帶來了好壞參半的結果。） 第二句的語氣較審慎，也更能容納不同觀點。

It helps control claim strength. A direct statement can sound like an absolute fact, whereas “It is fair to say that ...” marks a well-founded judgement that is not one hundred per cent certain. Compare: The reform has produced mixed results. It is fair to say that the reform has produced mixed results. The second version is more cautious and leaves room for other views.
容易總結多項證據 當你已經列出數據、例子或正反理據後，可以使用這個句型作出整體結論。 例如： 這樣可以把前面的多項資料自然地收束成一個清晰判斷。

It makes it easy to summarise several pieces of evidence. After listing data, examples or arguments on both sides, use the structure for an overall conclusion: Attendance increased, costs fell and customer feedback improved. It is fair to say that the programme was successful. This neatly draws the preceding evidence into one clear judgement.
適合處理好壞參半的情況 很多政策、產品和決定並非完全成功或完全失敗。 這個句型能幫助你作出較有分寸的評價：

It suits mixed outcomes. Many policies, products and decisions are neither wholly successful nor wholly unsuccessful, so the structure supports a measured evaluation: It is fair to say that the policy created new opportunities but also caused practical difficulties.
適合用於作文、報告、簡報和討論 這是一個現成的表達框架，能幫助你： ● 在議論文中提出整體判斷； ● 在報告中總結結果； ● 在簡報中評價表現； ● 在口語討論中表達審慎意見； ● 避免反覆使用 I think 或 In my opinion。

It provides a ready-made frame for essays, reports, presentations and discussions. Use it to give an overall judgement in an argumentative essay, summarise results in a report, evaluate performance in a presentation, express a cautious opinion in discussion, and avoid repeatedly using I think or In my opinion.

Fair here means reasonable, justified and balanced, not equal treatment of every person.
that 後面必須接完整子句 正確： that 後面的部分必須包含主語和動詞： ● the plan = 主語 ● needs = 動詞 錯誤：

The structure moderately softens a judgement. “The policy failed” sounds highly certain. “It is fair to say that the policy failed” still makes a clear judgement but presents it as a reasonable conclusion from the available evidence rather than an indisputable fact.

Use fair, not fairly, because the structure requires the adjective fair rather than the adverb fairly. Correct: It is fair to say that .... Incorrect: It is fairly to say that ....

「I would argue that ...」提出有理據的個人立場
I would argue that + complete clause
I would argue that critical thinking is more important than memorisation.
我認為，批判性思考比死記硬背更重要。
本課練習目標句型：I would argue that + complete clause。
這個句型能顯示你的說法並非一時感覺，而是一個可以用理由支持的立場。
It helps you express a reasoned opinion This structure shows that your statement is not merely a sudden personal feeling. It suggests that you have reasons for your position.
你可以清楚表明立場，同時避免把個人觀點說成絕對事實，令語氣堅定但不過分強硬。
It sounds confident without being too blunt Instead of presenting an opinion as an unquestionable fact, you can state your position firmly while leaving room for discussion.
這個句型適合用來提出作文立場、主要論點、討論題答案或工作上的建議。
It is useful in essays and discussions You can use the structure to introduce: ● a thesis statement; ● a main argument; ● an answer to a discussion question; ● a professional recommendation.
學生經常重複使用 I think。這個句型能提供另一種自然的立場表達方式，令說話和寫作不會過分 重複。
It gives you an alternative to “I think” Learners often repeat I think many times. I would argue that ... gives you another natural way to introduce an opinion.
使用這個句型提出立場後，你可以自然地補充理由、解釋、例子和結果，令整個論述更有組織。 Compare 比較 兩句都表示個人意見，但第二句更清楚地表示：這是一個說話者準備以理由支持的立場。

It makes it easier to develop an argument After using I would argue that ..., you can naturally continue with: ● because; ● one reason is that; ● for example; ● this is because; ● therefore. I think public transport needs more investment. I would argue that public transport needs more investment.

Follow that with a complete clause containing a subject and verb. Correct: I would argue that clear communication is essential. Incorrect: I would argue that clear communication. In the correct clause, clear communication is the subject and is is the verb.
I would argue that clear communication is essential.
I would argue that clear communication.
Would 在這裏通常不是表示將來 在 I would argue that ... 中，would 通常用來令語氣較有分寸，並不是表示「將會爭辯」。 因此，整句通常可自然理解為： ● 我認為…… ● 我會主張…… ● 我的看法是…… 不宜逐字翻譯成「我將會爭辯……」。

Would does not normally express the future in “I would argue that ...”. It makes the tone more measured, so the sentence naturally means “I think ...”, “I would maintain ...” or “My view is ....” Do not translate it literally as a promise that you will argue later.

It clearly marks an idea as your personal impression The listener understands that you are giving your own judgement rather than presenting the statement as an unquestionable fact.

It makes criticism or disagreement less blunt Instead of directly saying that another person is wrong, you can present your concern in a calmer and more respectful way. Compare: Your proposal ignores the main problem. It seems to me that your proposal ignores the main problem.

你可以先交代自己看到、聽到或分析過的資料，再提出結論，令推理過程更容易理解。

「As far as I am concerned, ...」表達個人立場
Using “As far as I am concerned, ...”
As far as I am concerned, + complete clause
As far as I am concerned, respect should never depend on social status.
就我而言，尊重絕不應取決於社會地位。
本課練習目標句型：As far as I am concerned, + complete clause。
清楚標示你的個人立場 這個句型能讓聽者或讀者立即知道，後面的內容是你的個人判斷，而不是你聲稱人人都必須接受 的客觀事實。
It makes your personal position clear. The listener or reader immediately knows that what follows is your judgement, not an objective fact that you claim everyone must accept.
提供一個可直接使用的開場框架 在討論、口試、作文或會議中，你可以先用這個句型整理立場，再補充理由和例子，不必每次從零 開始組織句子。

It gives you a ready-made opening. In a discussion, oral examination, essay or meeting, the frame lets you state and organise your position before adding reasons and examples instead of building every sentence from scratch.
讓立場聽起來堅定而有條理 它適合用來表達原則、建議、選擇和判斷。語氣通常比普通的 I think 更明確，但仍然是在陳述個 人立場。
It helps you sound firm but controlled. The frame suits principles, recommendations, choices and judgements; it is more definite than an ordinary I think while still presenting a personal position.
避免反覆使用 I think 學生在說話和寫作時經常重複使用 I think。這個句型能增加句式變化，令表達不會過於單調。
It gives you an alternative to I think. Learners often repeat I think in speech and writing, so this frame adds sentence variety and prevents a monotonous series of identical openings.
先提出立場，再加入理據 你可以在這個句型後面先說出核心立場，然後使用 because、although、if、when 等結構補充原 因、限制或條件。 （我認為這項規則是公平的。） （就我而言，這項規則是公平的。） 兩句都能表達意見，但第二句更清楚地把整項判斷框定為說話者的個人立場，語氣亦較堅定和完 整。

It helps organise an opinion before the supporting details. State the core position after the frame, then add reasons, limits or conditions with because, although, if or when. Compare: I think the rule is fair. As far as I am concerned, the rule is fair. Both express an opinion, but the second more clearly frames the entire judgement as the speaker’s personal and relatively firm position.
這是一個固定表達 必須使用： 不可寫成：
This is a fixed expression. Use: As far as I am concerned. Do not write: As far as I concern; As far as me concerned; or As far as I am concern.

This frame is normally firmer than I think and suits personal judgements, principles, choices and positions. In a contentious setting, it can carry the emphatic nuance “at least as far as I am concerned, this is how things stand.”

避免把說法講得過分絕對 使用普通的原因句時，讀者有時可能以為你只提出一個原因。 （項目因為周詳規劃而成功。） 加入 in large part 後，你可以清楚表示周詳規劃是主要原因，但可能仍有其他因素。 （項目能夠成功，很大程度上是因為周詳的規劃。）

It helps you avoid making an overly strong claim. An ordinary causal statement may sound as though it gives the only cause: The project succeeded because of careful planning. Adding in large part identifies careful planning as the main cause while leaving room for others: The project succeeded in large part because of careful planning.
清楚說明某個因素有多重要 這個句型不只是指出原因，還能表示該原因佔了相當大的比重。 （這項改善是由恆常練習造成的。） （這項改善很大程度上是由恆常練習造成的。） 第二句更清楚交代恆常練習的重要程度。

It shows how important a factor is, not merely that it is a cause. Compare: The improvement was caused by regular practice. The improvement was caused in large part by regular practice. The second sentence makes the substantial contribution of regular practice clearer.

「Needless to say」表示「不用多說／不言而喻」
Needless to say, public money should be used responsibly.
不用多說，公帑應該以負責任的方式運用。
本課練習目標句型：Needless to say, + complete clause。
能立即表示事情十分明顯 讀者或聽者一看到 Needless to say，便知道接下來的內容是合乎常理、可以預料或大家理應知 道的。 （不用多說，兒童需要一個安全的學習環境。）

It immediately marks a point as obvious. On hearing or reading Needless to say, the audience expects a reasonable, predictable or commonly understood statement: Needless to say, children need a safe place to learn.
能把較長的說法縮短 你不必每次都使用較長的 It is obvious that...。 （顯然，公帑應該以負責任的方式運用。） （不用多說，公帑應該以負責任的方式運用。） 第二句更直接，也更有力。

It shortens a longer expression such as It is obvious that .... Compare: It is obvious that public money should be used responsibly. Needless to say, public money should be used responsibly. The second version is more direct and forceful.
能引出自然或可以預料的結果 當前文已經提供足夠背景時，可以使用這個句型引出讀者早已預料到的結果。 （球隊已有數月沒有練習。不用多說，他們輸掉了比賽。）
It introduces a natural or predictable outcome after the context has supplied enough background: The team had not practised for months. Needless to say, they lost the match.
能避免重複使用 obviously 或 of course 這個句型為你提供另一種表達「顯然」的方法，令說話和寫作不會不斷重複相同的開場方式。
It avoids repeatedly using obviously or of course. The frame provides another way to express obviousness and varies the openings used in speech and writing.
能令論點顯得更有把握 在討論基本責任、常識或合理後果時，這個句型可以令語氣更堅定。 不過，它帶有一定的強調意味，因此不宜在短文中過度使用。
It makes a point sound more confident when discussing basic duties, common sense or reasonable consequences. Because it carries emphasis, however, do not overuse it in a short text.
後面須接完整句子 Needless to say 後面須有主語和動詞。 （不用多說，安全最重要。）
Follow Needless to say with a complete clause containing a subject and verb. Correct: Needless to say, safety comes first. Incorrect: Needless to say, the importance of safety.
Correct: Needless to say, safety comes first.
Incorrect: Needless to say, the importance of safety. ✗
後面通常使用逗號 在本課所學的標準句型中，Needless to say 放在句首，後面加逗號。 （不用多說，大家都很失望。）
Normally put a comma after the opening phrase. In the standard pattern taught here, write: Needless to say, everyone was disappointed.
Needless to say, everyone was disappointed.
本句型通常不加 that 本練習採用最自然和最常見的句式： 不要寫成：
Normally do not add that. This exercise uses the most natural and common form: Needless to say, the plan needs more work. Do not write: Needless to say that the plan needs more work.
Needless to say, the plan needs more work. ✓
Needless to say that the plan needs more work. ✗
只用於明顯或可以預料的事情 不要使用 Needless to say 引出尚未證實、具有爭議或令讀者意外的說法。 （不用多說，駕駛者必須遵守交通燈號。） （除非所有人都已同意，否則這項說法未必是不言而喻的。）

Use the phrase only for something obvious or expected, not for an unproven, controversial or surprising assertion. Natural: Needless to say, drivers must obey traffic lights. Unnatural without prior agreement: Needless to say, this is the only possible solution.
Natural: Needless to say, drivers must obey traffic lights.
Needless to say, this is the only possible solution.
它可以帶有強調語氣 這個句型不只是說「很明顯」，也表示說話者認為這件事是基本常識、合理責任或自然結果。 因此，使用時應避免帶有高高在上或輕視別人意見的語氣。

The phrase can add emphasis. It does more than label something obvious: it can present a point as basic common sense, a reasonable duty or a natural consequence. Use it carefully so that you do not sound condescending or dismissive of other views.

本課練習目標句型：In pursuit of + noun / noun phrase, + complete clause。
它能立即交代行動背後的目標，讓讀者迅速明白「做這件事是為了甚麼」。
It makes the goal immediately clear. The reader can quickly understand what the action is trying to achieve.
它能突出當事人正在有意識地付出努力，而不是隨意或碰巧做某件事。

它能把使用 because、so that 或 with the aim of 的較長解釋濃縮成一個簡潔短語。

It can shorten a longer explanation. Instead of using a full clause with because, so that or with the aim of, you can express the goal in a compact phrase. in pursuit of 的語氣較正式。 它適合用於作文、報告、新聞、政策、演說及商業寫作。日常小事通常直接使用 to + verb 會更 自然。本課集中教授「追求抽象目標」的用法，而不是「追趕某人或某物」的字面意思。

In pursuit of is formal and suits essays, reports, news, policies, speeches and business writing. For small everyday actions, to + verb is normally more natural. This lesson focuses on pursuing abstract goals, not the literal meaning of chasing a person or thing.

本課練習目標句型：One thing + defining clause + is / was + complement。
把讀者的注意力集中在一項重點上 當一個話題包含很多資料時，這個句型能告訴讀者：「以下這一點值得留意。」 讀者會立即知道句子的重點是 the cost of delay。

It focuses the reader on one important point. When a topic contains much information, the frame signals that the next point deserves attention. In “One thing we cannot ignore is the cost of delay”, the reader immediately recognises the cost of delay as the focus.
幫助你逐點組織內容 在作文、報告、會議或口頭回答中，你可以逐一提出不同重點： 這樣能避免把所有資料擠在同一句中，令說明更有條理。

It helps organise information point by point in essays, reports, meetings and spoken answers: One thing we need to consider is the cost. Another thing we need to consider is the time required. This avoids crowding all the information into one sentence.
把兩句短句合併成一句 比較： 改寫為： 第二個版本較緊湊，而且能清楚顯示「需要討論」與「預算」之間的關係。

It combines two short sentences into one. Compare: We need to discuss several matters. The budget is one of them. → One thing we need to discuss is the budget. The second version is tighter and clearly connects what needs discussion with the budget.
讓重點更加準確 中間部分可以說明為甚麼該項事情值得提出： 這不只是說「巴士不足」，而是準確說明這是令居民擔心的事情。

It makes the focus more precise because the middle clause can explain why the point matters: One thing that concerns residents is the lack of late-night buses. This identifies the bus shortage specifically as a concern, not merely as a fact.
避免重複使用 There is 或 It is important 學生經常寫： 你可以改用： 這能增加句式變化，令說話和寫作不會過分重複。

It avoids repeatedly using There is or It is important. Instead of “It is important to remember the deadline”, “It is important to consider the cost” and “It is important to check the details”, write: One thing we should remember is the deadline. One thing we should consider is the cost. One thing we should check is the details. This adds sentence variety.
提供容易使用的口語框架 在說話時，你可以先使用以下框架，再填入自己的內容： 這個框架能幫助你一邊思考，一邊有條理地表達答案。

It provides easy speaking frames: One thing I like about ___ is ___. One thing we need to improve is ___. One thing that concerns me is ___. One thing I learnt from this experience is ___. Fill in the blanks to organise an answer while you think.
中間部分用來限定 one thing 所指的是甚麼 （我們需要討論的一件事，是預算。） 中間的 we need to discuss 說明是哪一件事。
The middle clause defines which one thing is meant. In “One thing we need to discuss is the budget”, we need to discuss identifies the particular thing.
One thing we need to discuss is the budget.
當 thing 是中間子句的受詞時，that 通常可以省略 以下兩句均正確： 在日常英語中，省略 that 的版本較常見。

When thing is the object of the middle clause, that can normally be omitted. Both are correct: One thing that we should remember is the deadline. One thing we should remember is the deadline. The version without that is more common in everyday English.
One thing that we should remember is the deadline.
One thing we should remember is the deadline.
當 thing 是中間子句的主詞時，that 不可省略 正確： 錯誤： 因為是那件事情「令居民擔心」，所以 that 是子句的主詞，不可刪去。

When thing is the subject of the middle clause, that cannot be omitted. Correct: One thing that concerns residents is the lack of buses. Incorrect: One thing concerns residents is the lack of buses. Here, that is the subject of concerns because the thing itself concerns residents.
One thing that concerns residents is the lack of buses.
One thing concerns residents is the lack of buses.
按照時間使用 is 或 was 現在情況： 過去情況：
Choose is or was according to time. Present situation: One thing I enjoy is the flexible schedule. Past situation: One thing I noticed was how quiet the room was.
One thing I enjoy is the flexible schedule.
One thing I noticed was how quiet the room was.
is／was 後面可以接不同內容 名詞或名詞詞組 that 子句 疑問詞子句 行動 當中間部分含有 do 時，後面通常使用原形動詞：

Different complements can follow is or was: a noun or noun phrase, as in “One thing the room lacks is natural light”; a that-clause, as in “One thing we know is that regular sleep improves concentration”; a wh-clause, as in “One thing we need to discuss is how the plan will be funded”; or an action, as in “One thing you can do is ask the teacher for help.” When the middle clause contains do, the complement normally uses the base verb: One thing we should do is reduce waste.
One thing the room lacks is natural light.
One thing we know is that regular sleep improves concentration.
One thing we need to discuss is how the plan will be funded.

這個句型表示某件事情在某個時間或事件發生之前一直沒有發生，直到那一刻才發生。
這個句型能清楚指出，事情究竟到了哪個時間或發生哪件事之後才出現變化。
It makes the timing very clear. This structure clearly identifies the exact time or event that finally caused a change.
把 Not until 放在句首，可以突出事情比預期更遲發生，或經過一段時間後才發生。 比較： The team did not understand the problem until the final meeting. Not until the final meeting did the team understand the problem. 第二句更強調「直到最後一次會議才明白」。
It emphasises a delay. Putting Not until at the beginning draws attention to how late something happened.
讀者會先看到事情一直沒有發生，然後才知道最後出現甚麼結果，因此能增加故事的懸念。
It can create suspense in a story. The reader first learns about the delay and then discovers what finally happened.
這個句型能清楚連接兩件事情，表示第一件事發生後，第二件事才出現。
It connects two events clearly. The structure shows that the first event had to happen before the second event could take place.
你不需要每次都以人物或事物開始句子，也可以先提出最重要的時間或事件，增加句式變化。
It gives you another way to organise a sentence. You can begin with the important time or event instead of always beginning with the person or thing performing the action.
這個句型適合用於故事、報告和較正式的寫作，尤其適合描述發現、延遲的決定、轉捩點和重要 領悟。
It is useful in stories, reports and formal writing, especially for discoveries, delayed decisions, turning points and important realisations.
必須放在句首 一般句： The team did not realise how serious the issue was until the final meeting. 倒裝句： Not until the final meeting did the team realise how serious the issue was.

Place Not until at the beginning. Compare the ordinary sentence “The team did not realise how serious the issue was until the final meeting” with the inverted form “Not until the final meeting did the team realise how serious the issue was.”
主句必須使用倒裝語序 一般語序： the team realised 倒裝語序： did the team realise 正確： Not until Friday did Daniel finish the report. 錯誤： Not until Friday Daniel finished the report.
Use inversion in the main clause: did + subject + base verb. Write “Not until Friday did Daniel finish the report”, not “Not until Friday Daniel finished the report.”
後面必須使用動詞原形 正確： did the team realise did Sarah understand did the bus arrive 錯誤： did the team realised did Sarah understood did the bus arrived
Use the base form after did: did the team realise, did Sarah understand and did the bus arrive, not realised, understood or arrived.
後面的部分不使用倒裝 正確： Not until the rain stopped did the children go outside. 錯誤： Not until did the rain stop the children go outside. 只有主句需要倒裝；until 後面的時間從句保持正常語序。
Do not invert the clause after until. Only the main clause is inverted: “Not until the rain stopped did the children go outside.”
主句不需要再加入 not Not until 本身已經帶有否定意思。 正確： Not until midnight did the bus arrive. 錯誤： Not until midnight did the bus not arrive.
Do not add not to the inverted main clause because Not until already carries the negative meaning. Write “Not until midnight did the bus arrive.”
這個句型表示「直到……才……」 Not until the teacher explained it again did I understand. 這句不是表示「我一直理解」，而是表示老師再次解釋之前，我一直不明白。
The structure means “only when that time or event was reached”. It shows that the action had not happened before that point.

本課只練習過去式 did 倒裝 本課接受： Not until + past time or event + did + subject + base verb 本課不包括： Not until tomorrow will we know the result. Not until recently has the problem become clear. Not until then was he ready. 以上句子可以正確，但使用了其他時態或助動詞，不屬於本課的目標句型。
This lesson practises past-time inversion with did only. Forms with will, has or was may be grammatical, but they are outside this lesson’s target.
本練習不接受以下非倒裝答案 It was not until Friday that Daniel finished the report. Daniel did not finish the report until Friday. 以上句子意思相近，但沒有使用本課要求的 Not until ... did ... 倒裝結構。
Use the required inverted form. Similar non-inverted alternatives such as “It was not until ... that ...” or an ordinary “did not ... until ...” sentence are not accepted in this exercise.

清楚表達「只有達成這個條件才可以」 這個句型能讓讀者立即明白，一件事情不會隨便發生，而是必須先達成某項條件。 Only when the light turns green can drivers move. 這句清楚表示，司機必須等到綠燈亮起才可以前進。
It clearly expresses that something can happen only after a necessary condition has been met.
突出最重要的條件 比較： We can begin only when everyone is ready. Only when everyone is ready can we begin. 第二句把 everyone is ready 放在最前面，讓讀者先注意「所有人都準備好」這項條件。
It highlights the most important condition by placing that condition first.
幫助表達事情發生的先後次序 這個句型很適合說明： ● 先發生甚麼； ● 然後另一件事情才發生。 Only when I read the final email did I understand the problem. 讀者可以清楚看出，我是先閱讀最後一封電郵，之後才明白問題。
It helps show the sequence between an earlier condition and the event that follows.
適合用於規則、警告和指示 你可以使用這個句型清楚說明某件事情在甚麼情況下才可以進行。 Only when the machine has stopped should you open the cover. 這比只寫一個普通時間句更能突出安全條件。
It is useful for rules, warnings and instructions because it foregrounds the condition for safe or permitted action.

讓作文和報告的句子更有變化 學生經常以主詞開始句子： People speak honestly only when they feel safe. Students can improve only when they practise regularly. 使用 Only when 後，可以改變句子開首： Only when people feel safe do they speak honestly. Only when students practise regularly can they improve. 這能避免連續多句都使用相同的主詞開首。
It gives essays and reports more sentence variety by avoiding repeated subject-first openings.
讓重要觀點更有力量 在討論、演講、作文和報告中，這個句型可以用來強調真正需要改變的事情。 Only when everyone follows the rule will the system work properly. 這句把「每個人都遵守規則」表示為系統正常運作的必要條件，因此語氣較有力。
It gives important arguments more force by presenting a condition as essential to the result.

只倒裝主句 Only when 後面的子句保持正常語序。 正確： Only when people feel safe do they speak honestly. 錯誤： Only when do people feel safe, they speak honestly. people feel safe 是 when 子句，因此不需要倒裝。 需要倒裝的是主句： they speak honestly → do they speak honestly
Invert only the main clause. Keep normal statement order in the clause after Only when: “Only when people feel safe do they speak honestly.”
放在句首時，主句才需要倒裝 Only when 放在句尾： People speak honestly only when they feel safe. 這裏不需要倒裝。 Only when 放在句首： Only when people feel safe do they speak honestly. 這裏必須倒裝。
The main clause requires inversion only when Only when is placed at the beginning. No inversion is needed when the Only when phrase comes at the end.
和 did 後面使用原形動詞 does Tom smile did Ben realise do the students understand 不要寫： does Tom smiles did Ben realised do the students understood
Use the base form after do, does and did: does Tom smile, did Ben realise and do the students understand.

選擇正確的助動詞 I、you、we、they 或複數主詞 使用 do： Only when we practise regularly do we improve. He、she、it 或單數主詞 使用 does： Only when Jack feels tired does he rest. 過去發生的事情 使用 did： Only when Jack felt tired did he rest.
Choose the auxiliary to match the subject and tense: do with I/you/we/they and plural subjects, does with a third-person singular subject, and did for the past.
有情態動詞時，不要加入 do、does 或 did 正確： Only when the rain stops can we leave. 錯誤： Only when the rain stops do we can leave. 每個倒裝主句只需要使用原本的情態動詞。
When the main clause already contains a modal verb, move that modal before the subject and do not add do, does or did.

表示必要條件 這個句型並不只是表示兩件事情在同一時間發生。 它表示： 第一項條件必須達成，第二件事情才會發生。 普通時間關係： When the teacher arrived, the students sat down. （老師到達時，學生坐下來。） 必要條件： Only when the teacher arrived did the students sit down. （只有當老師到達時，學生才坐下來。） 第二句表示學生在老師到達前並沒有坐下。
Only when expresses a necessary condition, not merely two events happening at the same time. The condition must be met before the main event can occur.

開首子句後面通常使用逗號 Only when the shop opens, can customers enter. 在正式標準書寫中，更自然的標點是： Only when the shop opens can customers enter. 當開首的 when 子句較長時，可加入逗號以幫助閱讀： Only when every member of the team has checked the final plan, can the manager approve it. 不過，現代英語中也常省略這個逗號。這份練習會採用較流暢的無逗號形式。

A comma is usually omitted after a short opening Only when clause in modern standard English. A comma may help readability after a particularly long opening clause; this exercise uses the smoother form without a comma.
Place Only when at the beginning and use inversion in the main clause.
Preserve the original meaning and tense and follow the supplied first word.
把 Only when 放在句首，並在主句使用倒裝句式改寫以下句子。
保留原句的意思和時態，並按照已提供的第一個字作答。

I can concentrate only when the room is quiet.
我只有在房間安靜時才能集中精神。
Only when the room is quiet can I concentrate.

湯姆只有感到放鬆時才會微笑。

The bus stops only when a passenger presses the button.
只有乘客按下按鈕時，巴士才會停下。
Only when a passenger presses the button does the bus stop.

學生只有在圖書館開放時才可以進入。
Only when the library is open can students go inside.

我爸爸只有在天氣寒冷時才會開暖爐。

諾亞甚麼時候查看訊息？他只有吃完晚飯後才會查看。

直到閱讀最後一封電郵後，我們才發現真相。

Grace saw how serious the problem was only when she read the full report.
只有閱讀完整報告後，格蕾絲才明白問題有多嚴重。
Only when Grace read the full report did she see how serious the problem was.
The village became easy to reach only after the new bridge opened.

Only when the family is ready should we share the news.
The company understood the cause of the delay only after it had checked every delivery record.
只有在核對每項送貨紀錄後，公司才明白延誤的原因。

The public can trust the system only when decisions are explained clearly.
只有當決定得到清楚解釋時，公眾才可以信任這個制度。
Only when decisions are explained clearly can the public trust the system.

只有當每個部門都遵守新規則時，它才會有效。

Only when we have seen results over a longer period can we judge whether the programme has worked.
Only after + event/action + did + subject + base verb + other information
Only after + subject + verb + did + subject + base verb
Only after + V-ing + did + subject + base verb
Only after + noun phrase + did + subject + base verb
Only after the report was published did the public understand the scale of the problem.
只有在報告發表之後，大眾才明白問題的規模。
這個句型表示某件事情必須先發生，另一件事情才發生、才變得可能，或某人才獲得某種理解。
清楚強調事情發生的先後條件 這個句型不只是告訴讀者哪件事情先發生，還清楚表示第一件事情是第二件事情發生前的重要 條件。 Only after the final check did the doctor allow the patient to leave. （只有在完成最後檢查後，醫生才容許病人離開。） 讀者可以立即知道，病人在完成檢查之前不能離開。
It clearly emphasises the earlier event as a condition for what happened later.

把最重要的轉捩點放在句首 使用 Only after 開始句子，可以先把讀者的注意力放在重要的原因、條件或轉捩點上。 普通語序： The company admitted its mistake only after the evidence was published. 倒裝語序： Only after the evidence was published did the company admit its mistake. 第二句更強調「證據公開」是令公司承認錯誤的關鍵。
It puts the most important turning point first and directs attention to the event that caused the change.

讓事件之間的關係更清楚 與其只寫兩個分開的句子，這個句型能把較早和較遲發生的事情連接起來。 The alarm was repaired. The building became quiet. 這兩句只表示兩件事情發生了。 Only after the alarm was repaired did the building become quiet. （只有在警鐘修好後，大樓才回復安靜。） 新句子清楚表達兩件事情之間的關係。
It clarifies the relationship between two events instead of merely listing them as separate facts.
提供另一種句子開頭 學生經常使用： Then… After that… Finally… The company… The students… 使用 Only after 可以改變句子的開頭，令文章不會連續出現相同的主語加動詞結構。
It provides another sentence opening and reduces repetition of Then, After that, Finally or subject-first clauses.
適合強調遲來的理解、發現或行動 這個句型特別適合描述某人經過一件事情後，才： understood something 明白某事 realised something 意識到某事 discovered something 發現某事 recognised a problem 察覺問題 took action 採取行動 changed a decision 改變決定
It is especially useful for delayed understanding, discoveries, recognition, decisions and action.
令正式寫作更有層次 這個句型常見於故事、新聞報道、報告、論說文及較正式的解釋。 它能幫助學生準確表達事件的發展，而不只是把事情逐件列出。 不過，這是一種帶有強調作用的句式，不需要在每一個表示先後次序的句子中使用。
It gives stories, reports, essays and formal explanations a more structured and emphatic style.

倒裝只出現在主句 Only after 後面的部分使用正常語序。 Correct: Only after the report was published did the public understand the problem. （只有在報告發表之後，大眾才明白這個問題。） Incorrect: Only after was the report published did the public understand the problem. ✗ after 後面的子句應該是： the report was published 而不是： was the report published
Use inversion only in the main clause. The clause after Only after keeps normal word order: “the report was published”, not “was the report published”.

主句使用 did + 主語 + 原形動詞 普通語序： The public understood the problem. 倒裝語序： did the public understand the problem 加入 did 後，主要動詞必須使用原形。 Correct: Only after the report was published did the public understand the problem. Incorrect: Only after the report was published did the public understood the problem. ✗
Form the main clause with did + subject + base verb. After did, use understand rather than understood.
放在主語之前 Correct: Only after the rain stopped did the children go outside. Incorrect: Only after the rain stopped the children did go outside. ✗ 倒裝部分必須是： did + the children + go
Place did before the subject: “did the children go”, not “the children did go” in this target inversion.
這套練習集中使用過去式 本課所有答案均使用： Only after … did … 因此，主要動作發生在過去。 如談論現在或將來，可能需要使用 do、does、can、will 等其他助動詞，但這些形式不屬於本課的 主要目標。
This exercise focuses on past-time inversion with Only after ... did .... Other auxiliaries may be required for present or future meanings, but they are outside this lesson.

表示「之前沒有，之後才有」 Only after A did B 的意思不只是： A happened before B. 而是： B did not happen before A. 例如： Only after the teacher gave an example did Olivia understand the question. （只有在老師舉例之後，奧莉花才明白這條問題。） 這句暗示奧莉花在老師舉例之前並不明白。
Only after A did B means that B did not happen before A. It expresses more than ordinary chronological order.
不要把普通的先後次序強行改成這個句型 以下句子只說明兩件事情先後發生： Leo ate dinner and then watched television. （里奧吃過晚餐，然後看電視。） 它不一定表示里奧在吃晚餐之前不能或不會看電視，因此未必適合改成 Only after。 題目必須清楚表達「直到……之後才……」的意思。
Do not force this structure onto an ordinary sequence. Use it only when the prompt clearly means that the later event did not happen until after the earlier event.
Begin with Only after and use an inverted main clause with did.
Preserve the meaning, subject, tense, object, negation and other details; use the base verb after did.
把 Only after 放在句首，並在主句使用 did 倒裝改寫每題。
保留原句意思、主語、時態、受詞、否定意思及其他重要資料；did 後使用原形動詞。
The public did not understand the scale of the problem until after the report was published.
大眾直到報告發表之後，才明白問題的規模。
Only after the report was published did the public understand the scale of the problem.
只有在報告發表之後，大眾才明白問題的規模。

Only after Tom had finished her homework did she relax.
只有在完成家課後，湯姆才放鬆下來。
The lights did not come back on until after the electrician repaired the damaged wire.
電工修好損壞的電線後，燈才重新亮起。
Only after the electrician repaired the damaged wire did the lights come back on.
只有在電工修好損壞的電線後，燈才重新亮起。
We realised that the door was unlocked only after we returned home.
我們回到家後，才發現門沒有上鎖。

只有在回到家後，我們才發現門沒有上鎖。
Leo apologised only after the teacher explained why his comment was hurtful.
老師解釋了里奧的說話為甚麼傷人後，他才道歉。
Only after the teacher explained why his comment was hurtful did Leo apologise.
只有在老師解釋了他的說話為甚麼傷人後，里奧才道歉。
The bus did not start moving until every passenger had boarded.
所有乘客上車後，巴士才開動。
Only after every passenger had boarded did the bus start moving.
只有在所有乘客上車後，巴士才開動。
It was not until the rain stopped that the children went outside.
直到雨停後，孩子們才走到外面。
Only after the rain stopped did the children go outside.
只有在雨停後，孩子們才走到外面。
First, the manager approved the budget. The team did not begin work before that.
經理先批准預算。在此之前，團隊並沒有開始工作。
Only after the manager approved the budget did the team begin work.
只有在經理批准預算後，團隊才開始工作。
The doctor allowed the patient to leave only after completing a final check.
醫生完成最後檢查後，才容許病人離開。
Only after completing a final check did the doctor allow the patient to leave.

「Only by ... can ...」表示只有透過某種方法，才能做到某事
Using “Only by ... can ...” to express a necessary method
Only by + V-ing + can + subject + base verb + other information
Only by listening carefully can we understand what others truly need.
只有透過仔細聆聽，我們才能明白別人真正需要甚麼。
這個句型強調必須採取某個行動或使用某種方法，才能達到後面的結果。
這個句型能清楚強調必要的方法，讓讀者知道：如果不先採取前面的行動，後面的結果便難以達 成。
It clearly emphasises the necessary method. The result cannot normally be achieved without the action mentioned first.
句型前半部分說明必須採取的方法，後半部分則交代完成這個方法後可以達到的結果。
It connects a method and a result: the first part presents what must be done, and the second explains what can then be achieved.
在討論如何解決問題或改善情況時，這個句型能幫助你清楚提出所需行動。 Example: Only by reducing unnecessary waste can the company lower its environmental impact. （只有減少不必要的浪費，公司才能降低對環境的影響。）
It helps you explain solutions and the action required to solve a problem or achieve an improvement.
把 Only by 放在句首，可以立即把讀者的注意力帶到最重要的方法或條件上。
It makes the important method stand out by directing attention to the opening Only by action.
你不需要每句都以 We can 或 People can 開始，而可以先提出方法，令句式更有變化。 Compare: We can understand customers’ needs only by listening to them. Only by listening to customers can we understand their needs.
It gives sentences greater variety instead of repeatedly beginning with “We can ...” or “People can ....”
這個句型特別適合用於討論教育、環境保護、商業、公共政策和解決問題，也適用於作文、報告、 簡報和正式討論。
It is useful in discussions, essays and presentations about education, environmental protection, business, public policy and problem-solving.
是介詞。當後面表示一個行動時，動詞須使用 V-ing 形式。 Correct: Only by practising every day can you improve. Incorrect: Only by practise every day can you improve.
Use V-ing after by because by is a preposition: “Only by practising every day can you improve.”
當 Only by 短語放在句首時，主句必須使用倒裝語序： can + subject + base verb Correct: Only by working together can we solve the problem. Incorrect: Only by working together we can solve the problem.
When the Only by phrase begins the sentence, invert the main clause as can + subject + base verb.
後面的主要動詞必須使用原形。 Correct: Only by asking questions can pupils understand the lesson. Incorrect: Only by asking questions can pupils understands the lesson.
Use the base form after can: “can pupils understand”, not “can pupils understands”.
句中已有情態動詞 can，因此不需要再加入 do、does 或 did。 Correct: Only by checking the figures can we find the mistake. Incorrect: Only by checking the figures do we can find the mistake.
Do not add do, does or did because the modal can already forms the inversion.
當 only by 短語放在句尾時，不使用倒裝： We can improve only by practising regularly. 當 only by 短語移到句首時，才需要倒裝： Only by practising regularly can we improve.
Do not use inversion when the only by phrase remains at the end. Inversion is required when it moves to the beginning.

這個句型帶有「只有這樣做才可以」的強調意思。因此，前面的行動必須是達到結果所需的方法， 而不應只是其中一個普通建議。 Strong and logical: Only by entering the correct password can users open the protected file. Too strong in many situations: Only by drinking tea can people relax. 喝茶可能有助放鬆，但並不是放鬆的唯一方法，因此不適合使用這個句型。
Use the structure only when the method is genuinely necessary, not merely one optional suggestion among many.
通常不要在 can 前面加逗號。正確：Only by listening carefully can we understand the problem. 錯誤：Only by listening carefully, can we understand the problem.
Do not normally place a comma between the opening Only by phrase and can.
後面仍然先放主語，再使用 be + past participle。 Only by maintaining the equipment regularly can many breakdowns be prevented. （只有定期保養設備，才能避免很多故障。）
Passive main clauses are possible: after can and the subject, use be + past participle.
Rewrite each prompt using Only by + V-ing + can + subject + base verb.
Preserve the full original meaning and follow the supplied first word.
使用 Only by + V-ing + can + subject + base verb 改寫每題。

Hardly + had + subject + past participle + when + subject + past simple
Hardly had we sat down when the fire alarm went off.
我們才剛坐下，火警鐘就響了。
這個句型表示第一件事情才剛發生，第二件事情便立即或幾乎立即發生。
清楚表達兩件事情相隔很短時間 這個句型讓讀者立即明白，第二件事情幾乎在第一件事情完成後便發生。
It clearly shows that very little time passed between the two events.
令故事更有節奏 Hardly ... when ... 能突出突然而迅速的轉變，因此特別適合用來敘述故事、意外和令人驚訝的事 情。
It gives stories a stronger rhythm by highlighting a sudden and rapid change.
把兩個短句連接起來 Instead of: We sat down. The fire alarm went off immediately. You can write: Hardly had we sat down when the fire alarm went off. 你可以把兩件緊接發生的事情合併成一句完整句子。
It combines two short events into one complete sentence and makes their immediate relationship clear.
增加句式變化 學生經常使用： ● Then ... ● After that ... ● As soon as ... ● A moment later ... Hardly ... when ... 提供另一種表達方法，避免文章不斷使用相同的句式。
It adds sentence variety alongside expressions such as Then, After that, As soon as and A moment later.
適合故事、作文和較正式的敘述 這個句型可以令故事更生動，也適合在作文、報告或較正式的敘述中強調事情發生得非常快。
It is useful in stories, essays, reports and formal narration when events happen in rapid succession.
放在句首時，必須使用倒裝 正確： Hardly had we sat down when the fire alarm went off. 錯誤： Hardly we had sat down when the fire alarm went off. had 必須放在主語 we 前面。
When Hardly begins the sentence, use inversion by placing had before the subject.
第一件事情使用過去完成式 句式： had + past participle 例如： ● had sat ● had arrived ● had finished ● had gone ● had been opened 第一部分描述先發生的事情。
Use the past perfect, had + past participle, for the first event.
第二件事情通常使用一般過去式 Hardly had the lesson started when the lights went out. ● had started：先發生 ● went out：緊接着發生
Use the past simple for the second event after when.
與 when 配搭 正確： Hardly had I arrived when the meeting began. 錯誤： Hardly had I arrived than the meeting began. Hardly 通常與 when 配搭。
Pair Hardly with when, not than.
已包含「才剛」的意思 不要在第一部分再加入 just。 錯誤： Hardly had I just arrived when the meeting began. 正確： Hardly had I arrived when the meeting began.
Hardly already means that the event had only just happened, so do not add just to the first clause.
不要漏掉 had 錯誤： Hardly I arrived when the meeting began. 正確： Hardly had I arrived when the meeting began.
Do not omit had from the inverted opening.
兩件事情必須非常接近 這個句型不適合描述相隔很久的事件。 不自然： Hardly had Leo moved to London when he bought a house five years later. 第二件事情必須在第一件事情之後立即或很快發生。
The two events must be very close in time; the second should happen immediately or very soon after the first.

No sooner + had + subject + been + past participle + than + subject + past-tense verb
No sooner had the decision been announced than criticism began to spread.
決定一宣布，批評聲音便開始擴散。
這個句型連接兩件過去事件，表示第一件事情剛完成，第二件事情便幾乎立即發生。
這個句型能清楚表示兩件事之間幾乎沒有停頓：第一件事剛完成，第二件事便發生。 No sooner had the door opened than the children ran outside. （門一打開，孩子們便跑到外面。）
It shows that the second event happened immediately and that there was almost no delay between the events.
過去完成時指出先發生的事情，而一般過去時則指出緊接發生的事情，令先後次序一目了然。
It makes the order of events very clear: the past perfect marks the earlier event and the past simple marks what followed.
你不必把兩件事寫成兩個互不相連的事實，而可以在一句之內清楚顯示它們緊接發生的關係。 比較： The announcement was made. Criticism immediately began to spread. No sooner had the announcement been made than criticism began to spread. 第二句把兩件事連接得更緊密。
It links two events closely in one sentence instead of presenting them as unrelated facts.
這個句型特別強調第二件事來得非常快，因此比普通的 after 或 then 更有力量。
It creates stronger emphasis on how quickly the second event followed.
在故事、新聞報道、報告及較正式的文章中，這個句型很適合描述突然的發展、意外反應或接連 發生的事件。
It is useful in stories, reports and formal writing about sudden developments, unexpected reactions and rapid sequences.
除了反覆使用 As soon as 或 After，你也可以使用倒裝句開始句子，令作文的句式更有變化。
It gives you another way to begin a sentence instead of repeatedly using As soon as or After.
放在句首時，必須使用倒裝 正確： No sooner had the meeting begun than the fire alarm rang. 錯誤： No sooner the meeting had begun than the fire alarm rang. had 必須放在主語前面。
When No sooner begins the sentence, use inversion by placing had before the subject.
第一件事使用過去完成時 No sooner 後面的事件先發生，因此使用： had + past participle 例如： ● had arrived ● had finished ● had begun ● had been announced
Use the past perfect, had + past participle, for the first event.
第二件事通常使用一般過去時 than 後面的事件緊接着發生： No sooner had Amy arrived than the meeting started. 第一件事：Amy had arrived 第二件事：the meeting started
Use the past simple for the second event after than.
必須使用 than，而不是 when 正確： No sooner had he sat down than the phone rang. 錯誤： No sooner had he sat down when the phone rang. Hardly 和 scarcely 通常配合 when；no sooner 則配合 than。
Pair No sooner with than, not when. Hardly and scarcely normally pair with when.
適用於所有主語 無論主語是 I、he、they 或 the students，都使用 had： ● No sooner had I arrived than ... ● No sooner had she arrived than ... ● No sooner had they arrived than ... 不可因主語不同而改成 has 或 have。
Use had with every subject; do not change it to has or have.
第一個動詞必須使用過去分詞 正確： No sooner had the lesson begun than ... 錯誤： No sooner had the lesson began than ... begin 的過去分詞是 begun，而一般過去式是 began。
Use a past participle after had, such as begun rather than the past-simple form began.
兩件事必須幾乎緊接發生 這個句型不能只表示兩件事在過去先後發生。它強調兩者之間幾乎沒有時間間隔。 不適合： I finished school in June. I started university three months later. 兩件事相隔三個月，不符合 no sooner 所表達的即時關係。
The events must happen almost immediately one after the other, not merely at different times in the past.
句中通常不需要在 than 前加逗號 No sooner had the show ended than the audience stood up. 整個結構是一個緊密相連的句子，通常不在 than 前使用逗號。
Do not normally place a comma before than because the two parts form one closely connected structure.
Rewrite each sentence using No sooner ... than ... inversion.
Preserve the original meaning and order of events and follow the supplied first word.
使用 No sooner ... than ... 倒裝句改寫每題。
保留原句意思及事件的先後次序，並按照已提供的第一個字作答。

Scarcely + had + subject + past participle + when + subject + past simple
Scarcely + had + subject + past participle + other information + when + subject + past simple + other information
Scarcely had the teacher finished speaking when the students started asking questions.
老師話音剛落，學生就開始發問。
這個句型表示第一件事情剛剛完成，第二件事情便幾乎立即發生。
清楚表達兩件事緊接發生 這個句型能準確表示第一件事剛剛完成，第二件事便立即發生，讓事情的先後次序十分清楚。
It shows that two events happened almost immediately and makes their order clear.

加強速度感或突然感 Scarcely 放在句首，會特別強調第二件事情來得很快，有時甚至令人意外。 Compare： As soon as the teacher finished speaking, the students started asking questions. （老師一說完，學生便開始發問。） Scarcely had the teacher finished speaking when the students started asking questions. （老師話音剛落，學生就開始發問。） 第二句更強調學生幾乎沒有等待，老師剛說完，他們便立即發問。
It adds a sense of speed or surprise by emphasising how quickly the second event occurred.
避免反覆使用 as soon as 學生在描述事情先後發生時，經常只使用 as soon as。掌握這個句型後，可以用另一種方式表達 相同關係，使文章不會過於重複。
It gives you another way to express “as soon as” and reduces repetition.
增加句子開頭的變化 一般句子經常以人物或事物作為主語開始： The meeting had just begun when the alarm sounded. 使用倒裝後，可以用 Scarcely 開始： Scarcely had the meeting begun when the alarm sounded. 這能讓故事和文章的句式更有變化。
It creates a more varied sentence opening by beginning with Scarcely instead of the subject.
適合描述接連發生的事件 這個句型很適合描述： ● 突然收到消息 ● 警報響起 ● 人群作出反應 ● 意外發生 ● 某人剛完成一件事便遇到另一件事 它可以令故事發展更加緊湊。
It is useful for storytelling and for describing sudden messages, alarms, reactions and accidents.
把兩件事情清楚連成一句 不用寫成兩個互不相連的短句： The train stopped. The doors opened immediately. 你可以寫成： Scarcely had the train stopped when the doors opened. 讀者能立即理解兩件事情的時間關係。
It combines two events clearly in one sentence so that their time relationship is immediately understood.

放在句首時，必須使用倒裝語序 普通語序： The teacher had scarcely finished speaking when the students started asking questions. 倒裝語序： Scarcely had the teacher finished speaking when the students started asking questions. 必須把 had 放在主語前面： Scarcely + had + the teacher + finished... 不可寫成： Scarcely the teacher had finished...
When Scarcely begins the sentence, invert the first clause by placing had before the subject.
第一部分使用過去完成時 句型的第一部分是： had + past participle 例如： ● had finished ● had opened ● had left ● had begun ● had been completed
Use the past perfect, had + past participle, in the first clause.
第二部分通常使用過去式 Scarcely had the bell rung when the students left the classroom. ● 第一件事：had rung ● 第二件事：left
Use the past simple in the second clause after when.

與 when 配搭 正確： Scarcely had the meeting begun when the fire alarm sounded. 錯誤： Scarcely had the meeting begun than the fire alarm sounded. 請記住： ● Scarcely ... when ... ● Hardly ... when ... ● No sooner ... than ... 本練習只接受 Scarcely ... when ...。
Pair Scarcely with when. Hardly also pairs with when, whereas No sooner pairs with than.
兩件事情必須幾乎緊接發生 這個句型不能用來描述相隔很久的事情。 自然： Scarcely had I sat down when the phone rang. （我剛坐下，電話便響了。） 不自然： Scarcely had I finished school when I found a job three years later. （我畢業後三年才找到工作。） 三年後並不是「幾乎立即」。
Use the structure only for events that happen almost immediately one after the other, not events separated by a long period.
第一件事情通常先完成 Scarcely had Maya locked the door when she realised that her keys were inside. 先發生： Maya locked the door. 緊接發生： She realised that her keys were inside.
The first event is normally completed just before the second event occurs.
兩部分的主語可以不同 Scarcely had the train stopped when the doors opened. ● 第一部分主語：the train ● 第二部分主語：the doors 兩個主語不需要相同，但事情的先後關係必須清楚。
The two clauses may have different subjects as long as their sequence is clear.
在這裏不是「很少」 Scarcely 有時表示「幾乎不」： I could scarcely hear him. （我幾乎聽不到他說話。） 但在 Scarcely ... when ... 中，它表示： 「剛剛……便……」
In this pattern, Scarcely means “only just ... when ...”, not its separate meaning “hardly” or “almost not”.
這個句型語氣較正式 Scarcely ... when ... 常見於： ● 故事 ● 新聞敘述 ● 正式作文 ● 事件報告 ● 描述突然發生的事情 日常口語通常更常使用 as soon as。
The structure is relatively formal and is common in stories, news narratives, formal essays and incident reports; everyday speech more often uses as soon as.

「Not until then + 倒裝句」表達「直到那時才……」
Previous event + but not until then + auxiliary + subject + main verb
Previous event + but not until then did + subject + base verb
Previous event + but not until then was / were + subject + complement
Previous event + but not until then could + subject + base verb
I had heard the story before, but not until then did I understand its meaning.
我之前聽過這個故事，但直到那時我才明白它的意義。
這個句型表示某件事情在特定時刻之前一直沒有發生，直到前述事件發生後，情況才改變。
這個句型能清楚指出情況在哪一刻出現改變。 The doctor explained the results, but not until then was Sara calm. 讀者會明白，莎拉在醫生解釋結果之前一直未能平靜下來。
It clearly shows a turning point and tells the reader exactly when a situation changed.
第二句把 Not until then 放在較重要的位置，因此更能強調「在此之前一直不明白」。
It gives important information more emphasis by foregrounding the fact that something had not happened before that moment.
第一部分說明先發生的事情，第二部分說明其後才出現的結果，讓讀者更容易掌握事情的先後次 序。
It makes the order of events easier to follow: the first part gives the earlier event, and the second gives what changed afterwards.
你可以用這個句型描述發現真相、突然明白、情緒轉變、問題變得清楚，或某件事情終於變得可 行。
It is useful in stories for discoveries, sudden understanding, changes in feeling, newly clear problems and actions that finally become possible.
這個句型提供另一種組織句子的方法，避免不斷重複使用相同的 until 句式。
It gives you another way to organise a sentence instead of repeatedly using an ordinary did not ... until ... pattern.
這個句型適合用於反思文章，說明某段經歷如何令你產生新的理解。 I had seen the problem many times, but not until then did I understand its cause. （我以前曾多次看見這個問題，但直到那時我才明白它的成因。）
It can make reflective writing more effective when explaining how an experience changed your understanding.
後面要使用倒裝語序 普通語序： I understood the rule. 倒裝語序： Not until then did I understand the rule. 助動詞 did 要放在主語 I 前面。
Use inversion after not until then by placing the auxiliary before the subject: “Not until then did I understand the rule.”

一般過去式要使用 did + 主語 + 原形動詞 正確： Not until then did I understand the rule. 錯誤： Not until then I understood the rule. 錯誤： Not until then did I understood the rule. did 已經表示過去時間，因此後面的動詞必須使用原形： did I understand 不是： did I understood
For the past simple, use did + subject + base verb. Because did already marks past time, write did I understand, not did I understood.
使用 be 時，不需要加入 did 普通語序： Sara was calm. 倒裝語序： Not until then was Sara calm. 普通語序： The rooms were ready. 倒裝語序： Not until then were the rooms ready.
With the verb be, invert was or were directly and do not add did: “Not until then was Sara calm.”
使用 could 等情態動詞時，把情態動詞放在主語前面 普通語序： We could see the town. 倒裝語序： Not until then could we see the town. could 後面的動詞使用原形： could we see
With a modal such as could, place the modal before the subject and use the base verb after it.
必須清楚指向前面的一件事情或一個時刻 清楚： The teacher explained the rule again, but not until then did I understand it. then 指的是「老師再次解釋規則的時候」。 不清楚： Not until then did I understand it. 如果前文沒有說明發生了甚麼，讀者便不知道 then 指哪個時刻。
Then must refer clearly to an event or moment mentioned earlier; without that context, the reader cannot know which time then means.

Using “one” as a generic personal pronoun
One + singular verb / modal verb + other information
When / If / Before / After / Although + one + singular verb + main clause
In an unfamiliar situation, one should remain calm and ask questions.
在陌生的情況下，人應該保持冷靜並提出問題。
One 可以泛指任何人或一般人，適合用來表達普遍原則、建議、觀察和意見，而不直接以 you 稱呼讀者。
可以用來說明任何人都可能遇到的情況，或一般人應該採取的做法。句子的意思不只限於某 一個人。
It helps you express a general principle that applies to any person rather than one named individual.

使用 you 有時會令人覺得你正在直接指示讀者。使用 one 則可以把相同意思表達成普遍的觀察 或原則。 Compare: You should check your sources before publishing a claim. （你在發表說法前，應該核實自己的資料來源。） One should check one’s sources before publishing a claim. （人在發表說法前，應該核實自己的資料來源。） The first sentence speaks directly to the reader. The second presents a general rule. 第一句直接向讀者說話；第二句則提出一項普遍原則。
It avoids speaking directly to the reader and presents advice as a general observation or principle.
在作文、報告和正式解釋中，如需討論行為、責任、決定或共同經歷，one 十分實用。
It is useful in formal discussion about behaviour, responsibility, decisions and common experiences.
和 oneself 可以清楚表示相關物件或動作屬於同一個由 one 所代表的人。 One should accept responsibility for one’s decisions. （人應該為自己的決定承擔責任。） One should give oneself time to improve. （人應該給自己時間進步。）
One’s and oneself keep the reference clear by linking possession or reflexive action to the same generic person.
如果多個句子都以 People 或 You 開始，你有時可以使用 one，令句式更有變化。
It gives you an alternative to repeated uses of people and you and creates controlled sentence variety.
可以出現在句首、時間或條件子句內、that 之後，或作為動詞及介詞的受詞。這種靈活性有 助你以不同方式組織正式句子。
It can appear in several parts of a sentence, helping you organise formal writing in different ways.
One 後面使用單數動詞。應使用：one is、one has、one does、one needs、one thinks。不要使用：one are、one have、one do、one need、one think。
One takes a singular verb: one is, one has, one does, one needs and one thinks.

Keep pronouns consistent: use one, one’s and oneself throughout a reference instead of switching to your or their.
One 的語氣較正式。泛指的 one 特別適合用於作文、報告、正式建議、學術討論、一般原則及經過仔細撰寫的論點。日常對話通常使用泛指的 you 較自然：You never know what will happen。使用 one 的版本較正式：One never knows what will happen。One 並不一定比 you 更好，應按情境和語氣選擇。

Generic one is relatively formal and is especially useful in essays, reports, formal advice, academic discussion and carefully written arguments. Generic you is often more natural in ordinary conversation.

「Little did someone know that ...」表示當時完全不知道
Little + did + person + know + that + complete clause
Little did he know that his small decision would change the entire project.
他當時完全不知道，他那個小決定會改變整個項目。
這個句型表示某人在當時完全不知道一項重要、意外或後來才發現的事實，常用來製造懸念和轉折。
讓故事更有懸念 這個句型告訴讀者，人物當時並不知道一件重要的事。 讀者會想繼續了解事情後來如何發展。 Little did Sara know that someone was waiting for her outside.
It creates suspense by revealing that a character did not know an important fact at the time.
清楚表達「當時不知道，後來才知道」 它可以把兩個時間角度放在同一句中： ● 人物在過去並不知道； ● 說故事的人現在知道後來的結果。 這樣能令事件的先後關係更清楚。
It clearly contrasts what the character knew then with what the narrator later knows.
強調事情出乎意料 He did not know... 只是普通地說某人不知道。 Little did he know... 則強調後來的結果完全超出他的預期。
It emphasises that the later result was unexpected, more strongly than an ordinary “did not know” sentence.
讓句子有不同的開頭 學生經常以人物主語開始句子： He... She... Tom... The students... 以 Little 開始句子，可以增加句式變化，避免每句都使用相同開頭。
It gives sentences a different opening and avoids repeatedly beginning with a person’s name or pronoun.
可以代替較長的解釋 較長說法： At that time, she had no idea about what would happen later. 目標句型： Little did she know what would happen later. 第二句更集中，也更有故事感。
It can replace a longer explanation such as “At that time, she had no idea what would happen later.”
適合故事、演講和個人經歷 這個句型特別適合： ● 故事寫作； ● 個人經歷； ● 小說或電影簡介； ● 口頭講故事； ● 描述意外結果； ● 引出重要轉折。
It is useful in stories, speeches, personal experiences, film or novel summaries and descriptions of unexpected turning points.
在這裏表示「完全不知道」 這裏的 little 並不是指「細小」或「少量」。 Little did he know... 相等於： He had no idea... He did not know at all...
Here, little means “had no idea” or “did not know at all”; it does not mean small or a small quantity.
放在句首後，要使用倒裝 正常語序： He did not know that the door was open. 倒裝語序： Little did he know that the door was open. 正確順序是： Little + did + subject + know 不能寫成： Little he did know... ✗ Little he knew... ✗
When Little begins the sentence, use inversion in the order Little + did + subject + know.
後面必須使用原形 know 正確： Little did she know... 錯誤： Little did she knew... ✗ did 已經表示過去時間，所以 know 不可以再變成 knew。
Use the base form know after did, not the past form knew.
後面必須接完整子句 正確： Little did Tom know that the shop had closed. that 後面的子句包括： ● the shop：主語 ● had closed：動詞 錯誤： Little did Tom know that the closed shop. ✗
Follow that with a complete clause containing its own subject and verb.
這個句型主要用於過去的故事 它通常表示： ● 某人在當時不知道一件事； ● 那件事後來被發現； ● 結果帶有驚訝、轉折或意外。 例如： Little did Tom know that her photo would become famous. Tom 當時不知道這件事，但說故事的人已經知道後來的結果。
The structure is mainly used in past narratives when a character did not know a later-discovered, surprising or important fact.
表示「從當時角度看將會發生」 Little did he know that his decision would change the project. 作出決定時，改變項目仍是未來的事情，因此使用： would + 動詞原形
Use would + base verb for an event that was still in the future from the character’s past point of view.
這個句型帶有較強的故事語氣 普通說法： He had no idea that the letter would change his life. 較有故事感的說法： Little did he know that the letter would change his life. 兩句的基本意思相同，但第二句更能製造懸念和意外感。
The structure has a strong narrative tone. It expresses the same core fact as “had no idea” but creates more suspense and surprise.
