「The time has come to + 動詞」
Using “The time has come to + verb”
The time has come to + base verb + other information
The time has come to reconsider the policy.
是時候重新考慮這項政策了。
這個句型可以清楚表示：等待、討論或拖延的階段已經結束，現在應該採取行動。是時候作出決定了。 讀者會立即明白，這項決定不能再無限期拖延。
It clearly announces that action is now necessary The time has come to make a decision.
普通的 should 可以提出建議：【We should update the system.】 我們應該更新系統。 目標表達【The time has come to】則能表達更強的時機感：【The time has come to update the system.】 是時候更新系統了。 第二句聽起來較堅定，適合用於演說、會議、報告、建議書及重要討論。
It gives a statement more weight We should update the system. The time has come to The time has come to update the system.
詞語【has come】是現在完成式，能把之前的等待、準備、問題或變化連接到現在。經過數月測試，是時候推出產品了。 這句讓讀者明白，現在的行動是之前一連串事情發展後的結果。
It connects the past situation with the present decision After months of testing, the time has come to launch the product.
你可以用較簡潔而有力的方式，表達「已經到了應該做某事的階段」。
It can replace a longer explanation Instead of writing: We have reached a point at which we should reconsider the policy. You can write: The time has come to reconsider the policy.
是時候修改規則了。 現在是否應該修改規則？ 因此，這個句型既可以用來表達立場，也可以用來開展討論。
It works well in both statements and questions You can make a strong statement: The time has come to change the rules. You can also invite discussion: Has the time come to change the rules?

你不需要每次都把句子寫成：【The time has come to...】 你也可以寫：【I believe the time has come to...；After several delays, the time has come to...；Perhaps the time has come to...；Do you think the time has come to...?；The question is whether the time has come to...】 這些變化能避免所有句子使用相同開頭，令說話及寫作更自然。

It gives learners several useful sentence openings The time has come to... I believe the time has come to... After several delays, the time has come to... Perhaps the time has come to... Do you think the time has come to...? The question is whether the time has come to...
核心句型是：【The time has come to + base verb.】 是時候採取行動了。 是時候作出決定了。 是時候檢討規則了。 句中的 to + 動詞說明現在應該採取甚麼行動。
The core expression is fixed The time has come to + base verb. The time has come to act. The time has come to make a decision. The time has come to review the rules.
在 The time has come to 後面，to 是不定詞標記，因此必須接動詞原形，例如 change；不可接 changed 或 changing。
Use the base form after “to” The time has come to change the plan. The time has come to changed the plan. The time has come to changing the plan.
從文法上看，句子的主詞是 the time，但時間本身不會採取行動。這句並不是說 the time 會修橋，而是表示相關人士、政府部門、工程團隊或社區現在應該修橋。真正採取行動的人通常由上下文決定。
The action is performed by an understood person or group The time has come to repair the bridge.

以下內容可以加入句子，但並不是固定句型的一部分：【after years of discussion；following the successful trial；in my view；perhaps；at last；finally；before the problem becomes worse；After years of discussion, the time has come to make a decision.】 經過多年討論，是時候作出決定了。 核心句型仍然是：【the time has come to make a decision】 只是提供背景。

Introductory information is optional after years of discussion following the successful trial in my view perhaps at last finally before the problem becomes worse After years of discussion, the time has come to make a decision. the time has come to make a decision After years of discussion
我認為是時候改變計劃了。 委員會同意是時候採取行動了。 報告總結認為，是時候更新系統了。 前面的字詞是外層句法，不屬於核心固定句型。

The expression can appear inside a larger sentence After a thinking or reporting verb Subject + think / believe / agree / say + (that) + the time has come to + verb. I think the time has come to change the plan. The committee agrees that the time has come to act. The report concludes that the time has come to update the system. The words before the time has come are optional outer structures. They are not part of the fixed expression. the time has come
是否已經到了更換舊設備的時候？ 我們是否應該改變一貫的做法了？ 問句形式比直接陳述較為開放，表示說話者希望先聽取意見。
It can be used as a direct question Has the time come to + base verb? Has the time come to replace the old equipment? Has the time come to change our approach?
你認為我們是否應該搬遷了？ 本區居民是否認為應該限制交通了？ 這種結構常用於會議、討論、訪問及意見調查。
It can appear inside another question Do you think the time has come to + base verb? Do you think the time has come to move? Do local residents feel the time has come to limit traffic?
小組必須考慮是否已經到了修改規則的時候。 問題是現在是否應該擴展服務。 詞語【whether】表示這件事仍有待考慮，尚未完全確定。

It can follow “whether” Subject + consider / decide / ask + whether the time has come to + verb. The panel must consider whether the time has come to change the rules. The question is whether the time has come to expand the service.
現在尚未到公布結果的時候。 現在尚未到重開道路的時候。 這個否定形式表示現在仍然太早，適當時機尚未來到。不要混淆：【The time has not yet come to announce the result.】 現在仍未到公布結果的時候。 是時候不要公布結果了。 第二句的 not 是否定 announce，意思完全不同，而且通常不是最自然的表達方法。

A limited negative form is possible The time has not yet come to + base verb. The time has not yet come to announce the result. The time has not yet come to reopen the road. The time has come not to announce the result.
終於是時候開始這個項目了。 現在是時候作出選擇了。 或許是時候嘗試另一種方法了。 這些副詞只用來增加態度、時間感或強調效果，並非固定句型的必要部分。

Adverbs may be inserted, but they are optional Common optional adverbs include: finally now at last perhaps The time has finally come to begin the project. Now, the time has come to make a choice. Perhaps the time has come to try a different approach. The adverbs add attitude or emphasis. They are not compulsory parts of the expression.
在本練習中，其他表示「是時候」的近義句式雖然意思相關，但文法不同，因此不作目標答案。本課使用 The time has come to + 動詞原形。它可獨立成句，也可接在 think、believe 或 agree 後，或放在時間和背景短語之後；無論外層句框如何改變，核心結構都保持不變。

Related expressions are not the target structure The following expressions have related meanings, but they are grammatically different: It is time to change the plan. It is high time we changed the plan. Now is the time to change the plan. The time has come for us to change the plan. The present exercise uses: The time has come to + base verb. A strong learner should recognise and produce the following patterns. Independent statement The time has come to + verb. The time has come to act. After a thinking or reporting verb Subject + think / believe / agree + the time has come to + verb. We believe the time has come to change the system. After an introductory phrase Introductory phrase + the time has come to + verb. After months of preparation, the time has come to begin.

With an attitude word Perhaps / At last / Finally, + the time has come to + verb. Perhaps the time has come to ask for help. Direct question Has the time come to + verb? Has the time come to reconsider the decision? Question with “Do you think” Do you think the time has come to + verb? Do you think the time has come to replace the machine? Embedded question with “whether” Subject + consider / ask + whether the time has come to + verb. We must consider whether the time has come to expand. Negative form The time has not yet come to + verb. The time has not yet come to make an announcement.

With information after the action The time has come to + verb + object / place / time / reason. The time has come to explain the decision to the public. The time has come to repair the bridge before winter. The additional information is optional. It does not form part of the fixed expression.

「Gone are the days when + clause」表達「昔日已成過去」
Using “Gone are the days when + clause”
Gone are the days when + clause
Gone are the days when people waited weeks for an overseas letter.
人們要等候數星期才收到海外信件的年代已經過去了。
讀者可以立即明白，某種舊有習慣或情況現在已經不再普遍。
It makes a change between the past and present immediately clear The reader can immediately understand that an old habit or situation is no longer normal today.
你不需要分開兩句描述昔日情況和今天的改變，也可以把兩者合併成一句。第二句直接把「昔日的做法已經結束」放在同一句中，關係更清楚。

It combines the old situation and the present change Instead of explaining the past and present in two separate sentences, you can present the whole change in one sentence. Compare: People once had to visit a bank counter to pay every bill. They no longer need to do this. Gone are the days when people had to visit a bank counter to pay every bill.
以 Gone 開始句子，可以突出某個舊時代或舊做法已經結束。這特別適合用來討論：科技（technology）；教育（education）；工作模式交通（transport）；社會觀念公共服務
It gives strong emphasis to social or technological change Beginning with Gone draws attention to the fact that an old period has ended. working life social attitudes public services
你可以加入 thankfully、fortunately 或 sadly，表達你認為這項改變值得高興還是令人惋惜。值得慶幸的是，職場欺凌被置之不理的日子已經過去了。 令人惋惜的是，全家人每晚一起吃晚飯的日子已經過去了。

It allows you to show your attitude towards the change You can add thankfully, fortunately or sadly to show whether you see the change as positive or negative. Thankfully, gone are the days when workplace bullying was simply ignored. Sadly, gone are the days when the whole family ate dinner together every evening.
很多學習者經常以 People、Workers 或 Students 等主語開始句子。這個倒裝句能提供另一種句首寫法，使文章不會過於重複。

It gives you more varied sentence openings Many learners begin most sentences with the subject: People no longer... Workers no longer... Students no longer... Gone are the days when... gives you another way to organise and begin the sentence.
這個句型可以先提出一項重要轉變，然後再解釋轉變的原因、影響或重要性，因此適合用於作文、報告、演說和討論。
It is useful in essays, reports, speeches and discussions The structure helps you introduce a major change before explaining its causes, effects or importance.
倒裝句 Gone are the days when... 要把 Gone 放在 be 動詞之前，再接主語 the days；不可把主語移到 are 前面。
“Gone” is placed before the verb Gone are the days when people wrote every message by hand. Gone the days are when people wrote every message by hand. Gone + are + the days
真正的主語是複數名詞 the days，因此要使用 are。
The verb must be “are” The true subject is the plural noun the days, so the verb is are. Gone are the days when... Gone is the days when...
在這個句型中，gone 表示「已成過去」或「已經消失」。它並不是一個被動語態，也不是表示某些日子「去了某個地方」。
在【when】後面的子句說明我們所指的是哪一段日子或哪一個年代。這裏的 when employees wrote every report by hand 修飾 the days。詞語【when】並不是用來提出問題，因此句末不使用問號。
“When” describes which days Gone are the days when employees wrote every report by hand.
在 Gone are the days when... 中，when 子句通常描述過去情況。可用一般過去式說明昔日習慣，用 used to 表示過往常態，用 had to 表示當時的必要，用 could／could not 表示能力或限制，也可用 was／were expected to 說明過去的社會期望。

The “when” clause normally describes a past situation past simple when people paid every bill in cash used to + base verb when people used to store every photograph in an album had to + base verb when passengers had to wait without any travel information could / could not + base verb when students could pass by memorising facts alone was / were expected to + base verb when junior employees were expected to remain silent
以【when】為例：子句直接修飾 the days，因此兩者之間不加逗號。
Do not place a comma before “when” Gone are the days when every document was sent by fax. Gone are the days, when every document was sent by fax.
前置範圍語或語氣副詞後面通常使用逗號。
Use a comma after an introductory phrase In many workplaces, gone are the days when staff wore formal clothes every day. Thankfully, gone are the days when pupils were punished for asking questions.
目標表達【Gone are the days when...】表示某種情況已經結束，或已不再是正常做法。如果某種情況只是略為減少，卻仍然十分普遍，便不應隨意使用這個句型。這句可能過於絕對，因為很多人仍然使用現金。對很多購物者而言，每次購物都攜帶現金的日子已成過去。 加入 For many shoppers 可以更準確地限制適用範圍。

The expression makes a strong claim Gone are the days when... Too broad: Gone are the days when people use cash. 「It was not until X that Y」強調「直到……才……」
Using “It was not until X that Y”
It was not until + X + that + Y
It was not until the final meeting that we understood the seriousness of the problem.
直到最後一次會議，我們才明白問題的嚴重性。
突出重要的轉捩點直到醫生解釋檢查結果，伊森才明白病情的嚴重性。

It emphasises an important turning point This structure tells the reader that X was the moment when the situation finally changed. It was not until the doctor explained the results that Ethan understood the seriousness of the condition. The reader’s attention is drawn to the doctor’s explanation as the key turning point.
這個句式把「較早仍未發生的事情」和「事情終於發生的時間點」放在同一句中，令先後次序一目了然。例如直到雨停孩子才外出，讀者可立即知道雨停前他們一直留在室內，不會誤解兩件事的時間關係。

It makes a timeline easier to understand The structure clearly separates: what had not happened earlier the point when it finally happened. It was not until the rain stopped that the children went outside. The reader can immediately understand that the children remained indoors before the rain stopped.
這個強調句能把普通的 did not...until... 改寫得更有力度，把讀者注意力集中在延誤終結或事情終於發生的時間點。

It adds emphasis to an ordinary “did not... until...” sentence Compare: The team did not score until the second half. It was not until the second half that the team scored. Both versions are correct. The second version gives greater attention to the second half and makes the delay sound more important.
這個句式能把背景事件與其後的發現、領悟、回應或結果連成一個有條理的句子，清楚交代兩者的時間關係。

It helps combine background and discovery This structure is useful when describing: a realisation a discovery a delayed response a problem that became clear a result that appeared later. The director did not discover the design error before production began. The director admitted that it was not until production had begun that the team discovered the design error. The second version presents the delayed discovery as one organised idea.
這個句式可增加句式變化，避免反覆使用 did not...until...、only after、only when、then 或 finally，同時保留相同的時間關係。

It gives you more sentence variety Instead of repeatedly using: did not... until... only after... only when... then finally you can use it was not until... that... to express the same time relationship in a different way.
這個句式適合用於故事、報告、簡報和正式解釋，尤其可交代某人終於明白事情、問題被發現、決定作出或證據出現的時間。

It is useful in stories, reports and formal explanations The structure is particularly useful when explaining when: someone finally understood something a problem was discovered a decision was made evidence became available a system began to work the effects of a change became clear. It can therefore be used naturally in narratives, essays, reports, presentations and workplace communication.
在 It was not until X that Y 結構中，that 後面使用正常陳述句語序，即主語在前、動詞在後，不可加入 did 倒裝。Not until X + 助動詞 + 主語 + 主要動詞是另一個結構；兩者都能強調延誤的時間點，但語序不可混合。

Use normal word order after “that” It was not until the final meeting that we understood the problem. It was not until the final meeting that did we understand the problem. The inversion belongs to a different structure: Not until the final meeting did we understand the problem. Compare: Not until X + auxiliary verb + subject + main verb Not until Friday did she reply. It was not until X that + subject + normal verb It was not until Friday that she replied.
由「not...until」改寫成這個強調句時，that 子句通常改為肯定形式。原句的否定意思已由 not until 承擔，不可在 that 子句內再次加入否定。

The that-clause usually becomes affirmative Source: She did not notice the mistake until Friday. Target answer: It was not until Friday that she noticed the mistake. It was not until Friday that she did not notice the mistake. The incorrect version means that she still failed to notice it on Friday.
在 It was not until X that Y 結構中，X 與 that 子句之間不可加逗號；但整句前面的引導短語仍可按一般規則使用逗號。

Do not place a comma before “that” It was not until midnight that they arrived. It was not until midnight, that they arrived. An introductory phrase may have a comma: In the end, it was not until midnight that they arrived.
改寫時必須保留原句準確的時間關係。若原句表示晚飯後才致電，X 部分便要保留 after dinner；省去 after 會誤變成直到晚飯時間才致電。

Preserve the exact time relationship. Source: He called me only after dinner. Answer: It was not until after dinner that he called me. Do not remove after, because that would change the meaning to ‘not until dinner’.
在這個句式中，X 部分標示事情延遲至哪一刻才發生，並不表示因果或目的。例如 alarm sounded 只指出家人發現火警的時間，不代表警報造成火警。

X marks the delayed point, not the cause or purpose It was not until the alarm sounded that the family noticed the fire. This sentence identifies the moment when they first noticed the fire. It does not necessarily say that the alarm caused the fire or that anyone sounded it for that purpose.
在 Y 部分可按意思使用不同動詞形式，包括一般過去式、被動語態及情態動詞；X 部分也可使用過去完成式。X 或 Y 內部的時態和語態改變時，It was not until X that Y 的核心結構保持不變。

Different verb forms may appear in Y Simple past It was not until Friday that she replied. Passive voice It was not until the next morning that the bicycle was found. Modal verb It was not until the clouds cleared that the rescuers could see the village. Past perfect inside X It was not until every parent had been contacted that the trip was cancelled. The target structure remains the same even when the grammar inside X or Y changes.
本練習集中操練過去式 It was not until X that Y。現在式 It is not until X that Y 雖然合乎文法，但不是本組題目的目標形式。
